{

    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/google_drive",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Draft Spec: Policy Engine Extensions for Regional Failover Automation\",\n  \"owner\": \"Jordan Lee\",\n  \"drive_area\": \"shared_drives\",\n  \"path\": \"shared_drives/engineering/platform-engineering/policy-engine-failover-extensions-draft.json\",\n  \"doc_type\": \"doc\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-01-07\",\n  \"last_modified\": \"2026-01-12\",\n  \"collaborators\": [\n    \"Ravi Menon\",\n    \"Miles Thornton\",\n    \"Benji Okafor\",\n    \"Mina Haddad\",\n    \"Ethan Park\",\n    \"Allison Grant\"\n  ],\n  \"team\": \"eng-platform\",\n  \"status\": \"draft\",\n  \"tags\": [\n    \"failover\",\n    \"policy-engine\",\n    \"determinism\",\n    \"routing\",\n    \"guardrails\",\n    \"sre\",\n    \"reliability-program\"\n  ],\n  \"linked_artifacts\": [\n    \"Linear: ENG-2411\",\n    \"Linear: ENG-2412\",\n    \"Linear: ENG-2415\",\n    \"Linear: ENG-2416\",\n    \"Confluence: adr-042-failover-trigger-signal-hierarchy\",\n    \"Confluence: adr-043-automated-routing-policy-rollback\",\n    \"GitHub: redwood/pr-19812-policy-engine-signal-priority (planned)\",\n    \"GitHub: redwood/pr-19815-routing-policy-rollback-safety (planned)\"\n  ],\n  \"content\": \"Context / why this exists\\n- We\\u2019re upgrading regional failover automation as part of Reliability Program (Q1\\u2013Q2 2026). Today, routing policy evaluation has a few gaps:\\n  - Non-deterministic behavior in edge cases (e.g., multiple signals firing, partial signal availability, time-window ambiguity).\\n  - Hard to reason about priority across trigger signals (reachability, 5xx burn, tail latency burn, capacity exhaustion).\\n  - No first-class \\u201chold-down\\u201d / dampening in evaluation; logic is split between policy rules and external controller.\\n  - No consistent mechanism to enforce safety constraints per tenant/tier (max flips, blast radius caps, required approval).\\n\\nGoals\\n- Add policy engine primitives so failover decisioning is:\\n  - Deterministic and auditable (same inputs => same decision; explainability built-in).\\n  - Compatible with ADR-042 (signal priority + corroboration) and ADR-043 (rollback + anti-flap).\\n  - Safe by default (rate limits, required corroboration, blast radius constraints).\\n- Support both:\\n  - \\u201cRecommend\\u201d (dry-run) mode: compute candidate flips + evidence.\\n  - \\u201cEnforce\\u201d mode: same evaluation but returns executable actions.\\n\\nNon-goals\\n- Replace the automation controller. The controller still orchestrates execution, approvals, and cross-system workflow.\\n- Re-architect signal ingestion. We consume normalized, time-bucketed signals from Region Health + SLO toolkit.\\n- Build customer-facing UI here.\\n\\nTerminology\\n- Policy: configuration describing routing behavior for a route/service/model/tier.\\n- Region set: primary and fallback regions eligible for this route.\\n- Trigger signal: normalized boolean or scalar indicating regional impairment or risk.\\n- Decision: computed outcome (no-op, failover, partial shift, rollback, hold).\\n- Action: executable change (policy flip, weight adjustment, circuit breaker mode) emitted by controller.\\n\\nInputs / data model assumptions\\n- Policy engine receives inputs as a single evaluation payload, including:\\n  - route_id (e.g., hosted.chat.completions, dedicated.pool.<pool_id>)\\n  - tenant_id (optional for shared Hosted; required for Dedicated)\\n  - tenant_tier (free/pro/enterprise/dedicated)\\n  - current_routing_state (primary region, weights, last_flip_at)\\n  - signals (per region, per signal type):\\n    - reachability: ok|degraded|down + confidence + last_updated\\n    - errors_5xx_burn: burn_rate + window + confidence\\n    - tail_latency_burn: burn_rate + p95/p99 deltas + confidence\\n    - capacity_headroom: percent + \\u201chard gate\\u201d boolean\\n    - control_plane_health (optional): ok|degraded|down\\n  - evaluation_time (UTC epoch + monotonic sequence)\\n  - constraints (policy-level + tenant-level): max_flips_per_hour, min_hold_down_seconds, require_approval, blast_radius_limit\\n\\nDeterminism requirements (core)\\n1) Stable ordering\\n- Evaluation must not depend on map iteration order.\\n- Rule matching must define explicit ordering: by priority, then by tie-breakers.\\n\\n2) Stable time semantics\\n- All windowed signals must be anchored to evaluation_time and include:\\n  - effective_start, effective_end, and a \\u201cfreshness\\u201d timestamp.\\n- Engine must treat stale signals consistently:\\n  - If authoritative signals are stale beyond threshold, decision = HOLD (do not fail over) unless reachability is explicitly DOWN with high confidence.\\n\\n3) Single decision per evaluation\\n- For a given (route_id, tenant_id, evaluation_time), engine emits exactly one decision object, even if multiple actions are possible.\\n- Multi-step actions (e.g., drain -> shift weights -> finalize) must be represented as a sequence recommendation but still within a single decision record.\\n\\n4) Explainability\\n- Decision must include:\\n  - decision_type (NO_OP | FAILOVER | PARTIAL_SHIFT | ROLLBACK | HOLD)\\n  - chosen_reason (canonical enum)\\n  - evidence: ordered list of signals used, with values, freshness, and thresholds.\\n  - rejected_candidates: (optional) top 1\\u20133 alternatives and why they were not selected.\\n\\nProposed changes to policy engine\\nA) New predicates / functions\\n1) region_health(region, signal_type) -> {status, value, confidence, freshness_seconds}\\n- Wrapper that pulls normalized data from payload and enforces freshness calculations.\\n\\n2) is_authoritative_reachability_down(region) -> bool\\n- True only if:\\n  - reachability.status == down\\n  - confidence >= configured_min_confidence (default 0.9)\\n  - freshness_seconds <= reachability_max_staleness (default 30s)\\n\\n3) burn_rate_exceeded(region, metric, window, threshold) -> bool\\n- Works for errors_5xx_burn and tail_latency_burn.\\n- Window must be one of approved windows (e.g., 1m/5m/30m) to avoid configuration drift.\\n\\n4) capacity_hard_gate(region) -> bool\\n- True if headroom below threshold AND capacity signal confidence is high.\\n- Intended to prevent shifting into an already overloaded region.\\n\\n5) corroborated(primary_signal, secondary_signal) -> bool\\n- Enforces ADR-042 \\u201crequired corroboration signals\\u201d when configured.\\n- Example: if tail latency burn triggers, require either 5xx burn OR reachability degraded/down OR control plane degraded.\\n\\n6) hold_down_active(last_flip_at, min_hold_down_seconds) -> bool\\n- If true, policy engine returns HOLD unless reachability down is authoritative.\\n\\n7) flip_budget_ok(tenant_id, route_id, max_flips_per_hour) -> bool\\n- Input includes a precomputed counter from controller/state store (policy engine does not store state).\\n\\n8) blast_radius_ok(tenant_tier, requested_action) -> bool\\n- Enforces \\u201ccan\\u2019t shift more than X% traffic for tier Y without approval\\u201d.\\n- For Hosted, blast radius is route-scoped; for Dedicated, pool-scoped.\\n\\nB) Deterministic evaluation mode (required)\\n- Add an \\u201cevaluation_mode\\u201d field:\\n  - recommend: compute decision + evidence; do not mark as executable\\n  - enforce: compute decision; include explicit requested_action(s)\\n- Engine must produce identical decision_type and evidence in both modes (action packaging differs).\\n\\nC) Signal hierarchy evaluation (ADR-042)\\nPriority order (proposed canonical order for v1):\\n1) Reachability DOWN (authoritative) => FAILOVER (unless no healthy fallback)\\n2) Errors (5xx) fast burn (high severity) => FAILOVER or PARTIAL_SHIFT depending on blast radius and capacity\\n3) Tail latency burn (p99/p95) => PARTIAL_SHIFT first; escalate to FAILOVER if corroborated and sustained\\n4) Capacity exhaustion / hard gate => HOLD + load shed (controller action), avoid shifting into constrained region\\n5) Control plane degradation => HOLD (do not flip rapidly; prevent oscillation)\\n\\nNotes:\\n- \\u201cNo healthy fallback\\u201d means every eligible fallback region fails capacity_hard_gate OR reachability is down OR stale beyond threshold.\\n- If no healthy fallback, decision should be HOLD and include \\u201cdegrade_allowed=true\\u201d hint (controller can activate load shedding / retry-after).\\n\\nD) Policy language / config schema additions\\nAdd new fields (names tentative):\\n- failover:\\n  - enabled: boolean\\n  - eligible_regions: [us-east, eu-west, ...]\\n  - signal_requirements:\\n    - primary_trigger: enum\\n    - corroboration: [enum]\\n    - min_confidence: float\\n    - max_staleness_seconds: int\\n  - dampening:\\n    - min_hold_down_seconds: int\\n    - require_sustain_seconds: int (for non-reachability triggers)\\n  - safety:\\n    - require_approval: boolean (default true for prod initially)\\n    - max_flips_per_hour: int\\n    - max_traffic_shift_percent: int\\n    - rollback:\\n      - auto_rollback_enabled: boolean\\n      - rollback_after_seconds: int\\n      - rollback_require_healthy_primary_seconds: int\\n\\nE) Output schema\\nDecision output (single object, JSON):\\n- decision_id (stable hash of route_id + tenant_id + evaluation_time + policy_version)\\n- policy_version\\n- evaluation_time\\n- decision_type\\n- chosen_reason\\n- target_state (string encoding; owned by controller)\\n- requested_actions (string encoding; empty in recommend mode)\\n- evidence (string encoding; ordered)\\n- annotations (string encoding; includes thresholds, staleness, hold-down state)\\n\\nNote: In our implementation we\\u2019ll likely use structured objects, but for logging/audit we must generate a stable, versioned string representation.\\n\\nSafety constraints (ADR-043 alignment)\\n- Anti-flap:\\n  - Enforce hold-down between flips for non-reachability triggers.\\n  - Any rollback decision must respect a separate rollback hold-down (avoid ping-pong between primary and fallback).\\n- Rate limiting:\\n  - flip_budget_ok must be true, else HOLD.\\n- Approval hooks:\\n  - If require_approval is true, decision_type can still be FAILOVER but requested_actions must be empty and \\u201capproval_required=true\\u201d annotation set.\\n- Tenant/tier gates:\\n  - Enterprise/Dedicated can be configured with stricter \\u201cdo not cross data residency boundary\\u201d constraint (policy engine should surface \\u201cconstraint_violation:data_residency\\u201d rather than attempt partial shifts).\\n\\nEdge cases and expected behavior\\n1) Partial outage in primary region\\n- Reachability degraded (not down), 5xx burn elevated, capacity OK in fallback.\\n- Expected: PARTIAL_SHIFT (e.g., shift 25\\u201350% depending on max_traffic_shift_percent) if corroborated. If sustained and escalates to reachability down or error burn becomes severe => FAILOVER.\\n\\n2) Signal missing / ingestion delayed\\n- Any authoritative signal is stale beyond max_staleness_seconds.\\n- Expected: HOLD. Evidence must explicitly call out staleness and which signal blocked action.\\n\\n3) Fallback region constrained\\n- Primary is failing (5xx burn), fallback capacity_hard_gate true.\\n- Expected: HOLD + annotate \\u201cfallback_unhealthy_due_to_capacity\\u201d. Controller should invoke load shedding and retry-after rather than shifting load.\\n\\n4) Control plane degraded\\n- Control plane health degraded; data plane signals ambiguous.\\n- Expected: HOLD unless reachability down is authoritative. (Avoid flipping policies when control plane is suspect.)\\n\\n5) Multi-fallback selection\\n- If multiple eligible fallback regions are healthy, selection tie-breakers:\\n  1) policy-specified order\\n  2) lowest latency probe (if available in inputs)\\n  3) highest capacity headroom\\n  4) stable sort by region name\\n\\nTesting plan (draft)\\nUnit tests\\n- Determinism:\\n  - Same payload with randomized key order => same decision_id, decision_type, evidence ordering.\\n- Staleness gating:\\n  - Stale error burn + fresh reachability OK => HOLD.\\n- Priority:\\n  - Reachability DOWN overrides hold-down.\\n  - 5xx burn overrides latency burn when both exceed thresholds.\\n\\nIntegration tests\\n- Replay recorded signal snapshots from staging incidents + controlled game day traces.\\n- Validate output is compatible with controller dry-run UX (must contain reasons + evidence).\\n\\nPerformance considerations\\n- Evaluation must be cheap; do not add per-eval remote calls.\\n- Evidence strings must be bounded in size. Cap rejected_candidates and evidence list.\\n\\nOperational / observability hooks\\n- Emit a single log line per decision with:\\n  - decision_id, route_id, tenant_id (hashed in shared Hosted contexts), decision_type, chosen_reason\\n  - key thresholds and freshness\\n- Export metrics:\\n  - policy_engine_decisions_total{decision_type, chosen_reason, tier}\\n  - policy_engine_hold_reasons_total{reason}\\n  - policy_engine_eval_latency_ms\\n\\nOpen questions\\n- Exact shape of \\u201ctarget_state\\u201d string: should it be a controller-owned serialization of desired weights, or should the policy engine output high-level intent only?\\n- Do we want PARTIAL_SHIFT as a first-class decision type (recommended), or represent it as FAILOVER with weight < 100%?\\n- How strict should corroboration be for tail latency burn? (ADR-042 indicates corroboration required; we need the exact default set.)\\n- Where should data residency constraints live?\\n  - Option A: policy engine validates \\u201cregion set allowed\\u201d and blocks action.\\n  - Option B: upstream policy compilation prevents invalid eligible_regions.\\n\\nNear-term next steps\\n- Align with Miles/Ravi on canonical signal enum + reason enum.\\n- Draft schema PR for policy config additions (behind feature flag).\\n- Implement deterministic ordering + evidence output in policy engine.\\n- Wire to dry-run mode (ENG-2415) so the controller can display \\u201crecommended action + confidence + evidence\\u201d on game day.\\n\\nAppendix: candidate enums (WIP)\\nchosen_reason\\n- REACHABILITY_DOWN\\n- ERROR_BURN_FAST\\n- LATENCY_BURN_SUSTAINED\\n- CAPACITY_HARD_GATE\\n- SIGNALS_STALE\\n- HOLD_DOWN_ACTIVE\\n- FLIP_BUDGET_EXCEEDED\\n- CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION_DATA_RESIDENCY\\n- NO_HEALTHY_FALLBACK\\n\\nsignal_type\\n- REACHABILITY\\n- ERRORS_5XX_BURN\\n- TAIL_LATENCY_BURN\\n- CAPACITY_HEADROOM\\n- CONTROL_PLANE_HEALTH\\n\",\n  \"original_location\": \"google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/platform-engineering/policy-engine-failover-extensions-draft.json\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"content\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_184be937d34a412ab5e61366d54d8ed6\"\n}",

document.title: Draft Spec: Policy Engine Extensions for Regional Failover Automation
document.content:
{
  "title": "Draft Spec: Policy Engine Extensions for Regional Failover Automation",
  "owner": "Jordan Lee",
  "drive_area": "shared_drives",
  "path": "shared_drives/engineering/platform-engineering/policy-engine-failover-extensions-draft.json",
  "doc_type": "doc",
  "created_at": "2026-01-07",
  "last_modified": "2026-01-12",
  "collaborators": [
    "Ravi Menon",
    "Miles Thornton",
    "Benji Okafor",
    "Mina Haddad",
    "Ethan Park",
    "Allison Grant"
  ],
  "team": "eng-platform",
  "status": "draft",
  "tags": [
    "failover",
    "policy-engine",
    "determinism",
    "routing",
    "guardrails",
    "sre",
    "reliability-program"
  ],
  "linked_artifacts": [
    "Linear: ENG-2411",
    "Linear: ENG-2412",
    "Linear: ENG-2415",
    "Linear: ENG-2416",
    "Confluence: adr-042-failover-trigger-signal-hierarchy",
    "Confluence: adr-043-automated-routing-policy-rollback",
    "GitHub: redwood/pr-19812-policy-engine-signal-priority (planned)",
    "GitHub: redwood/pr-19815-routing-policy-rollback-safety (planned)"
  ],
  "content": "Context / why this exists
- We’re upgrading regional failover automation as part of Reliability Program (Q1–Q2 2026). Today, routing policy evaluation has a few gaps:
  - Non-deterministic behavior in edge cases (e.g., multiple signals firing, partial signal availability, time-window ambiguity).
  - Hard to reason about priority across trigger signals (reachability, 5xx burn, tail latency burn, capacity exhaustion).
  - No first-class “hold-down” / dampening in evaluation; logic is split between policy rules and external controller.
  - No consistent mechanism to enforce safety constraints per tenant/tier (max flips, blast radius caps, required approval).

Goals
- Add policy engine primitives so failover decisioning is:
  - Deterministic and auditable (same inputs => same decision; explainability built-in).
  - Compatible with ADR-042 (signal priority + corroboration) and ADR-043 (rollback + anti-flap).
  - Safe by default (rate limits, required corroboration, blast radius constraints).
- Support both:
  - “Recommend” (dry-run) mode: compute candidate flips + evidence.
  - “Enforce” mode: same evaluation but returns executable actions.

Non-goals
- Replace the automation controller. The controller still orchestrates execution, approvals, and cross-system workflow.
- Re-architect signal ingestion. We consume normalized, time-bucketed signals from Region Health + SLO toolkit.
- Build customer-facing UI here.

Terminology
- Policy: configuration describing routing behavior for a route/service/model/tier.
- Region set: primary and fallback regions eligible for this route.
- Trigger signal: normalized boolean or scalar indicating regional impairment or risk.
- Decision: computed outcome (no-op, failover, partial shift, rollback, hold).
- Action: executable change (policy flip, weight adjustment, circuit breaker mode) emitted by controller.

Inputs / data model assumptions
- Policy engine receives inputs as a single evaluation payload, including:
  - route_id (e.g., hosted.chat.completions, dedicated.pool.<pool_id>)
  - tenant_id (optional for shared Hosted; required for Dedicated)
  - tenant_tier (free/pro/enterprise/dedicated)
  - current_routing_state (primary region, weights, last_flip_at)
  - signals (per region, per signal type):
    - reachability: ok|degraded|down + confidence + last_updated
    - errors_5xx_burn: burn_rate + window + confidence
    - tail_latency_burn: burn_rate + p95/p99 deltas + confidence
    - capacity_headroom: percent + “hard gate” boolean
    - control_plane_health (optional): ok|degraded|down
  - evaluation_time (UTC epoch + monotonic sequence)
  - constraints (policy-level + tenant-level): max_flips_per_hour, min_hold_down_seconds, require_approval, blast_radius_limit

Determinism requirements (core)
1) Stable ordering
- Evaluation must not depend on map iteration order.
- Rule matching must define explicit ordering: by priority, then by tie-breakers.

2) Stable time semantics
- All windowed signals must be anchored to evaluation_time and include:
  - effective_start, effective_end, and a “freshness” timestamp.
- Engine must treat stale signals consistently:
  - If authoritative signals are stale beyond threshold, decision = HOLD (do not fail over) unless reachability is explicitly DOWN with high confidence.

3) Single decision per evaluation
- For a given (route_id, tenant_id, evaluation_time), engine emits exactly one decision object, even if multiple actions are possible.
- Multi-step actions (e.g., drain -> shift weights -> finalize) must be represented as a sequence recommendation but still within a single decision record.

4) Explainability
- Decision must include:
  - decision_type (NO_OP | FAILOVER | PARTIAL_SHIFT | ROLLBACK | HOLD)
  - chosen_reason (canonical enum)
  - evidence: ordered list of signals used, with values, freshness, and thresholds.
  - rejected_candidates: (optional) top 1–3 alternatives and why they were not selected.

Proposed changes to policy engine
A) New predicates / functions
1) region_health(region, signal_type) -> {status, value, confidence, freshness_seconds}
- Wrapper that pulls normalized data from payload and enforces freshness calculations.

2) is_authoritative_reachability_down(region) -> bool
- True only if:
  - reachability.status == down
  - confidence >= configured_min_confidence (default 0.9)
  - freshness_seconds <= reachability_max_staleness (default 30s)

3) burn_rate_exceeded(region, metric, window, threshold) -> bool
- Works for errors_5xx_burn and tail_latency_burn.
- Window must be one of approved windows (e.g., 1m/5m/30m) to avoid configuration drift.

4) capacity_hard_gate(region) -> bool
- True if headroom below threshold AND capacity signal confidence is high.
- Intended to prevent shifting into an already overloaded region.

5) corroborated(primary_signal, secondary_signal) -> bool
- Enforces ADR-042 “required corroboration signals” when configured.
- Example: if tail latency burn triggers, require either 5xx burn OR reachability degraded/down OR control plane degraded.

6) hold_down_active(last_flip_at, min_hold_down_seconds) -> bool
- If true, policy engine returns HOLD unless reachability down is authoritative.

7) flip_budget_ok(tenant_id, route_id, max_flips_per_hour) -> bool
- Input includes a precomputed counter from controller/state store (policy engine does not store state).

8) blast_radius_ok(tenant_tier, requested_action) -> bool
- Enforces “can’t shift more than X% traffic for tier Y without approval”.
- For Hosted, blast radius is route-scoped; for Dedicated, pool-scoped.

B) Deterministic evaluation mode (required)
- Add an “evaluation_mode” field:
  - recommend: compute decision + evidence; do not mark as executable
  - enforce: compute decision; include explicit requested_action(s)
- Engine must produce identical decision_type and evidence in both modes (action packaging differs).

C) Signal hierarchy evaluation (ADR-042)
Priority order (proposed canonical order for v1):
1) Reachability DOWN (authoritative) => FAILOVER (unless no healthy fallback)
2) Errors (5xx) fast burn (high severity) => FAILOVER or PARTIAL_SHIFT depending on blast radius and capacity
3) Tail latency burn (p99/p95) => PARTIAL_SHIFT first; escalate to FAILOVER if corroborated and sustained
4) Capacity exhaustion / hard gate => HOLD + load shed (controller action), avoid shifting into constrained region
5) Control plane degradation => HOLD (do not flip rapidly; prevent oscillation)

Notes:
- “No healthy fallback” means every eligible fallback region fails capacity_hard_gate OR reachability is down OR stale beyond threshold.
- If no healthy fallback, decision should be HOLD and include “degrade_allowed=true” hint (controller can activate load shedding / retry-after).

D) Policy language / config schema additions
Add new fields (names tentative):
- failover:
  - enabled: boolean
  - eligible_regions: [us-east, eu-west, ...]
  - signal_requirements:
    - primary_trigger: enum
    - corroboration: [enum]
    - min_confidence: float
    - max_staleness_seconds: int
  - dampening:
    - min_hold_down_seconds: int
    - require_sustain_seconds: int (for non-reachability triggers)
  - safety:
    - require_approval: boolean (default true for prod initially)
    - max_flips_per_hour: int
    - max_traffic_shift_percent: int
    - rollback:
      - auto_rollback_enabled: boolean
      - rollback_after_seconds: int
      - rollback_require_healthy_primary_seconds: int

E) Output schema
Decision output (single object, JSON):
- decision_id (stable hash of route_id + tenant_id + evaluation_time + policy_version)
- policy_version
- evaluation_time
- decision_type
- chosen_reason
- target_state (string encoding; owned by controller)
- requested_actions (string encoding; empty in recommend mode)
- evidence (string encoding; ordered)
- annotations (string encoding; includes thresholds, staleness, hold-down state)

Note: In our implementation we’ll likely use structured objects, but for logging/audit we must generate a stable, versioned string representation.

Safety constraints (ADR-043 alignment)
- Anti-flap:
  - Enforce hold-down between flips for non-reachability triggers.
  - Any rollback decision must respect a separate rollback hold-down (avoid ping-pong between primary and fallback).
- Rate limiting:
  - flip_budget_ok must be true, else HOLD.
- Approval hooks:
  - If require_approval is true, decision_type can still be FAILOVER but requested_actions must be empty and “approval_required=true” annotation set.
- Tenant/tier gates:
  - Enterprise/Dedicated can be configured with stricter “do not cross data residency boundary” constraint (policy engine should surface “constraint_violation:data_residency” rather than attempt partial shifts).

Edge cases and expected behavior
1) Partial outage in primary region
- Reachability degraded (not down), 5xx burn elevated, capacity OK in fallback.
- Expected: PARTIAL_SHIFT (e.g., shift 25–50% depending on max_traffic_shift_percent) if corroborated. If sustained and escalates to reachability down or error burn becomes severe => FAILOVER.

2) Signal missing / ingestion delayed
- Any authoritative signal is stale beyond max_staleness_seconds.
- Expected: HOLD. Evidence must explicitly call out staleness and which signal blocked action.

3) Fallback region constrained
- Primary is failing (5xx burn), fallback capacity_hard_gate true.
- Expected: HOLD + annotate “fallback_unhealthy_due_to_capacity”. Controller should invoke load shedding and retry-after rather than shifting load.

4) Control plane degraded
- Control plane health degraded; data plane signals ambiguous.
- Expected: HOLD unless reachability down is authoritative. (Avoid flipping policies when control plane is suspect.)

5) Multi-fallback selection
- If multiple eligible fallback regions are healthy, selection tie-breakers:
  1) policy-specified order
  2) lowest latency probe (if available in inputs)
  3) highest capacity headroom
  4) stable sort by region name

Testing plan (draft)
Unit tests
- Determinism:
  - Same payload with randomized key order => same decision_id, decision_type, evidence ordering.
- Staleness gating:
  - Stale error burn + fresh reachability OK => HOLD.
- Priority:
  - Reachability DOWN overrides hold-down.
  - 5xx burn overrides latency burn when both exceed thresholds.

Integration tests
- Replay recorded signal snapshots from staging incidents + controlled game day traces.
- Validate output is compatible with controller dry-run UX (must contain reasons + evidence).

Performance considerations
- Evaluation must be cheap; do not add per-eval remote calls.
- Evidence strings must be bounded in size. Cap rejected_candidates and evidence list.

Operational / observability hooks
- Emit a single log line per decision with:
  - decision_id, route_id, tenant_id (hashed in shared Hosted contexts), decision_type, chosen_reason
  - key thresholds and freshness
- Export metrics:
  - policy_engine_decisions_total{decision_type, chosen_reason, tier}
  - policy_engine_hold_reasons_total{reason}
  - policy_engine_eval_latency_ms

Open questions
- Exact shape of “target_state” string: should it be a controller-owned serialization of desired weights, or should the policy engine output high-level intent only?
- Do we want PARTIAL_SHIFT as a first-class decision type (recommended), or represent it as FAILOVER with weight < 100%?
- How strict should corroboration be for tail latency burn? (ADR-042 indicates corroboration required; we need the exact default set.)
- Where should data residency constraints live?
  - Option A: policy engine validates “region set allowed” and blocks action.
  - Option B: upstream policy compilation prevents invalid eligible_regions.

Near-term next steps
- Align with Miles/Ravi on canonical signal enum + reason enum.
- Draft schema PR for policy config additions (behind feature flag).
- Implement deterministic ordering + evidence output in policy engine.
- Wire to dry-run mode (ENG-2415) so the controller can display “recommended action + confidence + evidence” on game day.

Appendix: candidate enums (WIP)
chosen_reason
- REACHABILITY_DOWN
- ERROR_BURN_FAST
- LATENCY_BURN_SUSTAINED
- CAPACITY_HARD_GATE
- SIGNALS_STALE
- HOLD_DOWN_ACTIVE
- FLIP_BUDGET_EXCEEDED
- CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION_DATA_RESIDENCY
- NO_HEALTHY_FALLBACK

signal_type
- REACHABILITY
- ERRORS_5XX_BURN
- TAIL_LATENCY_BURN
- CAPACITY_HEADROOM
- CONTROL_PLANE_HEALTH

    "title": "Edge switch ARP proxying leads to VPN client IP duplication and intermittent routing to wrong host",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/jira",
    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"INT-460811\",\n  \"project\": \"internal-support\",\n  \"issue_type\": \"Incident\",\n  \"summary\": \"Edge switch ARP proxying leads to VPN client IP duplication and intermittent routing to wrong host\",\n  \"status\": \"In Progress\",\n  \"priority\": \"P2\",\n  \"severity\": \"Sev2\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-03-10\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-03-14\",\n  \"reporter\": \"Aisha Malik\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Jonah Reed\",\n  \"components\": [\n    \"edge-network\",\n    \"vpn\",\n    \"dhcp\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"networking\",\n    \"arp-proxy\",\n    \"investigation\",\n    \"high-impact\"\n  ],\n  \"environment\": \"prod-us-west\",\n  \"linked_issues\": [\n    \"INT-424246\",\n    \"INT-542019\"\n  ],\n  \"description\": \"Issue summary: Several users reporting intermittent loss of access to internal services while connected to corporate VPN. Symptoms include duplicate IP conflict alerts on endpoints, frequent VPN re-auth events, and traffic appearing to be routed to a different on-prem host (service 10.23.5.12). Impact: ~8% of VPN sessions in us-west over the last 48h experienced short blackholes (30-90s) impacting git pushes, internal CI jobs, and ssh sessions. Scope: affects users on Wi-Fi SSID 'Redwood-Corp' behind specific edge switches in building SF2 rack 7.\",\n  \"steps_to_reproduce\": [\n    \"1) Connect laptop to 'Redwood-Corp' Wi-Fi in SF2 building (tested on macOS 13 and Ubuntu 22.04)\",\n    \"2) Establish VPN session to redwood-vpn-usw.redwood.net (WireGuard-based corporate VPN)\",\n    \"3) Trigger continuous ping to an internal host (ping -i 0.2 10.23.5.12)\",\n    \"4) Observe intermittent duplicate IP warnings on client and packets forwarded to an unexpected MAC on the L2 domain\",\n    \"5) Reproduce frequency increases when there is a short burst of multicast/mDNS traffic on the same AP's radio\"\n  ],\n  \"observed_logs_and_artifacts\": [\n    \"Client syslog excerpt: 'kernel: arp: IP address 10.23.8.45 claimed by 00:11:22:33:44:55 (conflict)'\",\n    \"Switch (edge-sw-7) log: 'proxy-arp conflict detected for 10.23.8.45, source 00:66:77:88:99:AA bridging-port 5'\",\n    \"Packet capture (pcap) snippet: ARP reply for 10.23.8.45 with two different source MACs within 120ms\",\n    \"VPN server metrics: client rekey count spike (client 10.23.8.45) correlated to timestamp 2026-03-12T14:12Z\",\n    \"Internal service (10.23.5.12) reported TCP reset spikes aligning with client blackholes\"\n  ],\n  \"investigation_notes\": [\n    \"Hypothesis 1: Edge switch proxy-arp configured for legacy NAT path is responding to ARP for VPN-assigned addresses from an overlapping DHCP pool, causing two active ARP entries on the LAN.\",\n    \"Hypothesis 2: A misconfigured VXLAN/bridge on edge-sw-7 is advertising ARP for the VPN subnet into the campus L2 segment when multicast bursts occur.\",\n    \"What we tried: - Disabled proxy-arp on edge-sw-7 port-channel to AP group temporarily (no immediate reduction). - Isolated a suspect AP by moving a test client to a different AP (blackhole persisted only when client served by AP-7A). - Captured pcap on AP, switch uplink, and VPN server concurrently for correlated timestamps (pcaps saved to /mnt/logs/INT-460811/pcaps/).\",\n    \"Preliminary find: ARP 'gratuitous' replies with VPN client IP are being injected by the switch's 'proxy-arp' feature only when the AP's multicast queue exceeds threshold. The switch returns ARP for the same IP with a different MAC that matches a spare management interface in rack 7 (00:66:77:88:99:AA).\"\n  ],\n  \"impact_summary\": \"Intermittent connectivity loss for internal developer workflows (git/ssh/CI). Approximately 8% of VPN sessions in the SF2 us-west site affected in the window; potential for data-transfer retries and CI flakiness. No customer-facing outage but notable developer productivity hit.\",\n  \"initial_triage_actions\": [\n    \"1) Placed affected edge switch (edge-sw-7) in monitoring schedule and enabled debug logging for proxy-arp events.\",\n    \"2) Temporarily increased DHCP lease affinity for VPN pool for clients in SF2 to reduce the window for IP reuse.\",\n    \"3) Asked campus networking team to disable 'proxy-arp' global feature on a staging switch and observe (ongoing).\",\n    \"4) Notified platform reliability and CI owners of potential re-run needs for impacted jobs (Slack #incidents and #platform-alerts).\"\n  ],\n  \"comments\": [\n    \"2026-03-11 09:18 - Jonah Reed: Assigned to network; will coordinate switch config changes and gather pcaps. Next action: schedule maintenance window if we need to push config rollback.\",\n    \"2026-03-12 15:25 - Priya Shah (campus-net): Reproduced proxy-arp responses on edge-sw-7 when AP multicast queue > 70%. Suspect firmware 1.2.3 on these switches has a known misc bridging bug. Opened ticket with vendor (TAC-889233).\",\n    \"2026-03-13 08:52 - Jonah Reed: Vendor TAC confirmed the switch may respond to ARP for non-local subnets under multicast overload in 1.2.3. Recommended immediate mitigation: set 'proxy-arp disable' on VRF for AP VLANs and upgrade firmware to 1.2.6.\",\n    \"2026-03-14 07:30 - Aisha Malik: Applied 'proxy-arp disable' to edge-sw-7 in staged maintenance window (07:00-07:15). Monitoring: VPN rekey spikes reduced from 47/hr to 2/hr for affected clients in the first 24h.\",\n    \"2026-03-14 10:02 - Jonah Reed: Confirming RFC and rollout plan for global fix. Proposed follow-up: firmware upgrade across SF2 rack 4-9, audit for proxy-arp enabled on other edge switches, and update config baseline to explicitly disable proxy-arp for VPN/DHCP subnets.\"\n  ],\n  \"root_cause\": \"Switch firmware (1.2.3) bug caused proxy-arp behavior under high multicast load leading to ARP advertisements for VPN-assigned addresses. This created ephemeral duplicate IP assignments on the L2 domain and caused VPN clients to experience routing blackholes and rekeys.\",\n  \"resolution_notes\": [\n    \"Mitigation applied: 'proxy-arp disable' set on edge-sw-7 AP VLANs during maintenance window 2026-03-14 07:00-07:15.\",\n    \"Temporary workaround: increased DHCP lease affinity and moved high-multicast APs to separate RF profile to reduce multicast bursts.\",\n    \"Permanent fix: planned firmware upgrade to 1.2.6 across SF2 edge switches (racks 4-9) and config baseline change to disable proxy-arp for VPN/DHCP subnets. Vendor TAC provided patch notes and recommended upgrade path.\",\n    \"Follow-ups: - Create change request CR-2026-0415 for firmware rollout. - Run campus-wide audit script to detect 'proxy-arp' enabled instances and remediate. - Add regression test to onboarding checklist for AP multicast stress.\",\n    \"Status: Partial fix applied and validated; full remediation scheduled (see CR-2026-0415).\"\n  ],\n  \"related_github_prs\": [\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-config/pull/411\"\n  ],\n  \"related_confluence_pages\": [\n    \"https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/NET/pages/Edge+Switch+Proxy-ARP+Runbook\"\n  ],\n  \"original_location\": \"jira/internal-support/INT-460811-edge-switch-arp-proxy-ip-duplication.json\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"summary\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"steps_to_reproduce\",\n    \"observed_logs_and_artifacts\",\n    \"investigation_notes\",\n    \"impact_summary\",\n    \"initial_triage_actions\",\n    \"comments\",\n    \"root_cause\",\n    \"resolution_notes\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_59cb294da8964683bb165a3bb615df71\"\n}",

document.title: Edge switch ARP proxying leads to VPN client IP duplication and intermittent routing to wrong host
document.content:
{
  "key": "INT-460811",
  "project": "internal-support",
  "issue_type": "Incident",
  "summary": "Edge switch ARP proxying leads to VPN client IP duplication and intermittent routing to wrong host",
  "status": "In Progress",
  "priority": "P2",
  "severity": "Sev2",
  "created_at": "2026-03-10",
  "updated_at": "2026-03-14",
  "reporter": "Aisha Malik",
  "assignee": "Jonah Reed",
  "components": [
    "edge-network",
    "vpn",
    "dhcp"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "networking",
    "arp-proxy",
    "investigation",
    "high-impact"
  ],
  "environment": "prod-us-west",
  "linked_issues": [
    "INT-424246",
    "INT-542019"
  ],
  "description": "Issue summary: Several users reporting intermittent loss of access to internal services while connected to corporate VPN. Symptoms include duplicate IP conflict alerts on endpoints, frequent VPN re-auth events, and traffic appearing to be routed to a different on-prem host (service 10.23.5.12). Impact: ~8% of VPN sessions in us-west over the last 48h experienced short blackholes (30-90s) impacting git pushes, internal CI jobs, and ssh sessions. Scope: affects users on Wi-Fi SSID 'Redwood-Corp' behind specific edge switches in building SF2 rack 7.",
  "steps_to_reproduce": [
    "1) Connect laptop to 'Redwood-Corp' Wi-Fi in SF2 building (tested on macOS 13 and Ubuntu 22.04)",
    "2) Establish VPN session to redwood-vpn-usw.redwood.net (WireGuard-based corporate VPN)",
    "3) Trigger continuous ping to an internal host (ping -i 0.2 10.23.5.12)",
    "4) Observe intermittent duplicate IP warnings on client and packets forwarded to an unexpected MAC on the L2 domain",
    "5) Reproduce frequency increases when there is a short burst of multicast/mDNS traffic on the same AP's radio"
  ],
  "observed_logs_and_artifacts": [
    "Client syslog excerpt: 'kernel: arp: IP address 10.23.8.45 claimed by 00:11:22:33:44:55 (conflict)'",
    "Switch (edge-sw-7) log: 'proxy-arp conflict detected for 10.23.8.45, source 00:66:77:88:99:AA bridging-port 5'",
    "Packet capture (pcap) snippet: ARP reply for 10.23.8.45 with two different source MACs within 120ms",
    "VPN server metrics: client rekey count spike (client 10.23.8.45) correlated to timestamp 2026-03-12T14:12Z",
    "Internal service (10.23.5.12) reported TCP reset spikes aligning with client blackholes"
  ],
  "investigation_notes": [
    "Hypothesis 1: Edge switch proxy-arp configured for legacy NAT path is responding to ARP for VPN-assigned addresses from an overlapping DHCP pool, causing two active ARP entries on the LAN.",
    "Hypothesis 2: A misconfigured VXLAN/bridge on edge-sw-7 is advertising ARP for the VPN subnet into the campus L2 segment when multicast bursts occur.",
    "What we tried: - Disabled proxy-arp on edge-sw-7 port-channel to AP group temporarily (no immediate reduction). - Isolated a suspect AP by moving a test client to a different AP (blackhole persisted only when client served by AP-7A). - Captured pcap on AP, switch uplink, and VPN server concurrently for correlated timestamps (pcaps saved to /mnt/logs/INT-460811/pcaps/).",
    "Preliminary find: ARP 'gratuitous' replies with VPN client IP are being injected by the switch's 'proxy-arp' feature only when the AP's multicast queue exceeds threshold. The switch returns ARP for the same IP with a different MAC that matches a spare management interface in rack 7 (00:66:77:88:99:AA)."
  ],
  "impact_summary": "Intermittent connectivity loss for internal developer workflows (git/ssh/CI). Approximately 8% of VPN sessions in the SF2 us-west site affected in the window; potential for data-transfer retries and CI flakiness. No customer-facing outage but notable developer productivity hit.",
  "initial_triage_actions": [
    "1) Placed affected edge switch (edge-sw-7) in monitoring schedule and enabled debug logging for proxy-arp events.",
    "2) Temporarily increased DHCP lease affinity for VPN pool for clients in SF2 to reduce the window for IP reuse.",
    "3) Asked campus networking team to disable 'proxy-arp' global feature on a staging switch and observe (ongoing).",
    "4) Notified platform reliability and CI owners of potential re-run needs for impacted jobs (Slack #incidents and #platform-alerts)."
  ],
  "comments": [
    "2026-03-11 09:18 - Jonah Reed: Assigned to network; will coordinate switch config changes and gather pcaps. Next action: schedule maintenance window if we need to push config rollback.",
    "2026-03-12 15:25 - Priya Shah (campus-net): Reproduced proxy-arp responses on edge-sw-7 when AP multicast queue > 70%. Suspect firmware 1.2.3 on these switches has a known misc bridging bug. Opened ticket with vendor (TAC-889233).",
    "2026-03-13 08:52 - Jonah Reed: Vendor TAC confirmed the switch may respond to ARP for non-local subnets under multicast overload in 1.2.3. Recommended immediate mitigation: set 'proxy-arp disable' on VRF for AP VLANs and upgrade firmware to 1.2.6.",
    "2026-03-14 07:30 - Aisha Malik: Applied 'proxy-arp disable' to edge-sw-7 in staged maintenance window (07:00-07:15). Monitoring: VPN rekey spikes reduced from 47/hr to 2/hr for affected clients in the first 24h.",
    "2026-03-14 10:02 - Jonah Reed: Confirming RFC and rollout plan for global fix. Proposed follow-up: firmware upgrade across SF2 rack 4-9, audit for proxy-arp enabled on other edge switches, and update config baseline to explicitly disable proxy-arp for VPN/DHCP subnets."
  ],
  "root_cause": "Switch firmware (1.2.3) bug caused proxy-arp behavior under high multicast load leading to ARP advertisements for VPN-assigned addresses. This created ephemeral duplicate IP assignments on the L2 domain and caused VPN clients to experience routing blackholes and rekeys.",
  "resolution_notes": [
    "Mitigation applied: 'proxy-arp disable' set on edge-sw-7 AP VLANs during maintenance window 2026-03-14 07:00-07:15.",
    "Temporary workaround: increased DHCP lease affinity and moved high-multicast APs to separate RF profile to reduce multicast bursts.",

{
  "channel": "eng-releases",
  "thread_ts": "1729999999",
  "first_message_ts": "1729999999",
  "last_message_ts": "1730000450",
  "participants": [
    "jake",
    "mina",
    "praveen",
    "ops-qa",
    "release-bot"
  ],
  "messages": "jake: Quick pre-release check — planning to publish v1.14.0 tomorrow morning (UTC). Need someone to push an annotated+signed tag, create a GitHub draft release, and confirm artifacts + checksums are uploaded. Leaving a short checklist below.

mina: I can take the tag + create the draft. What should the exact tag message and procedures be?

jake: Tag message: "Release v1.14.0 — runtime + CLI: perf improvements, bugfixes, changelog entries". Steps I recommend:

```
# ensure branch is up to date
git checkout release/v1.14
git pull --ff-only origin release/v1.14

# create an annotated tag
git tag -a v1.14.0 -m "Release v1.14.0 — runtime + CLI: perf improvements, bugfixes"

# (optional) GPG-sign the tag locally
git tag -s v1.14.0 -m "Release v1.14.0"

# push the tag to origin
git push origin v1.14.0
```

Then create a GitHub draft release (gh CLI):
```
# create draft with changelog as notes
gh release create v1.14.0 dist/* --notes-file CHANGELOG.md --draft
```

Artifact steps (build pipeline has produced dist/*):
```
# checksums
shasum -a 256 dist/* > checksums.txt
# upload artifacts to S3
aws s3 cp dist/ s3://redwood-release-bucket/v1.14.0/ --recursive
aws s3 cp checksums.txt s3://redwood-release-bucket/v1.14.0/
```

praveen: Quick security notes: confirm the GPG key you use is the same key uploaded in your GitHub account (Settings -> SSH and GPG keys). We require a signed annotated tag for this release. Also add a manifest.json alongside checksums.txt with SHA256 hashes so downstream teams can verify.

jake: Example minimal manifest schema (we'll add full file in the release assets):
```
{
  "version": "v1.14.0",
  "files": [
    {"name": "redwood-runtime-linux.tar.gz", "sha256": "<hex>"},
    {"name": "redwood-cli-mac.tar.gz", "sha256": "<hex>"}
  ]
}
```

ops-qa: Can we do a quick smoke run after the draft exists but before publishing? I'll run a basic generate+embed test against staging and report back. :eyes:

mina: Plan: I'll push the signed tag and create the draft at 09:00 UTC, then ping here with links. Who will upload the artifacts?

jake: I'll handle artifact upload and checksum generation once the tag is present.

release-bot: Automated reminder: please ensure checksums.txt and manifest.json are included in the draft assets.

mina: Tag pushed and draft created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/releases/tag/v1.14.0 :rocket: (draft link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/releases/edit/??)

jake: Uploading artifacts to S3 now and attaching checksums+manifest to the draft.

jake: Done — artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-release-bucket/v1.14.0/ and checksums.txt + manifest.json attached to draft. Verified local checksums match S3.

ops-qa: Smoke run results: basic generation, embeddings, and regression tests passed on staging (no obvious regressions).

praveen: Verified GPG signature on tag and validated manifest/checksums. Security LGTM.

mina: If no objections, I'll publish the release at 09:20 UTC. Any last-minute blockers?

jake: No blockers from infra side — approving publish. :tada:

release-bot: Publishing scheduled by mina at 09:20 UTC.

mina: Published. Release URL: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/releases/tag/v1.14.0 — changelog and assets are attached. Congrats team! :confetti_ball:",

}

The feature surfaces per-route metric diffs between cohorts, links anomalous metric deltas to sampled request traces, and exposes suggested rollback signals (automated and manual) backed by thresholded telemetry. This is intended to reduce MTTI for rollout regressions and make auto-rollback decisions transparent to product and platform teams.\",\n  \"acceptance_criteria\": [\n    \"Comparator UI shows side-by-side cohort-level charts for latency (p50/p95), error rate, token cost, and request throughput for a selected time window\",\n    \"Diff view highlights statistically significant deltas and annotates percentage change with confidence intervals\",\n    \"User can click a diff to see sampled traces from both cohorts with request-level metadata (route, model version, routing policy, input hash)\",\n    \"Trace Linker pins causal spans and shows top 3 signal contributors (e.g., model variant, batch size, region) derived from instrumentation\",\n    \"Auto-rollback triggers are visible per-rollout and can be toggled; Console records the reason and suggested fallback model\",\n    \"All telemetry queries are reproducible (copyable query) and dashboards exportable as PNG/CSV\",\n    \"Feature is behind a Console feature flag and gated to Dedicated/Hosted customers in beta\"\n  ],\n  \"tasks\": [\n    \"Product: finalize comparator UX flows and error states (mockups)\",\n    \"Design: high-fidelity mockups for comparator panel, trace overlay, and diff heatmap\",\n    \"Engineering: instrument cohort labels in request pipeline and add trace sampling hook for cohort comparison\",\n    \"Engineering: build backend telemetry aggregator service to compute per-route deltas and significance tests\",\n    \"Engineering: expose API endpoints for cohort queries and trace joins\",\n    \"SRE: validate query performance and set retention defaults for cohort metrics\",\n    \"QA: e2e tests for trace linking across canary/A-B/shadow traffic scenarios\",\n    \"Docs: write Console help guide and rollout observability playbook\"\n  ],\n  \"design_assets\": [\n    \"https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/Cohort-Comparator-Prototype\",\n    \"https://drive.redwood/internal/Console/Mockups/cohort-comparator-v2.pdf\"\n  ],\n  \"telemetry_queries\": [\n    \"PromQL: rate(http_server_requests_total{route=~\\\"/v1/generate.*\\\"}[5m]) by (cohort)\",\n    \"PromQL: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, cohort))\",\n    \"SQL (clickhouse): select cohort, quantileExact(0.95, duration_ms) from document.title: Cohort Comparator & Trace Linker for Deployment Health
document.content:
{
  "key": "PM-24680",
  "team": "product-management",
  "title": "Cohort Comparator & Trace Linker for Deployment Health",
  "status": "In Progress",
  "priority": "P1",
  "created_at": "2026-03-10",
  "updated_at": "2026-03-14",
  "creator": "Aisha Kapoor",
  "assignee": "Marco Lin",
  "project": "Console Rollouts",
  "cycle": "2026-W10",
  "estimate": "8",
  "due_date": "2026-04-01",
  "labels": [
    "rollouts",
    "observability",
    "console",
    "canary",
    "a/b",
    "auto-rollback",
    "tracing"
  ],
  "parent_issue": [
    "PM-14091"
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    "ENG-20345",
    "ENG-20412",
    "DES-317"
  ],
  "customer_impact": "high",
  "release": "console-2026.03",
  "security_review_required": "false",
  "description": "Build a combined Cohort Comparator and Request Trace Linker inside the Console to make canary/A-B/shadow rollouts diagnosable end-to-end. The feature surfaces per-route metric diffs between cohorts, links anomalous metric deltas to sampled request traces, and exposes suggested rollback signals (automated and manual) backed by thresholded telemetry. This is intended to reduce MTTI for rollout regressions and make auto-rollback decisions transparent to product and platform teams.",
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    "Comparator UI shows side-by-side cohort-level charts for latency (p50/p95), error rate, token cost, and request throughput for a selected time window",
    "Diff view highlights statistically significant deltas and annotates percentage change with confidence intervals",
    "User can click a diff to see sampled traces from both cohorts with request-level metadata (route, model version, routing policy, input hash)",
    "Trace Linker pins causal spans and shows top 3 signal contributors (e.g., model variant, batch size, region) derived from instrumentation",
    "Auto-rollback triggers are visible per-rollout and can be toggled; Console records the reason and suggested fallback model",
    "All telemetry queries are reproducible (copyable query) and dashboards exportable as PNG/CSV",
    "Feature is behind a Console feature flag and gated to Dedicated/Hosted customers in beta"
  ],
  "tasks": [
    "Product: finalize comparator UX flows and error states (mockups)",
    "Design: high-fidelity mockups for comparator panel, trace overlay, and diff heatmap",
    "Engineering: instrument cohort labels in request pipeline and add trace sampling hook for cohort comparison",
    "Engineering: build backend telemetry aggregator service to compute per-route deltas and significance tests",
    "Engineering: expose API endpoints for cohort queries and trace joins",
    "SRE: validate query performance and set retention defaults for cohort metrics",
    "QA: e2e tests for trace linking across canary/A-B/shadow traffic scenarios",
    "Docs: write Console help guide and rollout observability playbook"
  ],
  "design_assets": [
    "https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/Cohort-Comparator-Prototype",
    "https://drive.redwood/internal/Console/Mockups/cohort-comparator-v2.pdf"
  ],
  "telemetry_queries": [
    "PromQL: rate(http_server_requests_total{route=~\"/v1/generate.*\"}[5m]) by (cohort)",
    "PromQL: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, cohort))",
    "SQL (clickhouse): select cohort, quantileExact(0.95, duration_ms) from requests where route='/v1/chat' and ts >= now()-interval 1 hour group by cohort"
  ],
  "rollout_plan": [
    "Alpha: enable feature flag for internal Redwood tenants only (1 week)",
    "Beta: open to selected customers on Dedicated and Hosted with opt-in (4 weeks)",
    "GA: enabled by default for all Console users with feature rollout controls (post-beta)"
  ],
  "risks": [
    "High cardinality of route/model/version labels could make diff computations slow",
    "Trace sampling bias between cohorts may create false-positive causes",
    "Auto-rollback without clear human-readable rationale could erode trust",
    "Data retention costs if coarse-grained sampling is insufficient for forensic analysis"
  ],
  "tradeoffs": [
    "Aggressive trace sampling increases root-cause fidelity but raises cost \u2014 start with adaptive sampling tied to metric deltas",
    "Pre-computing cohort diffs reduces UI latency but increases storage/compute; prefer on-demand with short cache window initially",
    "Expose simple auto-rollback toggles first; defer fully automated ML-driven rollback recommendations to later cycle"
  ],
  "reviewers": [
    "Nina Rodriguez (Security)",
    "Omar Patel (SRE)",
    "Leah Chen (Design)",
    "Devon Morris (Engineering lead)"
  ],
  "notes": [
    "PM/Design sync 2026-03-11: prioritize clear reasoning cards next to each suggested rollback action",
    "Prototype session 2026-03-12: product asked for side-by-side trace waterfall comparison; design to iterate",
    "Engineering spike 2026-03-13 showed ClickHouse aggregation of cohort diffs at 5m windows is 3x cheaper than per-request joins"
  ],
  "comments": [
    "2026-03-10 Aisha Kapoor: Created ticket \u2014 goal is to reduce MTTI for rollout regressions by surface-level correlation -> request-level evidence.",
    "2026-03-11 Marco Lin: Spun up spike; backend will reuse existing metrics pipeline but needs a lightweight join index for cohort -> trace linking (ENG-20345)",
    "2026-03-12 Leah Chen: Uploaded first mockups; recommended adding a confidence ribbon to diff charts to indicate statistical significance",
    "2026-03-13 Omar Patel: SRE flagged potential retention cost issue; recommending adaptive sampling and a 14-day lookback default",
    "2026-03-14 Marco Lin: Marked 'in progress' \u2014 backend API contract drafted and PR linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4128"
  ],
  "attachments": [
    "https://confluence.redwood/internal/Console-Rollouts/Cohort-Comparator-PRD",
    "https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/commit/ab12cd34",
    "https://internal.redwood/incidents/2025-11-canary-regression-postmortem.pdf"
  ],

    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/linear",
    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"ENG-77120\",\n  \"team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"title\": \"Fn schema mapper and streaming handshake for cross-SDK invocation\",\n  \"status\": \"In Progress\",\n  \"priority\": \"P1\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-02-18\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2025-03-05\",\n  \"creator\": \"Marcus Li\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Elena Rodriguez\",\n  \"project\": \"sdk-function-calls\",\n  \"cycle\": \"2025-W09\",\n  \"estimate\": \"5\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2025-03-14\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"sdk\",\n    \"function-calling\",\n    \"cross-language\",\n    \"streaming\",\n    \"retry\",\n    \"telemetry\"\n  ],\n  \"dependencies\": [\n    \"ENG-61452\",\n    \"ENG-74290\"\n  ],\n  \"customer_impact\": \"medium\",\n  \"release\": \"sdk-2025.03\",\n  \"security_review_required\": \"false\",\n  \"description\": \"Implement a lightweight, portable function-schema mapper and streaming handshake layer used by Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. The mapper will normalize model-declared function schemas into SDK-native typed descriptors, provide coercion and graceful-degradation rules, and expose invocation helpers that handle idempotency tokens, adaptive retry/backoff for non-streamed and streamed calls, and a streaming handshake that enables resume/fallthrough semantics when partial responses arrive or a connection drops.\",\n  \"acceptance_criteria\": [\n    \"SDKs (py/ts/go) include a shared schema mapper that converts model function definitions into native call signatures and JSON validators\",\n    \"Invocation helpers expose a consistent call surface across languages, including: call(), stream_call(), call_with_idempotency(), and fallback_to_text()\",\n    \"Retry/backoff policy supports at-least-once vs exactly-once semantics toggles, with telemetry events emitted for retry attempts and fallback triggers\",\n    \"Streaming handshake protocol enables resume from KV-prefix if server supports resume tokens; otherwise client falls back to graceful abort and server-side best-effort completion\",\n    \"Comprehensive unit and integration tests cover schema coercion, optional argument handling, enum coercion, nested objects, and streaming resume scenarios\",\n    \"Documentation pages and three example apps (py/ts/go) demonstrating function call patterns and recommended safety knobs\"\n  ],\n  \"design_notes\": [\n    \"Keep mapper small: generate validator code at package build-time where feasible, fall back to runtime checks for dynamic models\",\n    \"Prefer permissive coercion by default (string->enum, numeric strings->numbers) but surface a strict mode for enterprise users needing deterministic validation\",\n    \"Streaming handshake: introduce a small four-step exchange (CLIENT_HELLO -> SERVER_ACK(with resume_token?) -> CLIENT_STREAM_START -> KEEPALIVE frames). If SERVER_ACK includes no resume token, client must checkpoint locally and allow idempotent retry only for non-side-effecting tools\",\n    \"Idempotency token strategy: allow user-provided token or generate RFC4122 v4 by default; include an optional idempotency window header so routers can garbage-collect tokens early\",\n    \"Telemetry: emit events for schema_mismatch, coercion_event, retry_attempt, retry_abort_reason, stream_resume_success, stream_resume_failure\",\n    \"Trade-offs: full schema strictness reduces user errors but increases friction for rapid prototyping. Default to permissive but log and surface mismatches via console warnings and SDK diagnostics API\"\n  ],\n  \"implementation_plan\": [\n    \"Week 1: Implement core schema mapper library in a neutral TypeScript reference package with a minimal runtime validator interface\",\n    \"Week 2: Port mapper to Python and Go wrappers, add generator to produce thin language bindings (type stubs for py, d.ts for ts, go structs)\",\n    \"Week 3: Implement streaming handshake protocol and client-side resume logic; add resume_token plumbing to server contract (spec PR)\",\n    \"Week 4: Add invocation helpers with retry policies and idempotency token handling; expose policy knobs via client config\",\n    \"Week 5: Tests, examples, docs, and API reviews. Prepare SDK release artifacts and coordinate with Console/Runtime teams for telemetry keys and server-side resume support\"\n  ],\n  \"test_plan\": [\n    \"Unit: validator coercion matrix for primitives, enums, nested objects and arrays\",\n    \"Integration: end-to-end example calling a toy function (echo, counter) in all three SDKs verifying idempotency behavior\",\n    \"Chaos: simulate dropped connections during streaming and assert resume/fallback semantics and no double-execution where exact-once is requested\",\n    \"Performance: measure additional latency/cpu of runtime validation under high QPS and validate generator reduces runtime overhead\",\n    \"Security: fuzz malformed schemas and inputs to ensure validators fail closed when strict mode is enabled\"\n  ],\n  \"rollout_plan\": [\n    \"Alpha: release TypeScript reference package and experimental Python wrapper to internal SDK alpha channel; invite 3 beta customers to opt-in\",\n    \"Beta: widen to public SDK releases behind feature flag (enable_schema_mapper=true) and collect telemetry for coercion events\",\n    \"GA: enable by default with documentation and migration guide. Coordinate with runtime team to stop accepting legacy unstructured tool formats once 90% of clients migrated or after 3 months\",\n    \"Backward compatibility: provide an adapter that maps old 'tools' flat payload to new function schema descriptors for 6 months\"\n  ],\n  \"references\": [\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/3214\",\n    \"https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Function+Call+Schema+Platform+Spec\",\n    \"https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk/function-calling#streaming-handshake\",\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/412\"\n  ],\n  \"comments\": [\n    \"2025-02-18 Marcus Li: Initial write-up and scope. Decided to standardize on permissive coercion by default and expose strict mode.\",\n    \"2025-02-22 Elena Rodriguez: Added streaming handshake design. Concern: server needs resume_token support \\u2014 opened runtime issue #412\",\n    \"2025-02-26 Backend review (Raj Patel): Suggested adding idempotency_window header and clarified router GC implications. Marked as resolved in design notes.\",\n    \"2025-03-01 PR feedback (Sara Nguyen): Requested clearer examples for exactly-once vs at-least-once and a sample using external DB side effects. Assigned follow-up test task.\",\n    \"2025-03-05 Elena Rodriguez: Merged TS reference + Python wrappers into internal alpha branch. Triggered internal validation job; performance within budget on p3-standard test harness\"\n  ],\n  \"linked_pr\": [\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/3214\",\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/89\"\n  ],\n  \"artifacts\": [\n    \"design/fn-schema-mapper-v1.md\",\n    \"examples/py/function_call_echo.py\",\n    \"examples/ts/function_call_streaming.ts\",\n    \"examples/go/function_call_idempotent.go\",\n    \"benchmarks/schema-validator-overhead.csv\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"acceptance_criteria\",\n    \"design_notes\",\n    \"implementation_plan\",\n    \"test_plan\",\n    \"rollout_plan\",\n    \"comments\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_169dca195c96410b80ff166803a50512\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Fn schema mapper and streaming handshake for cross-SDK invocation\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-77120-fn-schema-mapper-compatibility-and-streaming-handshake.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: sdk-function-calls\nTeam: engineering\n\n- eng - 74290 customer impact : medium release : sdk - 2025. 03 security review required : false description : implement a lightweight, portable function - schema mapper and streaming handshake layer used by python / typescript / go sdks. the mapper will normalize model - declared function schemas into sdk - native typed descriptors, provide coercion and graceful - degradation rules, and expose invocation helpers that handle idempotency tokens, adaptive retry / backoff for non - streamed and streamed calls, and a streaming handshake that enables resume / fallthrough semantics when partial responses arrive or a connection drops. # # acceptance criteria",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Fn schema mapper and streaming handshake for cross-SDK invocation\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-77120-fn-schema-mapper-compatibility-and-streaming-handshake.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: sdk-function-calls\nTeam: engineering\n\n- sdks ( py / ts / go ) include a shared schema mapper that converts model function definitions into native call signatures and json validators - invocation helpers expose a consistent call surface across languages, including : call ( ), stream _ call ( ), call _ with _ idempotency ( ), and fallback _ to _ text ( ) - retry / backoff policy supports at - least - once vs exactly - once semantics toggles, with telemetry events emitted for retry attempts and fallback triggers - streaming handshake protocol enables resume from kv - prefix if server supports resume tokens ; otherwise client falls back to graceful abort and server - side best - effort completion - comprehensive unit and integration",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Fn schema mapper and streaming handshake for cross-SDK invocation\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-77120-fn-schema-mapper-compatibility-and-streaming-handshake.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: sdk-function-calls\nTeam: engineering\n\n- keep mapper small : generate validator code at package build - time where feasible, fall back to runtime checks for dynamic models - prefer permissive coercion by default ( string - > enum, numeric strings - > numbers ) but surface a strict mode for enterprise users needing deterministic validation - streaming handshake : introduce a small four - step exchange ( client _ hello - > server _ ack ( with resume _ token? ) - > client _ stream _ start - > keepalive frames ). if server _ ack includes no resume token, client must checkpoint locally and allow idempotent retry only for non - side - effecting tools - idempotency token strategy : allow user - provided token",

document.title: Fn schema mapper and streaming handshake for cross-SDK invocation
document.content:
{
  "key": "ENG-77120",
  "team": "engineering",
  "title": "Fn schema mapper and streaming handshake for cross-SDK invocation",
  "status": "In Progress",
  "priority": "P1",
  "created_at": "2025-02-18",
  "updated_at": "2025-03-05",
  "creator": "Marcus Li",
  "assignee": "Elena Rodriguez",
  "project": "sdk-function-calls",
  "cycle": "2025-W09",
  "estimate": "5",
  "due_date": "2025-03-14",
  "labels": [
    "sdk",
    "function-calling",
    "cross-language",
    "streaming",
    "retry",
    "telemetry"
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    "ENG-61452",
    "ENG-74290"
  ],
  "customer_impact": "medium",
  "release": "sdk-2025.03",
  "security_review_required": "false",
  "description": "Implement a lightweight, portable function-schema mapper and streaming handshake layer used by Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. The mapper will normalize model-declared function schemas into SDK-native typed descriptors, provide coercion and graceful-degradation rules, and expose invocation helpers that handle idempotency tokens, adaptive retry/backoff for non-streamed and streamed calls, and a streaming handshake that enables resume/fallthrough semantics when partial responses arrive or a connection drops.",
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    "SDKs (py/ts/go) include a shared schema mapper that converts model function definitions into native call signatures and JSON validators",
    "Invocation helpers expose a consistent call surface across languages, including: call(), stream_call(), call_with_idempotency(), and fallback_to_text()",
    "Retry/backoff policy supports at-least-once vs exactly-once semantics toggles, with telemetry events emitted for retry attempts and fallback triggers",
    "Streaming handshake protocol enables resume from KV-prefix if server supports resume tokens; otherwise client falls back to graceful abort and server-side best-effort completion",
    "Comprehensive unit and integration tests cover schema coercion, optional argument handling, enum coercion, nested objects, and streaming resume scenarios",
    "Documentation pages and three example apps (py/ts/go) demonstrating function call patterns and recommended safety knobs"
  ],
  "design_notes": [
    "Keep mapper small: generate validator code at package build-time where feasible, fall back to runtime checks for dynamic models",
    "Prefer permissive coercion by default (string->enum, numeric strings->numbers) but surface a strict mode for enterprise users needing deterministic validation",
    "Streaming handshake: introduce a small four-step exchange (CLIENT_HELLO -> SERVER_ACK(with resume_token?) -> CLIENT_STREAM_START -> KEEPALIVE frames). If SERVER_ACK includes no resume token, client must checkpoint locally and allow idempotent retry only for non-side-effecting tools",
    "Idempotency token strategy: allow user-provided token or generate RFC4122 v4 by default; include an optional idempotency window header so routers can garbage-collect tokens early",
    "Telemetry: emit events for schema_mismatch, coercion_event, retry_attempt, retry_abort_reason, stream_resume_success, stream_resume_failure",
    "Trade-offs: full schema strictness reduces user errors but increases friction for rapid prototyping. Default to permissive but log and surface mismatches via console warnings and SDK diagnostics API"
  ],
  "implementation_plan": [
    "Week 1: Implement core schema mapper library in a neutral TypeScript reference package with a minimal runtime validator interface",
    "Week 2: Port mapper to Python and Go wrappers, add generator to produce thin language bindings (type stubs for py, d.ts for ts, go structs)",
    "Week 3: Implement streaming handshake protocol and client-side resume logic; add resume_token plumbing to server contract (spec PR)",
    "Week 4: Add invocation helpers with retry policies and idempotency token handling; expose policy knobs via client config",
    "Week 5: Tests, examples, docs, and API reviews. Prepare SDK release artifacts and coordinate with Console/Runtime teams for telemetry keys and server-side resume support"
  ],
  "test_plan": [
    "Unit: validator coercion matrix for primitives, enums, nested objects and arrays",
    "Integration: end-to-end example calling a toy function (echo, counter) in all three SDKs verifying idempotency behavior",
    "Chaos: simulate dropped connections during streaming and assert resume/fallback semantics and no double-execution where exact-once is requested",
    "Performance: measure additional latency/cpu of runtime validation under high QPS and validate generator reduces runtime overhead",
    "Security: fuzz malformed schemas and inputs to ensure validators fail closed when strict mode is enabled"
  ],
  "rollout_plan": [
    "Alpha: release TypeScript reference package and experimental Python wrapper to internal SDK alpha channel; invite 3 beta customers to opt-in",
    "Beta: widen to public SDK releases behind feature flag (enable_schema_mapper=true) and collect telemetry for coercion events",
    "GA: enable by default with documentation and migration guide. Coordinate with runtime team to stop accepting legacy unstructured tool formats once 90% of clients migrated or after 3 months",
    "Backward compatibility: provide an adapter that maps old 'tools' flat payload to new function schema descriptors for 6 months"
  ],
  "references": [
    "https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/3214",
    "https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Function+Call+Schema+Platform+Spec",
    "https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk/function-calling#streaming-handshake",
    "https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/412"
  ],
  "comments": [
    "2025-02-18 Marcus Li: Initial write-up and scope. Decided to standardize on permissive coercion by default and expose strict mode.",
    "2025-02-22 Elena Rodriguez: Added streaming handshake design. Concern: server needs resume_token support \u2014 opened runtime issue #412",
    "2025-02-26 Backend review (Raj Patel): Suggested adding idempotency_window header and clarified router GC implications. Marked as resolved in design notes.",
    "2025-03-01 PR feedback (Sara Nguyen): Requested clearer examples for exactly-once vs at-least-once and a sample using external DB side effects. Assigned follow-up test task.",
    "2025-03-05 Elena Rodriguez: Merged TS reference + Python wrappers into internal alpha branch. Triggered internal validation job; performance within budget on p3-standard test harness"
  ],
  "linked_pr": [
    "https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/3214",
    "https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/89"
  ],
  "artifacts": [
    "design/fn-schema-mapper-v1.md",
    "examples/py/function_call_echo.py",
    "examples/ts/function_call_streaming.ts",
    "examples/go/function_call_idempotent.go",
    "benchmarks/schema-validator-overhead.csv"
  ],

{
  "company_id": "LR-0472",
  "company_name": "LanternRidge SaaS Analytics",
  "company_domain": "lanternridge.ai",
  "stage": "evaluation",
  "owner": "Jordan Reyes",
  "created_at": "2024-09-18",
  "updated_at": "2024-11-06",
  "account_tier": "mid_market",
  "industry": "analytics-saas",
  "employee_count_range": "201-1000",
  "hq_region": "na",
  "interested_products": [
    "hosted_api",
    "dedicated"
  ],
  "use_cases": [
    "support-agent",
    "document-search",
    "reranking",
    "summary-generation"
  ],
  "deployment_requirements": [
    "vpc"
  ],
  "security_requirements": [
    "sso_saml",
    "soc2",
    "audit_logging",
    "kms",
    "data_residency"
  ],
  "competitors": [
    "openai",
    "anthropic"
  ],
  "forecast_close_month": "2025-01",
  "estimated_arr_range": "$120k-$250k",
  "se_assigned": "Priya Nandakumar",
  "csm_assigned": "Ethan Cole",
  "last_activity_at": "2024-11-06",
  "next_step": "internal capacity sign-off + pricing review scheduled with finance 2024-11-13",
  "blockers": [
    "cost model alignment",
    "legal review on data residency",
    "throughput SLA for business tier"
  ],
  "linked_fireflies": [
    "ff_2024-10-22_lanternridge_poc"
  ],
  "linked_gmail_threads": [
    "thread-CA12345lantern-10-22"
  ],
  "linked_drive_docs": [
    "drive:/LanternRidge/Redwood_Dedicated_POC_results_v1.xlsx",
    "drive:/LanternRidge/Redwood_pricing_deck_v3.pdf"
  ],
  "linked_support_tickets": [
    "RDW-1523"
  ],
  "activities": [
    "2024-09-20: Intro call (AE Jordan + SE Priya) - high level infra + use-case",
    "2024-10-01: Hosted API trial started (10-day credit) - three feature teams onboarded",
    "2024-10-08: Mid-trial check-in - observed latency baseline, ask for token-cost breakdown",
    "2024-10-22: Fireflies / full demo - SE reviewed batching/kv cache options (ff_2024-10-22_lanternridge_poc)",
    "2024-10-28: Trial wrap-up metrics exported; Redwood team provided dedicated sizing proposal",
    "2024-11-05: Commercial call with finance - requested committed capacity pricing options"
  ],
  "notes": [
    "POC notes: Product + Platform teams very focused on predictable unit economics",
    "Shorthand: 'hosted works well but spikes worry us' - PM (S. Alvarez)",
    "Prefers VPC for production due to PII in support transcripts; wants SOC2 + audit logs",
    "Legal: data residency check required (EU tenants) for subset of customers",
    "Cost sensitivity: target at-or-below $0.015 per 1k prompt+completion tokens across steady state",
    "AE notes: leaning toward dedicated if dedicated pricing and burst model align with finance"
  ],
  "trial_findings": [
    "Observed latency: p95 ~120-180ms for chat generation (hosted_api) at request size ~450 tokens",
    "Stability: stable under sustained QPS up to ~8, intermittent spikes to 22 QPS during batch exports",
    "Quality: model variant (open-llm-v2) met accuracy bar for reranking; no quality regressions observed",
    "Integration: embedding pipeline integrated with LangChain-style pipelines, indexing cost acceptable"
  ],
  "capacity_forecast": [
    "Hosted API POC (10 days) raw metrics: peak QPS 22, sustained QPS 6, typical concurrency observed 9",
    "Token profile (sampled POC): avg prompt tokens = 120, avg completion tokens = 320, avg tokens/request = 440",
    "Token mix: prompt:completion ~1:2.7 (support chat heavy on completions), requests/day observed ~12k => ~5.3M tokens/day",
    "Projected production (year 1): baseline QPS target = 80 sustained, peak QPS = 200 (5x current sustained), concurrency target = 120",
    "Projected token volume (year 1): 30M - 90M tokens/month depending on adoption scenarios",
    "Batching opportunity: expect 2.0-3.0x throughput uplift with Redwood batching + KV cache on common prompts"
  ],
  "dedicated_capacity_recommendation": [
    "Baseline dedicated pool recommended: 3 x 80GB-class GPUs (baseline) with autoscale to 6 during peak",
    "Estimated capacity: baseline pool approx. 120-180 QPS with aggressive batching; autoscale to 350+ QPS when burst enabled",
    "Concurrency planning: design for 150-200 concurrent inferences with soft limits and request queuing",
    "Caching: prefix/KV cache expected to reduce prompt token re-send by ~18% for conversational flows",
    "Routing: policy to route EU traffic to EU dedicated pool (data residency) + fallback to hosted in disaster recovery",
    "Cost note: dedicated reduces per-token cost but requires commit; finance asked for 12-month vs 24-month pricing scenarios"
  ],
  "business_requirements_summary": [
    "Workloads: mixed - chat-first for support agent, embeddings for search/indexing, reranking for NLU pipeline",
    "SLAs: target p95 latency <250ms for chat; throughput SLOs vary by tier (Gold = 95th percentile under peak)",
    "Resilience: automatic fallback to lower-cost model variant when primary pool saturated",
    "Observability: token-level cost breakdown and per-route dashboards required for chargeback"
