{
  "thread_id": "th_20261028_soojin_senior_infra_freeze_exception_001",
  "mailbox_owner": "soojin_lee",
  "subject": "Req acceleration request — Senior Infrastructure Engineer backfill (freeze exception)",
  "participants_internal": [
    "soojin_lee",
    "lauren_bishop",
    "hannah_schmitt",
    "jordan_blake",
    "marcus_lin"
  ],
  "participants_external": [
    "emma@talentplace.com (TalentPlace Recruiter)"
  ],
  "message_count": "5",
  "first_email_at": "2026-10-26T09:18:00-07:00",
  "last_email_at": "2026-10-28T10:05:00-07:00",
  "thread_type": "hiring",
  "region": "us",
  "has_attachments": "true",
  "attachments": [
    "Req_Form_Senior_Infra_20261026.pdf",
    "Senior_Infra_JD_v2.docx"
  ],
  "related_links": [
    "https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cHiringSprintDocs",
    "JIRA: INFRA-1287"
  ],
  "messages": [
    "From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Req acceleration request — Senior Infrastructure Engineer backfill (freeze exception)

Hi team,

Short ask: request approval for a freeze-exception and immediate sourcing for a Senior Infrastructure Engineer (backfill for A. Gomez, who is leaving end of November). This role is mission-critical for the next two quarters: we have the infra resilience sprint (Nov–Jan) and the KV cache migration that is on the critical path for Dedicated capacity cost reductions. Without a replacement we risk delaying the migration and exposing us to higher unit costs and capacity constraints.

Why now: the work is infra-facing (low ramp tax for existing systems), the candidate profile should be hireable in-market quickly, and the team can get the first deliverables within 8–10 weeks of start. Hiring a contractor is an option but we lose knowledge-transfer continuity and it will cost ~30% more for the same throughput.

Request:
- Approve a freeze exception for 1 headcount (Senior Infra Eng) and allow active sourcing immediately.
- Approve the attached req form (Req_Form_Senior_Infra_20261026.pdf).
- If budget owner needs to sign off, please confirm who (cost center) so I can route.

If you want, we can open as an SDE3 vs Staff split; my recommendation is SDE3 with a strong infra/ops background. I’ve copied Emma at TalentPlace to begin outreach if we get the green light.

Attachments: Req_Form_Senior_Infra_20261026.pdf

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Director, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
",
    "From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Req acceleration request — Senior Infrastructure Engineer backfill (freeze exception)

Soojin —

I approve in principle. This sounds like a clear risk to the migration timeline and to our cost objectives. Before formal sign-off: please confirm the cost center and the target start date. If budget sign-off will take time, approve a contingency: allow the recruiter to start active sourcing and take candidates to initial screens; final offer contingent on budget approval.

If you think contractor interim is necessary to avoid blockers, include estimated delta vs perm in the req form.

Lauren
VP, Engineering Operations

On Mon, Oct 26, 2026 at 09:18 AM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Short ask: request approval for a freeze-exception and immediate sourcing for a Senior Infrastructure Engineer (backfill for A. Gomez, who is leaving end of November).
>
> Attachments: Req_Form_Senior_Infra_20261026.pdf
",
    "From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Req acceleration request — Senior Infrastructure Engineer backfill (freeze exception)

Thanks — backing the ask but want a quick calibration against other live infra reqs. Please attach the JD and a 3-month runway estimate (salary + hiring expenses + any contractor delta). Also flag any conflicting hiring signals (e.g., other teams with higher-priority infra reqs) so we can queue appropriately.

I put a placeholder folder for docs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cHiringSprintDocs (please drop the JD there).

—Marcus
Head of Platform Delivery

On Mon, Oct 26, 2026 at 11:02 AM Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com> wrote:
> I approve in principle. This sounds like a clear risk to the migration timeline and to our cost objectives.
",
    "From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Emma (TalentPlace) <emma@talentplace.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Req acceleration request — Senior Infrastructure Engineer backfill (freeze exception)

Thanks Marcus — uploaded the JD and a short cost runway to the drive link (Senior_Infra_JD_v2.docx). Summary below:

- Cost center: ENG-PLATFORM-2 (owner: Marcus Lin)
- Target start: ideally 2026-12-01 (accepting 2027-01-03 at latest)
- Salary band: $170–200k (USD) + standard equity band for Senior level
- 3-month runway estimate: $50k (includes recruiter fees if external)
- Contractor delta: ~30% higher total cost for same period; lower long-term ROI

Emma — can you start outreach against the JD and share initial candidate slate by Nov 9? Recruiter brief is in the drive folder.

Attachments: Senior_Infra_JD_v2.docx

--
Soojin

On Mon, Oct 26, 2026 at 02:30 PM Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks — backing the ask but want a quick calibration against other live infra reqs.
",
    "From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Emma (TalentPlace) <emma@talentplace.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Req acceleration request — Senior Infrastructure Engineer backfill (freeze exception)

Approved: I authorize a freeze exception for 1 FTE (Senior Infra Eng) and authorize active sourcing and interviews to start. Conditions:

1) Final offer requires budget owner (Marcus) sign-off on total comp within the posted band.
2) Recruiter may run active search and book screens; no offers until Marcus confirms runway.
3) If we do not have viable candidates within 3 weeks of live posting, escalate to me and we will evaluate contractor interim or re-prioritization of the backlog.

Soojin — proceed to post the JD and coordinate with Emma. Keep hiring updates to the weekly QBR hiring check-in thread.

Lauren
VP, Engineering Operations

On Tue, Oct 27, 2026 at 09:15 AM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Marcus — uploaded the JD and a short cost runway to the drive link (Senior_Infra_JD_v2.docx).

    "content": "{\n  \"thread_id\": \"gmail-soojin-20260818-hc-exc-001\",\n  \"mailbox_owner\": \"soojin_lee\",\n  \"subject\": \"Request: Exception to hiring freeze for Senior Infra IC (platform-migrate)\",\n  \"participants_internal\": [\n    \"soojin_lee\",\n    \"laura_bennett\",\n    \"markus_klein\",\n    \"neha_kapoor\"\n  ],\n  \"participants_external\": [\n    \"Polaris Talent <sarah@polaris-talent.com>\",\n    \"GreenCore migrations (eng@greencore.com)\"\n  ],\n  \"message_count\": \"4\",\n  \"first_email_at\": \"2026-08-12T09:15:00-07:00\",\n  \"last_email_at\": \"2026-08-18T16:05:00-07:00\",\n  \"thread_type\": \"hiring\",\n  \"related_links\": [\n    \"JIRA: INFRA-2247\",\n    \"Drive: https://drive.redwood/workspace/platform/migration-risk-matrix\"\n  ],\n  \"has_attachments\": \"true\",\n  \"attachments\": [\n    \"hc_exception_form.pdf\",\n    \"migration_risk_matrix.xlsx\",\n    \"cost_breakdown_6mo.csv\"\n  ],\n  \"messages\": [\n    \"From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>\\nTo: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>\\nCc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, sarah@polaris-talent.com\\nDate: 2026-08-12 09:15 -0700\\nSubject: Request: Exception to hiring freeze for Senior Infra IC (platform-migrate)\\n\\nHi Laura / Markus,\\n\\nTl;dr: Requesting a one-time hiring-freeze exception to backfill a departing Senior Infrastructure Engineer (IC4) on Platform Services. This role is critical to the data-plane migration scheduled for Q4; without a replacement we expect increased SLA risk and a potential multi-week delay.\\n\\nWhy this is exceptional:\\n- Role is highly specialized: candidate has deep KV-cache & continuous-batching experience (not easily covered by generalist backend hires).\\n- Timing: two weeks notice from current engineer (last day 9/3). Migration has hard deadlines tied to customer contract INFRA-2247.\\n- Impact: with current staffing we estimate +30\\u201345% risk of missing the rollout milestone and elevated on-call burden across two teams.\\n\\nProposed path:\\n1) Approve HC exception to backfill Senior IC (IC4) with either direct hire or 6-month contractor through Polaris Talent (attachment: cost_breakdown_6mo.csv).\\n2) If approved, prioritize internal candidates first (we have one internal transfer candidate in org).\\n3) If approval delayed >7 days, we will request temporary time-limited escalation budget for overtime and hiring agency retained search.\\n\\nAttached: HC exception form (filled), migration risk matrix, six-month cost comparison (direct hire vs contractor).\\n\\nAsk: Approve or provide guidance on preferred funnel (internal transfer vs external contractor) by EOD Aug 18 so we can start vendor engagement.\\n\\nThanks \\u2014 Soojin\\nSoojin Lee\\nDirector, Platform Services\\nRedwood Inference\\nphone: (415) 555-0142\\n\\n[attachment: hc_exception_form.pdf] [attachment: migration_risk_matrix.xlsx] [attachment: cost_breakdown_6mo.csv]\",\n    \"From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>\\nTo: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>\\nCc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>\\nDate: 2026-08-13 11:02 -07:00\\nSubject: Re: Request: Exception to hiring freeze for Senior Infra IC (platform-migrate)\\n\\nSoojin \\u2014 thanks for the clear summary. A couple quick Qs before I greenlight:\\n\\n1) Headcount budget: do you have the hiring cost vs committed budget this FY (include recruiting fees if external)? I saw your attachment but would like a one-line delta to the org budget.\\n2) Coverage plan: if we approve internal transfer, who covers the gaps left by that transfer? (need names/teams).\\n3) SLA tolerances: quantify the customer impact in $ or churn risk if migration slips by 4 weeks.\\n\\nIf you can get me the answers and sign-off from Finance (Markus) and HR (Neha) by EOD Aug 18 I can approve the exception. If Finance can't commit, consider a 6-month contractor approval as fallback.\\n\\n\\u2014 Laura\\nVP Engineering\\nRedwood Inference\\n\\nOn Wed, Aug 12, 2026 at 9:15 AM Soojin Lee wrote:...\",\n    \"From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>\\nTo: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>\\nCc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, sarah@polaris-talent.com\\nDate: 2026-08-14 08:45 -07:00\\nSubject: Re: Request: Exception to hiring freeze for Senior Infra IC (platform-migrate)\\n\\nLaura \\u2014 quick follow with the concrete numbers you asked for:\\n\\n1) Budget delta: direct hire (mid-band IC4) fully loaded = $240k/yr total comp equivalent; recruiting + ramp = ~ $30k in Y1, so net delta to FY budget = +$270k. 6-month contractor via agency = ~$85k (includes agency fee). See cost_breakdown_6mo.csv.\\n2) Internal transfer candidate: Marcus's team (Runtime) has Anna Park (IC3) flagged as stretch candidate; if Anna moves we estimate a 40% drop in Velocity on two active runtime tickets for 8 weeks. Proposed mitigation: shift two noncritical tickets to FY27 backlog and assign a 3rd rotation from SRE for 6 weeks.\\n3) SLA impact: conservative estimate is $120k ARR at risk (single large customer migration) and increased engineering support cost ~$25k in third-party consulting if we miss milestone by 4 weeks.\\n\\nAttached is an updated one-pager summarizing these points and the requested approval box filled out on the HC exception form. I recommend approving a contractor for 6 months while we run a parallel external search \\u2014 this minimizes SLA risk and gives time to evaluate internal transfer without blocking the migration schedule.\\n\\nIf you want, I can arrange a short sync with Finance (Markus) and Neha to run through the numbers tomorrow.\\n\\n\\u2014 Soojin\\n\\n[inline: migration_risk_matrix.xlsx excerpt]\\n\\n--- Forwarded message ---\\nFrom: Sarah Miller <sarah@polaris-talent.com>\\nTo: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>\\nDate: 2026-08-14 07:22 -07:00\\nSubject: Candidate availability\\n\\nSoojin \\u2014 we have two senior infra contractors available starting 9/7 and a permanent candidate who could move by late Sept. If you'd like the contractor hold we'll need a 3-day confirmation.\\n\\nBest,\\nSarah\\nPolaris Talent\",\n    \"From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>\\nTo: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>\\nCc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>\\nDate: 2026-08-18 16:05 -07:00\\nSubject: RE: Request: Exception to hiring freeze for Senior Infra IC (platform-migrate)\\n\\nAll \\u2014 reviewed the cost sheet and migration risk matrix. Finance can support a time-limited contractor approval up to $95k for six months on the condition that: \\n\\n- Recruiting runs concurrently and we aim for a permanent hire within 4 months,\\n- Team documents handover & runbooks in the first 30 days (Soojin, please own),\\n- A post-mortem and budget reconciliation is provided to Finance within 90 days.\\n\\nLaura \\u2014 if that's acceptable from your side, consider this the Finance conditional approval. Neha \\u2014 please confirm any compliance/contracting constraints on short-term contractor engagements and confirm whether Polaris has passed vendor onboarding.\\n\\nMarkus Klein\\nDirector, Finance Planning\\nRedwood Inference\\n\\nOn Aug 14, 2026, Soojin Lee wrote:...\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"subject\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"messages\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_fada7b2423644aa1af718d9eaa50b573\"\n}",

{
  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_04b24bf957c047f4b7d8ceefdfde8290",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-declarative-contract-tests-and-schema-fencing-2026.json",
    "title": "ADR: Declarative Contract Tests and Schema Fencing",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"ADR: Declarative Contract Tests and Schema Fencing\",\n  \"space\": \"architecture-and-standards\",\n  \"author\": \"Aisha Patel\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-02-15\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2026-03-01\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Diego Martinez\",\n    \"Sara Kim\",\n    \"Liam O'Connor\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"adr\",\n    \"contract-testing\",\n    \"schema-fencing\",\n    \"ci-cd\",\n    \"conformance\"\n  ],\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/canonical-request-schema-and-validation-playbook-2025\",\n    \"/architecture-and-standards/model-serving-standards/variant-compatibility-ledger-and-stewardship-protocol-2026\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"internal\",\n  \"content\": \"Summary\\n\\nThis ADR defines a company-wide standard for declarative contract tests and a complementary \\\"schema fencing\\\" discipline to prevent schema drift between services and the Redwood platform (APIs, telemetry, and model-serving payloads). The goal is to make API and model I/O contracts machine-testable, versioned, and CI-gated, minimizing production surprises and simplifying rollback and compatibility reasoning.\\n\\nContext and motivation\\n\\nRecent incidents and near-misses were traced to silent schema changes that allowed malformed or unexpectedly shaped requests/telemetry to flow into the runtime. Ad-hoc unit tests are insufficient for cross-service contract guarantees because:\\n\\n- Contracts span teams (edge proxies, gateways, runtime, and client SDKs).\\n- Behavioral compatibility is not captured by type checks alone (e.g., field deprecation with semantic changes).\\n- Runtime routing fallback and model-variant compatibility require an explicit, testable matrix.\\n\\nThis ADR proposes:\\n\\n1. A declarative, YAML-first contract-test spec that lives next to service code and in a central conformance repo for cross-service scopes.\\n2. A \\\"schema fencing\\\" lifecycle that fences allowed shape changes via explicit change proposals, automated conformance checks, and CI gates.\\n3. A conformance status ledger and telemetry for contract drift and failed-matrix cell SLI.\\n\\nScope\\n\\nApplies to:\\n\\n- Public and internal HTTP/GRPC REST endpoints (edge, control-plane, telemetry ingestion).\\n- Model-serving input/output schemas (prompts, structured responses, embeddings metadata).\\n- Streaming/session protocols where message schemas are negotiated.\\n\\nOut of scope:\\n\\n- Internal-only helper functions that are never consumed by other services.\\n- Ad-hoc developer prototypes until they are promoted to a supported service.\\n\\nKey concepts\\n\\nDeclarative contract test spec (DCTS):\\n- A human-friendly YAML format that describes request/response shapes, example inputs, success/failure predicates, and conformance categories (strict, tolerant, deprecated).\\n- DCTS entries can be unit-run (local), CI-run (service-level), and cross-service-run (integration conformance matrix).\\n\\nSchema fencing:\\n- Every change to a DCTS schema field must be accompanied by a Change Proposal (CP) file and an automated compatibility check.\\n- CPs are accepted automatically if they pass compatibility rules or fail open for manual review if they are breaking.\\n\\nConformance matrix and ledger:\\n- A centrally aggregated matrix that tracks which service versions (and model variants) satisfy which DCTS cells.\\n- Each matrix cell has a pass/fail history and a conformance SLI aggregated daily.\\n\\nRules and compatibility classes\\n\\nFields are labeled with one of: required, optional, deprecated, extension. Compatibility rules:\\n\\n- required -> optional: allowed but requires explicit CP and CI signal.\\n- optional -> required: breaking change; requires canary/rollout plan and staged opt-in.\\n- remove deprecated field: allowed only after 3 release cycles and >95% conformance across callers.\\n- add new field marked extension: always allowed if receivers ignore unknown fields (tolerant mode).\\n\\nChange proposal workflow (brief)\\n\\n1. Author creates a CP file in the service repo under docs/contracts/cps/<pr>.yaml describing intent, compatibility class, rollout plan, and rollback criteria.\\n2. CI runs: unit tests, DCTS local run, contract linters, and cross-service dry-run against the latest conformance snapshot.\\n3. If auto-check passes (non-breaking or safe extension), merge proceeds. If flagged as potentially breaking, the CP moves to manual review by contract stewards and product owners.\\n4. After merge, integration conformance jobs run nightly to validate callers and receivers.\\n\\nExample DCTS snippet (YAML)\\n\\n# Example: /v1/generate request/response\\n# Save as service/docs/contracts/dcts/generate.v1.yaml\\n---\\nendpoint: POST /v1/generate\\nscope: public\\nversion: 1.0.0\\nmode: strict\\nrequest: \\n  content-type: application/json\\n  schema: |\\n    type: object\\n    properties:\\n      prompt:\\n        type: string\\n      features:\\n        type: object\\n        additionalProperties: true\\n    required: [prompt]\\nexamples:\\n  - name: simplest\\n    request: {\\\"prompt\\\": \\\"Summarize the following text...\\\"}\\nresponse:\\n  schema: |\\n    type: object\\n    properties:\\n      id: {type: string}\\n      output: {type: string}\\n      tokens_consumed: {type: integer}\\n    required: [id, output]\\npredicates:\\n  - description: output must be non-empty\\n    jq: \\\".output | length > 0\\\"\\nconformance_category: strict\\n\\nAutomation and CI integration\\n\\nCI responsibilities (service repo):\\n- Run local DCTS validation (schema validity, example conformance).\\n- Run contract linter: enforces required metadata fields (owner, risk_level, test_coverage_min).\\n- Publish DCTS artifact to conformance-bucket/<service>/<version>/dcts.yaml on successful merge.\\n\\nCross-repo conformance job (central):\\n- Nightly job that pulls the published DCTS artifacts and runs pairwise checks across known callers and receivers.\\n- Failing cells create RFC-style issues in the responsible service repo and update the conformance ledger with failure signals.\\n\\nConformance ledger and dashboard\\n\\nThe ledger is a time-series-friendly table with columns described below and exposed in the Redwood Console and an internal dashboard. Store as rows in our metrics DB and index in the conformance service. (Table described in prose below.)\\n\\nRequired columns (ledger row): timestamp, service_a, service_a_version, service_b, service_b_version, endpoint, dcts_version, test_case_id, result (pass|fail), failure_reason, run_id.\\n\\nOperational SLOs and alerting\\n\\n- Nightly conformance pass rate for critical public endpoints >= 99.0%. Alert if < 98.0% over a 24-hour rolling window.\\n- Any new CP that causes a regression in an existing passing matrix cell triggers a P1 review if the affected client is production and >= 10% traffic.\\n\\nGating and release policy\\n\\n- Service merge gating: Non-breaking CPs are mergeable. Breaking CPs require manual approval and a staged rollout with canary conformance verifying client behavior.\\n- Platform releases (runtime, SDKs): must maintain 100% conformance for official SDK bindings across supported minor versions.\\n\\nRollout and rollback playbook (high level)\\n\\n1. Pre-merge: author runs smoke DCTS locally and creates CP with rollout notes.\\n2. Merge: DCTS published and cross-repo nightlies scheduled.\\n3. Canary: route 5% traffic to new service variant for 2 hours while conformance checks run.\\n4. Monitor: observe ledger and user-facing errors for regressions.\\n5. If failure SLI breached or critical callers fail, execute rollback to previous version and open an incident review.\\n\\nTelemetry and observability requirements\\n\\nEach contract-test run must emit:\\n- conftest.run_id (UUID)\\n- conftest.service (service name/version)\\n- conftest.endpoint\\n- conftest.test_case_id\\n- conftest.result (pass|fail)\\n- conftest.duration_ms\\n\\nThese fields are sent to the conformance-ingest pipeline with low-cardinality sampling for historical debugging. Link failures to trace IDs when available.\\n\\nOwner and stewardship\\n\\n- Contract steward role: a cross-functional team (API Platform + SRE + Product) that maintains the conformance harness, linter rules, and central ledger.\\n- Service owners: must author and maintain DCTS files for each public surface and model variant.\\n\\nOpen questions and tradeoffs\\n\\n- How strict should default mode be for internal endpoints? Proposal: internal endpoints default to tolerant mode, but any endpoint used by another service must be promoted to strict with a DCTS.\\n- Cost vs. coverage: nightly full-matrix checks are expensive. We propose prioritized sweeps (critical endpoints every night, others weekly).\\n\\nMigration plan\\n\\n1. Pilot: Onboard three services (edge-proxy, runtime-controller, and the embeddings-ingest) to the DCTS and CP workflow over Q2 2026.\\n2. Expand to all public endpoints and model-serving inputs by Q4 2026.\\n3. Enforce gate for new public endpoints starting Q1 2027.\\n\\nAppendix: sample CLI commands and linter config\\n\\n# Local validation\\n#   conftest validate service/docs/contracts/dcts/*.yaml\\n\\n# Publish artifact (CI step)\\n#   conftest publish --bucket=conformance-bucket --service=$SERVICE --version=$VERSION dcts.yaml\\n\\n# Central conformance run (dry-run example)\\n#   conformance-runner --matrix-file=matrix.json --artifacts-dir=artifacts/ --output=ledger.csv\\n\\n# Linter rules (excerpt)\\n# required: [owner, risk_level, conformance_category, test_coverage_min]\\n\\nNotes on documentation style\\n\\n- Keep DCTS files short and example-driven. Prefer real-world examples over exhaustive machine-generated schemas.\\n- Use the CP description field to capture rationale and expected client impact.\\n\\nReferences\\n\\n- See canonical request schema and validation playbook: /architecture-and-standards/api-standards/canonical-request-schema-and-validation-playbook-2025\\n- Variant compatibility ledger: /architecture-and-standards/model-serving-standards/variant-compatibility-ledger-and-stewardship-protocol-2026\\n\\nApproval\\n\\nApproved by: API Platform leadership, SRE management, and Product for runtime conformance.\\n\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"content\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_04b24bf957c047f4b7d8ceefdfde8290\"\n}",

document.title: ADR: Declarative Contract Tests and Schema Fencing
document.content:
{
  "title": "ADR: Declarative Contract Tests and Schema Fencing",
  "space": "architecture-and-standards",
  "author": "Aisha Patel",
  "owner_team": "engineering",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2026-02-15",
  "last_updated": "2026-03-01",
  "reviewers": [
    "Diego Martinez",
    "Sara Kim",
    "Liam O'Connor"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "adr",
    "contract-testing",
    "schema-fencing",
    "ci-cd",
    "conformance"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/canonical-request-schema-and-validation-playbook-2025",
    "/architecture-and-standards/model-serving-standards/variant-compatibility-ledger-and-stewardship-protocol-2026"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "content": "Summary

This ADR defines a company-wide standard for declarative contract tests and a complementary "schema fencing" discipline to prevent schema drift between services and the Redwood platform (APIs, telemetry, and model-serving payloads). The goal is to make API and model I/O contracts machine-testable, versioned, and CI-gated, minimizing production surprises and simplifying rollback and compatibility reasoning.

Context and motivation

Recent incidents and near-misses were traced to silent schema changes that allowed malformed or unexpectedly shaped requests/telemetry to flow into the runtime. Ad-hoc unit tests are insufficient for cross-service contract guarantees because:

- Contracts span teams (edge proxies, gateways, runtime, and client SDKs).
- Behavioral compatibility is not captured by type checks alone (e.g., field deprecation with semantic changes).
- Runtime routing fallback and model-variant compatibility require an explicit, testable matrix.

This ADR proposes:

1. A declarative, YAML-first contract-test spec that lives next to service code and in a central conformance repo for cross-service scopes.
2. A "schema fencing" lifecycle that fences allowed shape changes via explicit change proposals, automated conformance checks, and CI gates.
3. A conformance status ledger and telemetry for contract drift and failed-matrix cell SLI.

Scope

Applies to:

- Public and internal HTTP/GRPC REST endpoints (edge, control-plane, telemetry ingestion).
- Model-serving input/output schemas (prompts, structured responses, embeddings metadata).
- Streaming/session protocols where message schemas are negotiated.

Out of scope:

- Internal-only helper functions that are never consumed by other services.
- Ad-hoc developer prototypes until they are promoted to a supported service.

Key concepts

Declarative contract test spec (DCTS):
- A human-friendly YAML format that describes request/response shapes, example inputs, success/failure predicates, and conformance categories (strict, tolerant, deprecated).
- DCTS entries can be unit-run (local), CI-run (service-level), and cross-service-run (integration conformance matrix).

Schema fencing:
- Every change to a DCTS schema field must be accompanied by a Change Proposal (CP) file and an automated compatibility check.
- CPs are accepted automatically if they pass compatibility rules or fail open for manual review if they are breaking.

Conformance matrix and ledger:
- A centrally aggregated matrix that tracks which service versions (and model variants) satisfy which DCTS cells.
- Each matrix cell has a pass/fail history and a conformance SLI aggregated daily.

Rules and compatibility classes

Fields are labeled with one of: required, optional, deprecated, extension. Compatibility rules:

- required -> optional: allowed but requires explicit CP and CI signal.
- optional -> required: breaking change; requires canary/rollout plan and staged opt-in.
- remove deprecated field: allowed only after 3 release cycles and >95% conformance across callers.
- add new field marked extension: always allowed if receivers ignore unknown fields (tolerant mode).

Change proposal workflow (brief)

1. Author creates a CP file in the service repo under docs/contracts/cps/<pr>.yaml describing intent, compatibility class, rollout plan, and rollback criteria.
2. CI runs: unit tests, DCTS local run, contract linters, and cross-service dry-run against the latest conformance snapshot.
3. If auto-check passes (non-breaking or safe extension), merge proceeds. If flagged as potentially breaking, the CP moves to manual review by contract stewards and product owners.
4. After merge, integration conformance jobs run nightly to validate callers and receivers.

Example DCTS snippet (YAML)

# Example: /v1/generate request/response
# Save as service/docs/contracts/dcts/generate.v1.yaml
---
endpoint: POST /v1/generate
scope: public
version: 1.0.0
mode: strict
request: 
  content-type: application/json
  schema: |
    type: object
    properties:
      prompt:
        type: string
      features:
        type: object
        additionalProperties: true
    required: [prompt]
examples:
  - name: simplest
    request: {"prompt": "Summarize the following text..."}
response:
  schema: |
    type: object
    properties:
      id: {type: string}
      output: {type: string}
      tokens_consumed: {type: integer}
    required: [id, output]
predicates:
  - description: output must be non-empty
    jq: ".output | length > 0"
conformance_category: strict

Automation and CI integration

CI responsibilities (service repo):
- Run local DCTS validation (schema validity, example conformance).
- Run contract linter: enforces required metadata fields (owner, risk_level, test_coverage_min).
- Publish DCTS artifact to conformance-bucket/<service>/<version>/dcts.yaml on successful merge.

Cross-repo conformance job (central):
- Nightly job that pulls the published DCTS artifacts and runs pairwise checks across known callers and receivers.
- Failing cells create RFC-style issues in the responsible service repo and update the conformance ledger with failure signals.

Conformance ledger and dashboard

The ledger is a time-series-friendly table with columns described below and exposed in the Redwood Console and an internal dashboard. Store as rows in our metrics DB and index in the conformance service. (Table described in prose below.)

Required columns (ledger row): timestamp, service_a, service_a_version, service_b, service_b_version, endpoint, dcts_version, test_case_id, result (pass|fail), failure_reason, run_id.

Operational SLOs and alerting

- Nightly conformance pass rate for critical public endpoints >= 99.0%. Alert if < 98.0% over a 24-hour rolling window.
- Any new CP that causes a regression in an existing passing matrix cell triggers a P1 review if the affected client is production and >= 10% traffic.

Gating and release policy

- Service merge gating: Non-breaking CPs are mergeable. Breaking CPs require manual approval and a staged rollout with canary conformance verifying client behavior.
- Platform releases (runtime, SDKs): must maintain 100% conformance for official SDK bindings across supported minor versions.

Rollout and rollback playbook (high level)

1. Pre-merge: author runs smoke DCTS locally and creates CP with rollout notes.
2. Merge: DCTS published and cross-repo nightlies scheduled.
3. Canary: route 5% traffic to new service variant for 2 hours while conformance checks run.
4. Monitor: observe ledger and user-facing errors for regressions.
5. If failure SLI breached or critical callers fail, execute rollback to previous version and open an incident review.

Telemetry and observability requirements

Each contract-test run must emit:
- conftest.run_id (UUID)
- conftest.service (service name/version)
- conftest.endpoint
- conftest.test_case_id
- conftest.result (pass|fail)
- conftest.duration_ms

These fields are sent to the conformance-ingest pipeline with low-cardinality sampling for historical debugging. Link failures to trace IDs when available.

Owner and stewardship

- Contract steward role: a cross-functional team (API Platform + SRE + Product) that maintains the conformance harness, linter rules, and central ledger.
- Service owners: must author and maintain DCTS files for each public surface and model variant.

Open questions and tradeoffs

- How strict should default mode be for internal endpoints? Proposal: internal endpoints default to tolerant mode, but any endpoint used by another service must be promoted to strict with a DCTS.
- Cost vs. coverage: nightly full-matrix checks are expensive. We propose prioritized sweeps (critical endpoints every night, others weekly).

Migration plan

1. Pilot: Onboard three services (edge-proxy, runtime-controller, and the embeddings-ingest) to the DCTS and CP workflow over Q2 2026.
2. Expand to all public endpoints and model-serving inputs by Q4 2026.
3. Enforce gate for new public endpoints starting Q1 2027.

Appendix: sample CLI commands and linter config

# Local validation
#   conftest validate service/docs/contracts/dcts/*.yaml

# Publish artifact (CI step)
#   conftest publish --bucket=conformance-bucket --service=$SERVICE --version=$VERSION dcts.yaml

# Central conformance run (dry-run example)
#   conformance-runner --matrix-file=matrix.json --artifacts-dir=artifacts/ --output=ledger.csv

# Linter rules (excerpt)
# required: [owner, risk_level, conformance_category, test_coverage_min]

Notes on documentation style

- Keep DCTS files short and example-driven. Prefer real-world examples over exhaustive machine-generated schemas.
- Use the CP description field to capture rationale and expected client impact.

References

- See canonical request schema and validation playbook: /architecture-and-standards/api-standards/canonical-request-schema-and-validation-playbook-2025
- Variant compatibility ledger: /architecture-and-standards/model-serving-standards/variant-compatibility-ledger-and-stewardship-protocol-2026

Approval

Approved by: API Platform leadership, SRE management, and Product for runtime conformance.

    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-48123-embedding-calibration-sentinel.json",
    "title": "Embedding calibration & drift sentinel: nightly eval + rerank latency probes",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/linear",
    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"ENG-48123\",\n  \"team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"title\": \"Embedding calibration & drift sentinel: nightly eval + rerank latency probes\",\n  \"status\": \"In Progress\",\n  \"priority\": \"P1\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-02-15\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2025-02-28\",\n  \"creator\": \"Ariana Patel\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Diego Morales\",\n  \"project\": \"embed-quality\",\n  \"cycle\": \"2025-W08\",\n  \"estimate\": \"8\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2025-03-10\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"embeddings\",\n    \"rerank\",\n    \"drift\",\n    \"nightly\",\n    \"telemetry\",\n    \"calibration\"\n  ],\n  \"parent_issue\": [\n    \"ENG-46890\"\n  ],\n  \"dependencies\": [\n    \"ENG-47200\",\n    \"ENG-47911\"\n  ],\n  \"customer_impact\": \"high\",\n  \"release\": \"runtime-1.22\",\n  \"security_review_required\": \"false\",\n  \"description\": \"Objective: Build a production-ready evaluation harness that runs nightly to validate embedding accuracy and reranking fidelity, detect distribution drift, and capture latency/backpressure signals for the reranking endpoint. The harness will combine curated anchor sets (small high-quality reference queries + human-labeled relevance tiers), synthetic perturbations, and production-sampled traffic probes to provide both offline quality metrics and operational alerts.\\n\\nWhy: We have observed intermittent regressions after model swaps and quantization profile changes; current alerts are noisy and slow. A focused nightly sentinel will surface systematic quality shifts, and adding lightweight rerank latency probes will correlate quality changes with SLO violations.\\n\\nScope:\\n- Curate a compact \\\"anchor\\\" reference corpus (2k queries across domains, with graded relevance labels) stored in s3://redwood-embed-gold/anchor-v1/\\n- Nightly batch job that computes: recall@1/5/10, MRR, NDCG@10, mean cosine drift, calibration_score (distance -> rerank score monotonicity), and a lightweight rerank latency microbenchmark (p95/p99 token latency and end-to-end rerank latency).\\n- Drift detectors: population KS test on cosine similarity distributions, centroid shift cosine, and online change point detection on MRR using EWMA; configurable thresholds per-customer and global baselines.\\n- Alerting: If drift or quality regression exceeds thresholds, create a ticket, send Slack/SRE paged runbook link, and attach a snapshot of top failing queries and histogram diffs.\\n- Telemetry: Emit deltas into Grafana dashboard and Record in BigQuery daily table for longitudinal analysis.\\n\\nAcceptance criteria:\\n1) Nightly job runs successfully for last 7 consecutive nights on staging and sends artifacts to s3 and BigQuery.\\n2) Calculated metrics (recall@k, MRR, NDCG) have stable baselines and documented test harness reproducibility (seeded).\\n3) Drift detectors fire with <5% false positive rate on synthetic non-drift runs and detect injected drift scenarios in internal tests.\\n4) Rerank latency microbenchmark correlates with observed production SLO violations in at least two historical incidents.\\n5) Runbook and automated ticket creation implemented; on-drift action triggers an ENG triage workflow.\\n\\nImplementation plan:\\n- Week 1: Anchor set curation (PM + Research + Data team) and schema (label tiers, canonical query canonicalization).\\n- Week 2: Batch evaluation job (Spark/Beam) to compute offline metrics + synthetic perturbations generator.\\n- Week 3: Lightweight rerank probe harness (go microclient) and integration into nightly flow.\\n- Week 4: Drift detectors, thresholds, dashboards, and alerting hooks.\\n- Week 5: Runbook, automation for ticketing, and staging validation.\\n\\nArtifacts:\\n- Confluence design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/Embed+Calibration+Sentinel (design + thresholds)\\n- Proto PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1482\\n- Dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/embeds/embedding-quality-sentinel\\n- Anchor S3: s3://redwood-embed-gold/anchor-v1/\",\n  \"updates\": [\n    \"2025-02-15 \\u2014 Triage: initial scope and owner assigned. Ariana curated initial anchor set candidates (1200 queries across docs, chat, queries).\",\n    \"2025-02-17 \\u2014 Decision: use seeded synthetic perturbations (token dropout, paraphrase, template swap) to create drift tests; flagged need for human relabeling of 300 ambiguous queries \\u2014 assigned to DataOps.\",\n    \"2025-02-19 \\u2014 Design review: team (Eng, Research, PM) agreed on metrics: recall@1/5/10, MRR, NDCG@10, calibration monotonicity. Action: Diego to prototype Beam job for nightly metrics.\",\n    \"2025-02-21 \\u2014 PR opened: infra/pull/1482 contains batch job scaffolding and S3 integration. Requesting review from infra and observability.\",\n    \"2025-02-23 \\u2014 Blocker: Observability team noted missing BigQuery dataset permissions for service account; ticket created ENG-48590 to provision. Working with SRE.\",\n    \"2025-02-25 \\u2014 Prototype results: staging run on anchor-v1 shows baseline MRR=0.62, recall@1=0.48. Synthetic drift injection (add gaussian noise to embeddings) reduced recall@1 by 0.12 and fired KS alpha=0.01. Need to tune alert thresholds to reduce noise from small runtime fluctuations.\",\n    \"2025-02-28 \\u2014 Infra PR merged for rerank probe client (infra/pull/1497). Next: wire probe to nightly pipeline and add dashboard panels for p95/p99 latencies. Preparing runbook for triage flow.\"\n  ],\n  \"notes\": [\n    \"Trade-offs: small anchor sets are manageable and fast to run nightly but may miss low-frequency regressions; plan to add periodic full-corpus runs weekly.\",\n    \"Calibration approach: we will compute monotonicity score instead of trying to map distance to absolute probabilities to avoid brittleness across model families.\",\n    \"Alerting policy: start with conservative thresholds and collect 14 days of signal before escalating to paging for P1 customers.\"\n  ],\n  \"artifacts\": [\n    \"Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/Embed+Calibration+Sentinel\",\n    \"PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1482\",\n    \"PR rerank probe: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1497\",\n    \"Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/embeds/embedding-quality-sentinel\",\n    \"S3 anchor: s3://redwood-embed-gold/anchor-v1/\",\n    \"BQ table: redwood_prod.embed_quality.daily_metrics\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"updates\",\n    \"notes\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_a701c13b9d9c4f8699164cf8899b6564\"\n}",

document.title: Embedding calibration & drift sentinel: nightly eval + rerank latency probes
document.content:
{
  "key": "ENG-48123",
  "team": "engineering",
  "title": "Embedding calibration & drift sentinel: nightly eval + rerank latency probes",
  "status": "In Progress",
  "priority": "P1",
  "created_at": "2025-02-15",
  "updated_at": "2025-02-28",
  "creator": "Ariana Patel",
  "assignee": "Diego Morales",
  "project": "embed-quality",
  "cycle": "2025-W08",
  "estimate": "8",
  "due_date": "2025-03-10",
  "labels": [
    "embeddings",
    "rerank",
    "drift",
    "nightly",
    "telemetry",
    "calibration"
  ],
  "parent_issue": [
    "ENG-46890"
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    "ENG-47200",
    "ENG-47911"
  ],
  "customer_impact": "high",
  "release": "runtime-1.22",
  "security_review_required": "false",
  "description": "Objective: Build a production-ready evaluation harness that runs nightly to validate embedding accuracy and reranking fidelity, detect distribution drift, and capture latency/backpressure signals for the reranking endpoint. The harness will combine curated anchor sets (small high-quality reference queries + human-labeled relevance tiers), synthetic perturbations, and production-sampled traffic probes to provide both offline quality metrics and operational alerts.\n\nWhy: We have observed intermittent regressions after model swaps and quantization profile changes; current alerts are noisy and slow. A focused nightly sentinel will surface systematic quality shifts, and adding lightweight rerank latency probes will correlate quality changes with SLO violations.\n\nScope:\n- Curate a compact \"anchor\" reference corpus (2k queries across domains, with graded relevance labels) stored in s3://redwood-embed-gold/anchor-v1/\n- Nightly batch job that computes: recall@1/5/10, MRR, NDCG@10, mean cosine drift, calibration_score (distance -> rerank score monotonicity), and a lightweight rerank latency microbenchmark (p95/p99 token latency and end-to-end rerank latency).\n- Drift detectors: population KS test on cosine similarity distributions, centroid shift cosine, and online change point detection on MRR using EWMA; configurable thresholds per-customer and global baselines.\n- Alerting: If drift or quality regression exceeds thresholds, create a ticket, send Slack/SRE paged runbook link, and attach a snapshot of top failing queries and histogram diffs.\n- Telemetry: Emit deltas into Grafana dashboard and Record in BigQuery daily table for longitudinal analysis.\n\nAcceptance criteria:\n1) Nightly job runs successfully for last 7 consecutive nights on staging and sends artifacts to s3 and BigQuery.\n2) Calculated metrics (recall@k, MRR, NDCG) have stable baselines and documented test harness reproducibility (seeded).\n3) Drift detectors fire with <5% false positive rate on synthetic non-drift runs and detect injected drift scenarios in internal tests.\n4) Rerank latency microbenchmark correlates with observed production SLO violations in at least two historical incidents.\n5) Runbook and automated ticket creation implemented; on-drift action triggers an ENG triage workflow.\n\nImplementation plan:\n- Week 1: Anchor set curation (PM + Research + Data team) and schema (label tiers, canonical query canonicalization).\n- Week 2: Batch evaluation job (Spark/Beam) to compute offline metrics + synthetic perturbations generator.\n- Week 3: Lightweight rerank probe harness (go microclient) and integration into nightly flow.\n- Week 4: Drift detectors, thresholds, dashboards, and alerting hooks.\n- Week 5: Runbook, automation for ticketing, and staging validation.\n\nArtifacts:\n- Confluence design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/Embed+Calibration+Sentinel (design + thresholds)\n- Proto PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1482\n- Dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/embeds/embedding-quality-sentinel\n- Anchor S3: s3://redwood-embed-gold/anchor-v1/",
  "updates": [
    "2025-02-15 \u2014 Triage: initial scope and owner assigned. Ariana curated initial anchor set candidates (1200 queries across docs, chat, queries).",
    "2025-02-17 \u2014 Decision: use seeded synthetic perturbations (token dropout, paraphrase, template swap) to create drift tests; flagged need for human relabeling of 300 ambiguous queries \u2014 assigned to DataOps.",
    "2025-02-19 \u2014 Design review: team (Eng, Research, PM) agreed on metrics: recall@1/5/10, MRR, NDCG@10, calibration monotonicity. Action: Diego to prototype Beam job for nightly metrics.",
    "2025-02-21 \u2014 PR opened: infra/pull/1482 contains batch job scaffolding and S3 integration. Requesting review from infra and observability.",
    "2025-02-23 \u2014 Blocker: Observability team noted missing BigQuery dataset permissions for service account; ticket created ENG-48590 to provision. Working with SRE.",
    "2025-02-25 \u2014 Prototype results: staging run on anchor-v1 shows baseline MRR=0.62, recall@1=0.48. Synthetic drift injection (add gaussian noise to embeddings) reduced recall@1 by 0.12 and fired KS alpha=0.01. Need to tune alert thresholds to reduce noise from small runtime fluctuations.",
    "2025-02-28 \u2014 Infra PR merged for rerank probe client (infra/pull/1497). Next: wire probe to nightly pipeline and add dashboard panels for p95/p99 latencies. Preparing runbook for triage flow."
  ],
  "notes": [
    "Trade-offs: small anchor sets are manageable and fast to run nightly but may miss low-frequency regressions; plan to add periodic full-corpus runs weekly.",
    "Calibration approach: we will compute monotonicity score instead of trying to map distance to absolute probabilities to avoid brittleness across model families.",
    "Alerting policy: start with conservative thresholds and collect 14 days of signal before escalating to paging for P1 customers."
  ],
  "artifacts": [
    "Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/Embed+Calibration+Sentinel",
    "PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1482",
    "PR rerank probe: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1497",
    "Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/embeds/embedding-quality-sentinel",
    "S3 anchor: s3://redwood-embed-gold/anchor-v1/",
    "BQ table: redwood_prod.embed_quality.daily_metrics"
  ],
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "description",
    "updates",
    "notes"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_a701c13b9d9c4f8699164cf8899b6564"
}

{
  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_f853f992f7a0416ea9ab1c2b287f61dc",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/slack/eng-ml/1760004322-intake-bench-phase-contracts.json",
    "title": "1760004322 intake bench phase contracts",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/slack",
    "content": "{\n  \"channel\": \"eng-ml\",\n  \"thread_ts\": \"1760004322\",\n  \"first_message_ts\": \"1760004322\",\n  \"last_message_ts\": \"1760004442\",\n  \"participants\": [\n    \"jia\",\n    \"mike\",\n    \"sara\",\n    \"oliver\",\n    \"bench-bot\"\n  ],\n  \"text\": \"jia: Quick follow-up on the onboarding pipeline tradeoffs \\u2014 thinking about moving the heavy bench (full golden/regression eval) to async post-accept, and keep the fast adapter/tokenizer checks sync at intake. Thoughts?\\n\\nmike: Agree in principle. Main risk is we accept models that pass lightweight checks but fail the heavy bench later => downstream quality incidents. We need mitigations: canary traffic + auto-rollback and a clear quarantine state.\\n\\nsara: Proposal: two-phase acceptance. 1) intake sync smoke: tokenizer sanity, basic forward pass, tiny perf check. 2) gated async bench: full golden + regression eval on reserved bench pool. If async fails, mark model as `quarantine` and block routing. Also need a narrow interface between intake and bench for signals.\\n\\noliver: Important note \\u2014 keep a compact \\\"fast-probe\\\" golden set in intake (~50 inputs) to catch obvious mismatches (tokenizer encodings, padding, EOS behavior). That will reduce wasteful async runs. Bench infra should emit categorical verdicts: accept / flag / critical-fail.\\n\\njia: How should we version golden artifacts? If intake and async bench use different golden sets we risk false positives/negatives. Idea: store `golden_set_id` in model metadata and surface it to runtime & bench.\\n\\nmike: +1. Also: make smoke thresholds intentionally loose; async bench enforces strict thresholds. For rollout, use shadow traffic + small canaries to validate behavior on real queries before full promotion.\\n\\nsara: API contract sketch: intake returns a candidate_id. Bench polls /bench-status?candidate_id or we push a webhook. Bench status payload should include: status, failed_tests[], drift_score, latency_p95, golden_set_id. Example minimal payload:\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"candidate_id\\\": \\\"cand-2026-03-01-42\\\",\\n  \\\"status\\\": \\\"quarantine\\\",\\n  \\\"failed_tests\\\": [\\\"regression:qa-v2\\\"],\\n  \\\"drift_score\\\": \\\"0.32\\\",\\n  \\\"latency_p95_ms\\\": \\\"312\\\",\\n  \\\"golden_set_id\\\": \\\"gold-2026-02-15-v3\\\"\\n}\\n```\\n\\nbench-bot: Bench job queued: candidate_id=cand-2026-03-01-42, estimated_gpu_hours=3, expected_completion=~6h. Status webhook will fire to intake when done.\\n\\noliver: Ops checklist: we need cost caps for async bench (max GPU-hours per org/day) and a fallback if bench never completes (e.g., pending >24h => auto-reject or require human override). Also consider prioritization queue for high-risk customers.\\n\\njia: Noted. I'll draft a short RFC with proposed API surface, lifecycle states (candidate -> accepted_pending_bench -> accepted / quarantine / rejected), and rollout recipe (shadow -> small canary -> ramp). Will include golden_set versioning + sample inputs for intake. Volunteers to review the RFC? :coffee:\\nmike: I'll review. :+1:\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"channel\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"text\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_f853f992f7a0416ea9ab1c2b287f61dc\"\n}",

{
  "channel": "eng-ml",
  "thread_ts": "1760004322",
  "first_message_ts": "1760004322",
  "last_message_ts": "1760004442",
  "participants": [
    "jia",
    "mike",
    "sara",
    "oliver",
    "bench-bot"
  ],
  "text": "jia: Quick follow-up on the onboarding pipeline tradeoffs — thinking about moving the heavy bench (full golden/regression eval) to async post-accept, and keep the fast adapter/tokenizer checks sync at intake. Thoughts?

mike: Agree in principle. Main risk is we accept models that pass lightweight checks but fail the heavy bench later => downstream quality incidents. We need mitigations: canary traffic + auto-rollback and a clear quarantine state.

sara: Proposal: two-phase acceptance. 1) intake sync smoke: tokenizer sanity, basic forward pass, tiny perf check. 2) gated async bench: full golden + regression eval on reserved bench pool. If async fails, mark model as `quarantine` and block routing. Also need a narrow interface between intake and bench for signals.

oliver: Important note — keep a compact "fast-probe" golden set in intake (~50 inputs) to catch obvious mismatches (tokenizer encodings, padding, EOS behavior). That will reduce wasteful async runs. Bench infra should emit categorical verdicts: accept / flag / critical-fail.

jia: How should we version golden artifacts? If intake and async bench use different golden sets we risk false positives/negatives. Idea: store `golden_set_id` in model metadata and surface it to runtime & bench.

mike: +1. Also: make smoke thresholds intentionally loose; async bench enforces strict thresholds. For rollout, use shadow traffic + small canaries to validate behavior on real queries before full promotion.

sara: API contract sketch: intake returns a candidate_id. Bench polls /bench-status?candidate_id or we push a webhook. Bench status payload should include: status, failed_tests[], drift_score, latency_p95, golden_set_id. Example minimal payload:
```json
{
  "candidate_id": "cand-2026-03-01-42",
  "status": "quarantine",
  "failed_tests": ["regression:qa-v2"],
  "drift_score": "0.32",
  "latency_p95_ms": "312",
  "golden_set_id": "gold-2026-02-15-v3"
}
```

bench-bot: Bench job queued: candidate_id=cand-2026-03-01-42, estimated_gpu_hours=3, expected_completion=~6h. Status webhook will fire to intake when done.

oliver: Ops checklist: we need cost caps for async bench (max GPU-hours per org/day) and a fallback if bench never completes (e.g., pending >24h => auto-reject or require human override). Also consider prioritization queue for high-risk customers.

jia: Noted. I'll draft a short RFC with proposed API surface, lifecycle states (candidate -> accepted_pending_bench -> accepted / quarantine / rejected), and rollout recipe (shadow -> small canary -> ramp). Will include golden_set versioning + sample inputs for intake. Volunteers to review the RFC? :coffee:
mike: I'll review. :+1:",

    "content": "{\n  \"meeting_id\": \"ff-20250211-001\",\n  \"recorded_at\": \"2025-02-11T16:00:00-08:00\",\n  \"duration_minutes\": \"40\",\n  \"call_type\": \"other\",\n  \"title\": \"Candidate Interview: Senior Sales Engineer\",\n  \"redwood_owner\": \"Sophie Martinez\",\n  \"redwood_attendees\": [\n    \"Sophie Martinez\",\n    \"Evan Liu\"\n  ],\n  \"customer_company\": \"Candidate: Priya Rao\",\n  \"customer_attendees\": [\n    \"Priya Rao (Candidate)\",\n    \"Leah Kim (Recruiter)\"\n  ],\n  \"transcription_quality\": \"medium\",\n  \"summary\": \"First-stage technical interview for a Senior Sales Engineer candidate. Covered candidate background, systems experience, brief product walkthrough, and a short troubleshooting scenario. Agreed on next steps: a take-home assignment and scheduling a panel interview.\",\n  \"topics\": [\n    \"background and experience\",\n    \"technical troubleshooting scenario\",\n    \"Redwood product fit\",\n    \"next steps and scheduling\"\n  ],\n  \"next_steps\": [\n    \"Sophie to send take-home assignment by 2025-02-12\",\n    \"Schedule panel interview with PM and Eng by 2025-02-18\",\n    \"Recruiter to confirm candidate availability\"\n  ],\n  \"action_items\": [\n    \"Sophie Martinez - send assignment - 2025-02-12\",\n    \"Evan Liu - prepare technical rubric and notes - 2025-02-14\",\n    \"Leah Kim - confirm panel availability - 2025-02-13\"\n  ],\n  \"competitors_mentioned\": [\n    \"Databricks\",\n    \"Anthropic\"\n  ],\n  \"transcript\": \"Meeting Header:\\nDate: 2025-02-11\\nTime: 16:00 PST\\nDuration: 40 minutes\\nAttendees: Sophie Martinez (Redwood AE), Evan Liu (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Candidate), Leah Kim (Recruiter)\\n\\n[00:00] Sophie Martinez: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. This is Sophie from Redwood, Evan's with me. Priya, thanks for taking the time today. Can you hear us ok?\\n[00:08] Priya Rao: Yes, I can hear you. Thanks for having me.\\n[00:12] Evan Liu: Great, we'll start with a quick intro then jump to a short technical scenario. Sounds good?\\n[00:16] Priya Rao: Sounds perfect.\\n[00:20] Sophie Martinez: Cool. Priya, can you give a 2-3 minute background\\u2014recent roles, what you've been shipping, and why you're interested in Redwood?\\n[00:32] Priya Rao: Sure. I most recently was at InfraAnalytics where I was a senior solutions engineer supporting AI infra customers, mostly focused on model serving and cost optimizations. I worked a lot with GPU provisioning, autoscaling policies, and helping customers design fallback routing for multi-model setups. I'm excited about Redwood because of the focus on production-grade inference\\u2014I've seen a lot of customers struggle with predictable latency and cost, so the product fit seems good for my background.\\n[01:05] Evan Liu: When you say autoscaling policies, can you give an example\\u2014like what metrics you tuned and tradeoffs you considered?\\n[01:12] Priya Rao: We tuned on queue length and P95 latency for the endpoint. The tradeoff was throughput vs. cold-starts; we had to pick batch windows carefully so spikes didn't blow up latency, and we used a small warm pool to avoid tail latency for critical routes. Also we used quantized weights at night for cost savings on non-critical workloads.\\n[01:38] Sophie Martinez: Nice, that aligns with what our Optimize team talks about. Quick question about customer conversations\\u2014how did you surface reliability concerns without scaring customers about cost?\\n[01:50] Priya Rao: I led with SLOs and a simple example: show them current costs and what latency looks like with and without aggressive batching. I often propose a two-stage rollout: first optimize for cost in staging, then pin to a more conservative config in prod and monitor.\\n[02:10] Evan Liu: Ok, let's do a short troubleshooting scenario. Imagine a customer reports intermittent 5xxs from streaming API when traffic spikes. Walk me through your investigation and immediate mitigations.\\n[02:22] Priya Rao: First I'd confirm the scope: is it a single model, region, or route? Check the gateway and per-route logs, look at KV cache hit rates, and check GPU memory pressure. Immediate mitigations: enable rate-limiting/queue throttling, fallback to a lower-capacity model variant, or divert non-critical traffic to a cached response. For long-term fix, tune batching thresholds and increase warm pool or adjust autoscaler cooldowns.\\n[03:05] Evan Liu: In practice, when you say divert to cached response, what kind of cache policies did you use?\\n[03:12] Priya Rao: Mostly prefix and user-session cache for deterministic flows, TTL-based for semistochastic outputs. We were careful with PII\\u2014consistent with KMS policies\\u2014so cache keys were hashed and encrypted.\\n[03:30] Sophie Martinez: There's sometimes confusion between caching and reranking\\u2014good answer. Follow-up: have you ever helped design a private deployment or VPC/on-prem setup?\\n[03:40] Priya Rao: Yes, we ran a couple private deployments. Main issues were networking: TLS cert management, DNS, and ensuring audit logs to the customer's SIEM. For onboarding we provided runbooks for firewall rules and IAM roles.\\n[03:58] Evan Liu: Any experience with HSM/KMS integrations?\\n[04:02] Priya Rao: Yes, customers usually had a preferred KMS. We wrote examples for AWS KMS and a generic HSM handshake.\\n[04:12] Leah Kim: Priya, quick note on timeline\\u2014are you available for a take-home exercise this week?\\n[04:18] Priya Rao: Yes, I am. I can take it and return within 48 hours.\\n[04:22] Sophie Martinez: Great. Final part: do you have any questions for us?\\n[04:26] Priya Rao: A couple. One, how do teams at Redwood balance latency SLOs vs. model cost when running mixed workloads? Two, what's the typical ramp for a new hire in SE?\\n[04:36] Evan Liu: For the first\\u2014it's a combination of RBAC-based routing and workload tagging; we use profiling to recommend quantization, autoscale settings, and sometimes model-variant routing. In product it's a lot of labelling routes by criticality and setting different batch windows.\\n[04:52] Sophie Martinez: On ramp\\u2014two weeks onboarding then shadowing calls for about a month; you pair with an AE/SE for the first quarter on new accounts.\\n[05:00] Priya Rao: That sounds good.\\n[05:03] Sophie Martinez: Ok we'll wrap. Leah, we'll send the take-home and schedule the panel. Priya, thanks again.\\n[05:10] Leah Kim: Thanks, everyone.\\n\\n(Transcription notes: occasional overlap and filler words; some technical terms auto-corrected\\u2014e.g., KV cache was sometimes transcribed as \\\"K-V cash\\\").\",\n  \"dataset_noise_document\": true,\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"summary\",\n    \"transcript\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_2c9dcc3afa3249f39c725884e5be5c72\"\n}",

document.content:
{
  "meeting_id": "ff-20250211-001",
  "recorded_at": "2025-02-11T16:00:00-08:00",
  "duration_minutes": "40",
  "call_type": "other",
  "title": "Candidate Interview: Senior Sales Engineer",
  "redwood_owner": "Sophie Martinez",
  "redwood_attendees": [
    "Sophie Martinez",
    "Evan Liu"
  ],
  "customer_company": "Candidate: Priya Rao",
  "customer_attendees": [
    "Priya Rao (Candidate)",
    "Leah Kim (Recruiter)"
  ],
  "transcription_quality": "medium",
  "summary": "First-stage technical interview for a Senior Sales Engineer candidate. Covered candidate background, systems experience, brief product walkthrough, and a short troubleshooting scenario. Agreed on next steps: a take-home assignment and scheduling a panel interview.",
  "topics": [
    "background and experience",
    "technical troubleshooting scenario",
    "Redwood product fit",
    "next steps and scheduling"
  ],
  "next_steps": [
    "Sophie to send take-home assignment by 2025-02-12",
    "Schedule panel interview with PM and Eng by 2025-02-18",
    "Recruiter to confirm candidate availability"
  ],
  "action_items": [
    "Sophie Martinez - send assignment - 2025-02-12",
    "Evan Liu - prepare technical rubric and notes - 2025-02-14",
    "Leah Kim - confirm panel availability - 2025-02-13"
  ],
  "competitors_mentioned": [
    "Databricks",
    "Anthropic"
  ],
  "transcript": "Meeting Header:\nDate: 2025-02-11\nTime: 16:00 PST\nDuration: 40 minutes\nAttendees: Sophie Martinez (Redwood AE), Evan Liu (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Candidate), Leah Kim (Recruiter)\n\n[00:00] Sophie Martinez: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. This is Sophie from Redwood, Evan's with me. Priya, thanks for taking the time today. Can you hear us ok?\n[00:08] Priya Rao: Yes, I can hear you. Thanks for having me.\n[00:12] Evan Liu: Great, we'll start with a quick intro then jump to a short technical scenario. Sounds good?\n[00:16] Priya Rao: Sounds perfect.\n[00:20] Sophie Martinez: Cool. Priya, can you give a 2-3 minute background\u2014recent roles, what you've been shipping, and why you're interested in Redwood?\n[00:32] Priya Rao: Sure. I most recently was at InfraAnalytics where I was a senior solutions engineer supporting AI infra customers, mostly focused on model serving and cost optimizations. I worked a lot with GPU provisioning, autoscaling policies, and helping customers design fallback routing for multi-model setups. I'm excited about Redwood because of the focus on production-grade inference\u2014I've seen a lot of customers struggle with predictable latency and cost, so the product fit seems good for my background.\n[01:05] Evan Liu: When you say autoscaling policies, can you give an example\u2014like what metrics you tuned and tradeoffs you considered?\n[01:12] Priya Rao: We tuned on queue length and P95 latency for the endpoint. The tradeoff was throughput vs. cold-starts; we had to pick batch windows carefully so spikes didn't blow up latency, and we used a small warm pool to avoid tail latency for critical routes. Also we used quantized weights at night for cost savings on non-critical workloads.\n[01:38] Sophie Martinez: Nice, that aligns with what our Optimize team talks about. Quick question about customer conversations\u2014how did you surface reliability concerns without scaring customers about cost?\n[01:50] Priya Rao: I led with SLOs and a simple example: show them current costs and what latency looks like with and without aggressive batching. I often propose a two-stage rollout: first optimize for cost in staging, then pin to a more conservative config in prod and monitor.\n[02:10] Evan Liu: Ok, let's do a short troubleshooting scenario. Imagine a customer reports intermittent 5xxs from streaming API when traffic spikes. Walk me through your investigation and immediate mitigations.\n[02:22] Priya Rao: First I'd confirm the scope: is it a single model, region, or route? Check the gateway and per-route logs, look at KV cache hit rates, and check GPU memory pressure. Immediate mitigations: enable rate-limiting/queue throttling, fallback to a lower-capacity model variant, or divert non-critical traffic to a cached response. For long-term fix, tune batching thresholds and increase warm pool or adjust autoscaler cooldowns.\n[03:05] Evan Liu: In practice, when you say divert to cached response, what kind of cache policies did you use?\n[03:12] Priya Rao: Mostly prefix and user-session cache for deterministic flows, TTL-based for semistochastic outputs. We were careful with PII\u2014consistent with KMS policies\u2014so cache keys were hashed and encrypted.\n[03:30] Sophie Martinez: There's sometimes confusion between caching and reranking\u2014good answer. Follow-up: have you ever helped design a private deployment or VPC/on-prem setup?\n[03:40] Priya Rao: Yes, we ran a couple private deployments. Main issues were networking: TLS cert management, DNS, and ensuring audit logs to the customer's SIEM. For onboarding we provided runbooks for firewall rules and IAM roles.\n[03:58] Evan Liu: Any experience with HSM/KMS integrations?\n[04:02] Priya Rao: Yes, customers usually had a preferred KMS. We wrote examples for AWS KMS and a generic HSM handshake.\n[04:12] Leah Kim: Priya, quick note on timeline\u2014are you available for a take-home exercise this week?\n[04:18] Priya Rao: Yes, I am. I can take it and return within 48 hours.\n[04:22] Sophie Martinez: Great. Final part: do you have any questions for us?\n[04:26] Priya Rao: A couple. One, how do teams at Redwood balance latency SLOs vs. model cost when running mixed workloads? Two, what's the typical ramp for a new hire in SE?\n[04:36] Evan Liu: For the first\u2014it's a combination of RBAC-based routing and workload tagging; we use profiling to recommend quantization, autoscale settings, and sometimes model-variant routing. In product it's a lot of labelling routes by criticality and setting different batch windows.\n[04:52] Sophie Martinez: On ramp\u2014two weeks onboarding then shadowing calls for about a month; you pair with an AE/SE for the first quarter on new accounts.\n[05:00] Priya Rao: That sounds good.\n[05:03] Sophie Martinez: Ok we'll wrap. Leah, we'll send the take-home and schedule the panel. Priya, thanks again.\n[05:10] Leah Kim: Thanks, everyone.\n\n(Transcription notes: occasional overlap and filler words; some technical terms auto-corrected\u2014e.g., KV cache was sometimes transcribed as \"K-V cash\").",
  "dataset_noise_document": true,
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "summary",
    "transcript"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_2c9dcc3afa3249f39c725884e5be5c72"
}

    "title": "Edge switch ARP proxying leads to VPN client IP duplication and intermittent routing to wrong host",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/jira",
    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"INT-460811\",\n  \"project\": \"internal-support\",\n  \"issue_type\": \"Incident\",\n  \"summary\": \"Edge switch ARP proxying leads to VPN client IP duplication and intermittent routing to wrong host\",\n  \"status\": \"In Progress\",\n  \"priority\": \"P2\",\n  \"severity\": \"Sev2\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-03-10\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-03-14\",\n  \"reporter\": \"Aisha Malik\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Jonah Reed\",\n  \"components\": [\n    \"edge-network\",\n    \"vpn\",\n    \"dhcp\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"networking\",\n    \"arp-proxy\",\n    \"investigation\",\n    \"high-impact\"\n  ],\n  \"environment\": \"prod-us-west\",\n  \"linked_issues\": [\n    \"INT-424246\",\n    \"INT-542019\"\n  ],\n  \"description\": \"Issue summary: Several users reporting intermittent loss of access to internal services while connected to corporate VPN. Symptoms include duplicate IP conflict alerts on endpoints, frequent VPN re-auth events, and traffic appearing to be routed to a different on-prem host (service 10.23.5.12). Impact: ~8% of VPN sessions in us-west over the last 48h experienced short blackholes (30-90s) impacting git pushes, internal CI jobs, and ssh sessions. Scope: affects users on Wi-Fi SSID 'Redwood-Corp' behind specific edge switches in building SF2 rack 7.\",\n  \"steps_to_reproduce\": [\n    \"1) Connect laptop to 'Redwood-Corp' Wi-Fi in SF2 building (tested on macOS 13 and Ubuntu 22.04)\",\n    \"2) Establish VPN session to redwood-vpn-usw.redwood.net (WireGuard-based corporate VPN)\",\n    \"3) Trigger continuous ping to an internal host (ping -i 0.2 10.23.5.12)\",\n    \"4) Observe intermittent duplicate IP warnings on client and packets forwarded to an unexpected MAC on the L2 domain\",\n    \"5) Reproduce frequency increases when there is a short burst of multicast/mDNS traffic on the same AP's radio\"\n  ],\n  \"observed_logs_and_artifacts\": [\n    \"Client syslog excerpt: 'kernel: arp: IP address 10.23.8.45 claimed by 00:11:22:33:44:55 (conflict)'\",\n    \"Switch (edge-sw-7) log: 'proxy-arp conflict detected for 10.23.8.45, source 00:66:77:88:99:AA bridging-port 5'\",\n    \"Packet capture (pcap) snippet: ARP reply for 10.23.8.45 with two different source MACs within 120ms\",\n    \"VPN server metrics: client rekey count spike (client 10.23.8.45) correlated to timestamp 2026-03-12T14:12Z\",\n    \"Internal service (10.23.5.12) reported TCP reset spikes aligning with client blackholes\"\n  ],\n  \"investigation_notes\": [\n    \"Hypothesis 1: Edge switch proxy-arp configured for legacy NAT path is responding to ARP for VPN-assigned addresses from an overlapping DHCP pool, causing two active ARP entries on the LAN.\",\n    \"Hypothesis 2: A misconfigured VXLAN/bridge on edge-sw-7 is advertising ARP for the VPN subnet into the campus L2 segment when multicast bursts occur.\",\n    \"What we tried: - Disabled proxy-arp on edge-sw-7 port-channel to AP group temporarily (no immediate reduction). - Isolated a suspect AP by moving a test client to a different AP (blackhole persisted only when client served by AP-7A). - Captured pcap on AP, switch uplink, and VPN server concurrently for correlated timestamps (pcaps saved to /mnt/logs/INT-460811/pcaps/).\",\n    \"Preliminary find: ARP 'gratuitous' replies with VPN client IP are being injected by the switch's 'proxy-arp' feature only when the AP's multicast queue exceeds threshold. The switch returns ARP for the same IP with a different MAC that matches a spare management interface in rack 7 (00:66:77:88:99:AA).\"\n  ],\n  \"impact_summary\": \"Intermittent connectivity loss for internal developer workflows (git/ssh/CI). Approximately 8% of VPN sessions in the SF2 us-west site affected in the window; potential for data-transfer retries and CI flakiness. No customer-facing outage but notable developer productivity hit.\",\n  \"initial_triage_actions\": [\n    \"1) Placed affected edge switch (edge-sw-7) in monitoring schedule and enabled debug logging for proxy-arp events.\",\n    \"2) Temporarily increased DHCP lease affinity for VPN pool for clients in SF2 to reduce the window for IP reuse.\",\n    \"3) Asked campus networking team to disable 'proxy-arp' global feature on a staging switch and observe (ongoing).\",\n    \"4) Notified platform reliability and CI owners of potential re-run needs for impacted jobs (Slack #incidents and #platform-alerts).\"\n  ],\n  \"comments\": [\n    \"2026-03-11 09:18 - Jonah Reed: Assigned to network; will coordinate switch config changes and gather pcaps. Next action: schedule maintenance window if we need to push config rollback.\",\n    \"2026-03-12 15:25 - Priya Shah (campus-net): Reproduced proxy-arp responses on edge-sw-7 when AP multicast queue > 70%. Suspect firmware 1.2.3 on these switches has a known misc bridging bug. Opened ticket with vendor (TAC-889233).\",\n    \"2026-03-13 08:52 - Jonah Reed: Vendor TAC confirmed the switch may respond to ARP for non-local subnets under multicast overload in 1.2.3. Recommended immediate mitigation: set 'proxy-arp disable' on VRF for AP VLANs and upgrade firmware to 1.2.6.\",\n    \"2026-03-14 07:30 - Aisha Malik: Applied 'proxy-arp disable' to edge-sw-7 in staged maintenance window (07:00-07:15). Monitoring: VPN rekey spikes reduced from 47/hr to 2/hr for affected clients in the first 24h.\",\n    \"2026-03-14 10:02 - Jonah Reed: Confirming RFC and rollout plan for global fix. Proposed follow-up: firmware upgrade across SF2 rack 4-9, audit for proxy-arp enabled on other edge switches, and update config baseline to explicitly disable proxy-arp for VPN/DHCP subnets.\"\n  ],\n  \"root_cause\": \"Switch firmware (1.2.3) bug caused proxy-arp behavior under high multicast load leading to ARP advertisements for VPN-assigned addresses. This created ephemeral duplicate IP assignments on the L2 domain and caused VPN clients to experience routing blackholes and rekeys.\",\n  \"resolution_notes\": [\n    \"Mitigation applied: 'proxy-arp disable' set on edge-sw-7 AP VLANs during maintenance window 2026-03-14 07:00-07:15.\",\n    \"Temporary workaround: increased DHCP lease affinity and moved high-multicast APs to separate RF profile to reduce multicast bursts.\",\n    \"Permanent fix: planned firmware upgrade to 1.2.6 across SF2 edge switches (racks 4-9) and config baseline change to disable proxy-arp for VPN/DHCP subnets. Vendor TAC provided patch notes and recommended upgrade path.\",\n    \"Follow-ups: - Create change request CR-2026-0415 for firmware rollout. - Run campus-wide audit script to detect 'proxy-arp' enabled instances and remediate. - Add regression test to onboarding checklist for AP multicast stress.\",\n    \"Status: Partial fix applied and validated; full remediation scheduled (see CR-2026-0415).\"\n  ],\n  \"related_github_prs\": [\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-config/pull/411\"\n  ],\n  \"related_confluence_pages\": [\n    \"https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/NET/pages/Edge+Switch+Proxy-ARP+Runbook\"\n  ],\n  \"original_location\": \"jira/internal-support/INT-460811-edge-switch-arp-proxy-ip-duplication.json\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"summary\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"steps_to_reproduce\",\n    \"observed_logs_and_artifacts\",\n    \"investigation_notes\",\n    \"impact_summary\",\n    \"initial_triage_actions\",\n    \"comments\",\n    \"root_cause\",\n    \"resolution_notes\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_59cb294da8964683bb165a3bb615df71\"\n}",
