document.title: Edge switch ARP proxying leads to VPN client IP duplication and intermittent routing to wrong host
document.content:
{
  "key": "INT-460811",
  "project": "internal-support",
  "issue_type": "Incident",
  "summary": "Edge switch ARP proxying leads to VPN client IP duplication and intermittent routing to wrong host",
  "status": "In Progress",
  "priority": "P2",
  "severity": "Sev2",
  "created_at": "2026-03-10",
  "updated_at": "2026-03-14",
  "reporter": "Aisha Malik",
  "assignee": "Jonah Reed",
  "components": [
    "edge-network",
    "vpn",
    "dhcp"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "networking",
    "arp-proxy",
    "investigation",
    "high-impact"
  ],
  "environment": "prod-us-west",
  "linked_issues": [
    "INT-424246",
    "INT-542019"
  ],
  "description": "Issue summary: Several users reporting intermittent loss of access to internal services while connected to corporate VPN. Symptoms include duplicate IP conflict alerts on endpoints, frequent VPN re-auth events, and traffic appearing to be routed to a different on-prem host (service 10.23.5.12). Impact: ~8% of VPN sessions in us-west over the last 48h experienced short blackholes (30-90s) impacting git pushes, internal CI jobs, and ssh sessions. Scope: affects users on Wi-Fi SSID 'Redwood-Corp' behind specific edge switches in building SF2 rack 7.",
  "steps_to_reproduce": [
    "1) Connect laptop to 'Redwood-Corp' Wi-Fi in SF2 building (tested on macOS 13 and Ubuntu 22.04)",
    "2) Establish VPN session to redwood-vpn-usw.redwood.net (WireGuard-based corporate VPN)",
    "3) Trigger continuous ping to an internal host (ping -i 0.2 10.23.5.12)",
    "4) Observe intermittent duplicate IP warnings on client and packets forwarded to an unexpected MAC on the L2 domain",
    "5) Reproduce frequency increases when there is a short burst of multicast/mDNS traffic on the same AP's radio"
  ],
  "observed_logs_and_artifacts": [
    "Client syslog excerpt: 'kernel: arp: IP address 10.23.8.45 claimed by 00:11:22:33:44:55 (conflict)'",
    "Switch (edge-sw-7) log: 'proxy-arp conflict detected for 10.23.8.45, source 00:66:77:88:99:AA bridging-port 5'",
    "Packet capture (pcap) snippet: ARP reply for 10.23.8.45 with two different source MACs within 120ms",
    "VPN server metrics: client rekey count spike (client 10.23.8.45) correlated to timestamp 2026-03-12T14:12Z",
    "Internal service (10.23.5.12) reported TCP reset spikes aligning with client blackholes"
  ],
  "investigation_notes": [
    "Hypothesis 1: Edge switch proxy-arp configured for legacy NAT path is responding to ARP for VPN-assigned addresses from an overlapping DHCP pool, causing two active ARP entries on the LAN.",
    "Hypothesis 2: A misconfigured VXLAN/bridge on edge-sw-7 is advertising ARP for the VPN subnet into the campus L2 segment when multicast bursts occur.",
    "What we tried: - Disabled proxy-arp on edge-sw-7 port-channel to AP group temporarily (no immediate reduction). - Isolated a suspect AP by moving a test client to a different AP (blackhole persisted only when client served by AP-7A). - Captured pcap on AP, switch uplink, and VPN server concurrently for correlated timestamps (pcaps saved to /mnt/logs/INT-460811/pcaps/).",
    "Preliminary find: ARP 'gratuitous' replies with VPN client IP are being injected by the switch's 'proxy-arp' feature only when the AP's multicast queue exceeds threshold. The switch returns ARP for the same IP with a different MAC that matches a spare management interface in rack 7 (00:66:77:88:99:AA)."
  ],
  "impact_summary": "Intermittent connectivity loss for internal developer workflows (git/ssh/CI). Approximately 8% of VPN sessions in the SF2 us-west site affected in the window; potential for data-transfer retries and CI flakiness. No customer-facing outage but notable developer productivity hit.",
  "initial_triage_actions": [
    "1) Placed affected edge switch (edge-sw-7) in monitoring schedule and enabled debug logging for proxy-arp events.",
    "2) Temporarily increased DHCP lease affinity for VPN pool for clients in SF2 to reduce the window for IP reuse.",
    "3) Asked campus networking team to disable 'proxy-arp' global feature on a staging switch and observe (ongoing).",
    "4) Notified platform reliability and CI owners of potential re-run needs for impacted jobs (Slack #incidents and #platform-alerts)."
  ],
  "comments": [
    "2026-03-11 09:18 - Jonah Reed: Assigned to network; will coordinate switch config changes and gather pcaps. Next action: schedule maintenance window if we need to push config rollback.",
    "2026-03-12 15:25 - Priya Shah (campus-net): Reproduced proxy-arp responses on edge-sw-7 when AP multicast queue > 70%. Suspect firmware 1.2.3 on these switches has a known misc bridging bug. Opened ticket with vendor (TAC-889233).",
    "2026-03-13 08:52 - Jonah Reed: Vendor TAC confirmed the switch may respond to ARP for non-local subnets under multicast overload in 1.2.3. Recommended immediate mitigation: set 'proxy-arp disable' on VRF for AP VLANs and upgrade firmware to 1.2.6.",
    "2026-03-14 07:30 - Aisha Malik: Applied 'proxy-arp disable' to edge-sw-7 in staged maintenance window (07:00-07:15). Monitoring: VPN rekey spikes reduced from 47/hr to 2/hr for affected clients in the first 24h.",
    "2026-03-14 10:02 - Jonah Reed: Confirming RFC and rollout plan for global fix. Proposed follow-up: firmware upgrade across SF2 rack 4-9, audit for proxy-arp enabled on other edge switches, and update config baseline to explicitly disable proxy-arp for VPN/DHCP subnets."
  ],
  "root_cause": "Switch firmware (1.2.3) bug caused proxy-arp behavior under high multicast load leading to ARP advertisements for VPN-assigned addresses. This created ephemeral duplicate IP assignments on the L2 domain and caused VPN clients to experience routing blackholes and rekeys.",
  "resolution_notes": [
    "Mitigation applied: 'proxy-arp disable' set on edge-sw-7 AP VLANs during maintenance window 2026-03-14 07:00-07:15.",
    "Temporary workaround: increased DHCP lease affinity and moved high-multicast APs to separate RF profile to reduce multicast bursts.",
    "Permanent fix: planned firmware upgrade to 1.2.6 across SF2 edge switches (racks 4-9) and config baseline change to disable proxy-arp for VPN/DHCP subnets. Vendor TAC provided patch notes and recommended upgrade path.",
    "Follow-ups: - Create change request CR-2026-0415 for firmware rollout. - Run campus-wide audit script to detect 'proxy-arp' enabled instances and remediate. - Add regression test to onboarding checklist for AP multicast stress.",
    "Status: Partial fix applied and validated; full remediation scheduled (see CR-2026-0415)."
  ],
  "related_github_prs": [
    "https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-config/pull/411"
  ],
  "related_confluence_pages": [
    "https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/NET/pages/Edge+Switch+Proxy-ARP+Runbook"
  ],

What should the exact tag message and procedures be?\\n\\njake: Tag message: \\\"Release v1.14.0 \\u2014 runtime + CLI: perf improvements, bugfixes, changelog entries\\\". Steps I recommend:\\n\\n```\\n# ensure branch is up to date\\ngit checkout release/v1.14\\ngit pull --ff-only origin release/v1.14\\n\\n# create an annotated tag\\ngit tag -a v1.14.0 -m \\\"Release v1.14.0 \\u2014 runtime + CLI: perf improvements, bugfixes\\\"\\n\\n# (optional) GPG-sign the tag locally\\ngit tag -s v1.14.0 -m \\\"Release v1.14.0\\\"\\n\\n# push the tag to origin\\ngit push origin v1.14.0\\n```\\n\\nThen create a GitHub draft release (gh CLI):\\n```\\n# create draft with changelog as notes\\ngh release create v1.14.0 dist/* --notes-file CHANGELOG.md --draft\\n```\\n\\nArtifact steps (build pipeline has produced dist/*):\\n```\\n# checksums\\nshasum -a 256 dist/* > checksums.txt\\n# upload artifacts to S3\\naws s3 cp dist/ s3://redwood-release-bucket/v1.14.0/ --recursive\\naws s3 cp checksums.txt s3://redwood-release-bucket/v1.14.0/\\n```\\n\\npraveen: Quick security notes: confirm the GPG key you use is the same key uploaded in your GitHub account (Settings -> SSH and GPG keys). We require a signed annotated tag for this release. Also add a manifest.json alongside checksums.txt with SHA256 hashes so downstream teams can verify.\\n\\njake: Example minimal manifest schema (we'll add full file in the release assets):\\n```\\n{\\n  \\\"version\\\": \\\"v1.14.0\\\",\\n  \\\"files\\\": [\\n    {\\\"name\\\": \\\"redwood-runtime-linux.tar.gz\\\", \\\"sha256\\\": \\\"<hex>\\\"},\\n    {\\\"name\\\": \\\"redwood-cli-mac.tar.gz\\\", \\\"sha256\\\": \\\"<hex>\\\"}\\n  ]\\n}\\n```\\n\\nops-qa: Can we do a quick smoke run after the draft exists but before publishing? {
  "channel": "eng-releases",
  "thread_ts": "1729999999",
  "first_message_ts": "1729999999",
  "last_message_ts": "1730000450",
  "participants": [
    "jake",
    "mina",
    "praveen",
    "ops-qa",
    "release-bot"
  ],
  "messages": "jake: Quick pre-release check — planning to publish v1.14.0 tomorrow morning (UTC). Need someone to push an annotated+signed tag, create a GitHub draft release, and confirm artifacts + checksums are uploaded. Leaving a short checklist below.

mina: I can take the tag + create the draft. What should the exact tag message and procedures be?

jake: Tag message: "Release v1.14.0 — runtime + CLI: perf improvements, bugfixes, changelog entries". Steps I recommend:

```
# ensure branch is up to date
git checkout release/v1.14
git pull --ff-only origin release/v1.14

# create an annotated tag
git tag -a v1.14.0 -m "Release v1.14.0 — runtime + CLI: perf improvements, bugfixes"

# (optional) GPG-sign the tag locally
git tag -s v1.14.0 -m "Release v1.14.0"

# push the tag to origin
git push origin v1.14.0
```

Then create a GitHub draft release (gh CLI):
```
# create draft with changelog as notes
gh release create v1.14.0 dist/* --notes-file CHANGELOG.md --draft
```

Artifact steps (build pipeline has produced dist/*):
```
# checksums
shasum -a 256 dist/* > checksums.txt
# upload artifacts to S3
aws s3 cp dist/ s3://redwood-release-bucket/v1.14.0/ --recursive
aws s3 cp checksums.txt s3://redwood-release-bucket/v1.14.0/
```

praveen: Quick security notes: confirm the GPG key you use is the same key uploaded in your GitHub account (Settings -> SSH and GPG keys). We require a signed annotated tag for this release. Also add a manifest.json alongside checksums.txt with SHA256 hashes so downstream teams can verify.

jake: Example minimal manifest schema (we'll add full file in the release assets):
```
{
  "version": "v1.14.0",
  "files": [
    {"name": "redwood-runtime-linux.tar.gz", "sha256": "<hex>"},
    {"name": "redwood-cli-mac.tar.gz", "sha256": "<hex>"}
  ]
}
```

ops-qa: Can we do a quick smoke run after the draft exists but before publishing? I'll run a basic generate+embed test against staging and report back. :eyes:

mina: Plan: I'll push the signed tag and create the draft at 09:00 UTC, then ping here with links. Who will upload the artifacts?

jake: I'll handle artifact upload and checksum generation once the tag is present.

release-bot: Automated reminder: please ensure checksums.txt and manifest.json are included in the draft assets.

mina: Tag pushed and draft created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/releases/tag/v1.14.0 :rocket: (draft link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/releases/edit/??)

jake: Uploading artifacts to S3 now and attaching checksums+manifest to the draft.

jake: Done — artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-release-bucket/v1.14.0/ and checksums.txt + manifest.json attached to draft. Verified local checksums match S3.

ops-qa: Smoke run results: basic generation, embeddings, and regression tests passed on staging (no obvious regressions).

praveen: Verified GPG signature on tag and validated manifest/checksums. Security LGTM.

mina: If no objections, I'll publish the release at 09:20 UTC. Any last-minute blockers?

jake: No blockers from infra side — approving publish. :tada:

release-bot: Publishing scheduled by mina at 09:20 UTC.

mina: Published. Release URL: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/releases/tag/v1.14.0 — changelog and assets are attached. Congrats team! :confetti_ball:",

    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"PM-24680\",\n  \"team\": \"product-management\",\n  \"title\": \"Cohort Comparator & Trace Linker for Deployment Health\",\n  \"status\": \"In Progress\",\n  \"priority\": \"P1\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-03-10\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-03-14\",\n  \"creator\": \"Aisha Kapoor\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Marco Lin\",\n  \"project\": \"Console Rollouts\",\n  \"cycle\": \"2026-W10\",\n  \"estimate\": \"8\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2026-04-01\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"rollouts\",\n    \"observability\",\n    \"console\",\n    \"canary\",\n    \"a/b\",\n    \"auto-rollback\",\n    \"tracing\"\n  ],\n  \"parent_issue\": [\n    \"PM-14091\"\n  ],\n  \"dependencies\": [\n    \"ENG-20345\",\n    \"ENG-20412\",\n    \"DES-317\"\n  ],\n  \"customer_impact\": \"high\",\n  \"release\": \"console-2026.03\",\n  \"security_review_required\": \"false\",\n  \"description\": \"Build a combined Cohort Comparator and Request Trace Linker inside the Console to make canary/A-B/shadow rollouts diagnosable end-to-end. The feature surfaces per-route metric diffs between cohorts, links anomalous metric deltas to sampled request traces, and exposes suggested rollback signals (automated and manual) backed by thresholded telemetry. This is intended to reduce MTTI for rollout regressions and make auto-rollback decisions transparent to product and platform teams.\",\n  \"acceptance_criteria\": [\n    \"Comparator UI shows side-by-side cohort-level charts for latency (p50/p95), error rate, token cost, and request throughput for a selected time window\",\n    \"Diff view highlights statistically significant deltas and annotates percentage change with confidence intervals\",\n    \"User can click a diff to see sampled traces from both cohorts with request-level metadata (route, model version, routing policy, input hash)\",\n    \"Trace Linker pins causal spans and shows top 3 signal contributors (e.g., model variant, batch size, region) derived from instrumentation\",\n    \"Auto-rollback triggers are visible per-rollout and can be toggled; Console records the reason and suggested fallback model\",\n    \"All telemetry queries are reproducible (copyable query) and dashboards exportable as PNG/CSV\",\n    \"Feature is behind a Console feature flag and gated to Dedicated/Hosted customers in beta\"\n  ],\n  \"tasks\": [\n    \"Product: finalize comparator UX flows and error states (mockups)\",\n    \"Design: high-fidelity mockups for comparator panel, trace overlay, and diff heatmap\",\n    \"Engineering: instrument cohort labels in request pipeline and add trace sampling hook for cohort comparison\",\n    \"Engineering: build backend telemetry aggregator service to compute per-route deltas and significance tests\",\n    \"Engineering: expose API endpoints for cohort queries and trace joins\",\n    \"SRE: validate query performance and set retention defaults for cohort metrics\",\n    \"QA: e2e tests for trace linking across canary/A-B/shadow traffic scenarios\",\n    \"Docs: write Console help guide and rollout observability playbook\"\n  ],\n  \"design_assets\": [\n    \"https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/Cohort-Comparator-Prototype\",\n    \"https://drive.redwood/internal/Console/Mockups/cohort-comparator-v2.pdf\"\n  ],\n  \"telemetry_queries\": [\n    \"PromQL: rate(http_server_requests_total{route=~\\\"/v1/generate.*\\\"}[5m]) by (cohort)\",\n    \"PromQL: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, cohort))\",\n    \"SQL (clickhouse): select cohort, quantileExact(0.95, duration_ms) from requests where route='/v1/chat' and ts >= now()-interval 1 hour group by cohort\"\n  ],\n  \"rollout_plan\": [\n    \"Alpha: enable feature flag for internal Redwood tenants only (1 week)\",\n    \"Beta: open to selected customers on Dedicated and Hosted with opt-in (4 weeks)\",\n    \"GA: enabled by default for all Console users with feature rollout controls (post-beta)\"\n  ],\n  \"risks\": [\n    \"High cardinality of route/model/version labels could make diff computations slow\",\n    \"Trace sampling bias between cohorts may create false-positive causes\",\n    \"Auto-rollback without clear human-readable rationale could erode trust\",\n    \"Data retention costs if coarse-grained sampling is insufficient for forensic analysis\"\n  ],\n  \"tradeoffs\": [\n    \"Aggressive trace sampling increases root-cause fidelity but raises cost \\u2014 start with adaptive sampling tied to metric deltas\",\n    \"Pre-computing cohort diffs reduces UI latency but increases storage/compute; prefer on-demand with short cache window initially\",\n    \"Expose simple auto-rollback toggles first; defer fully automated ML-driven rollback recommendations to later cycle\"\n  ],\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Nina Rodriguez (Security)\",\n    \"Omar Patel (SRE)\",\n    \"Leah Chen (Design)\",\n    \"Devon Morris (Engineering lead)\"\n  ],\n  \"notes\": [\n    \"PM/Design sync 2026-03-11: prioritize clear reasoning cards next to each suggested rollback action\",\n    \"Prototype session 2026-03-12: product asked for side-by-side trace waterfall comparison; design to iterate\",\n    \"Engineering spike 2026-03-13 showed ClickHouse aggregation of cohort diffs at 5m windows is 3x cheaper than per-request joins\"\n  ],\n  \"comments\": [\n    \"2026-03-10 Aisha Kapoor: Created ticket \\u2014 goal is to reduce MTTI for rollout regressions by surface-level correlation -> request-level evidence.\",\n    \"2026-03-11 Marco Lin: Spun up spike; backend will reuse existing metrics pipeline but needs a lightweight join index for cohort -> trace linking (ENG-20345)\",\n    \"2026-03-12 Leah Chen: Uploaded first mockups; recommended adding a confidence ribbon to diff charts to indicate statistical significance\",\n    \"2026-03-13 Omar Patel: SRE flagged potential retention cost issue; recommending adaptive sampling and a 14-day lookback default\",\n    \"2026-03-14 Marco Lin: Marked 'in progress' \\u2014 backend API contract drafted and PR linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4128\"\n  ],\n  \"attachments\": [\n       "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Cohort Comparator & Trace Linker for Deployment Health\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/product-management/PM-24680-cohort-comparator-and-trace-linker-for-deployment-health.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: product-management\nProject: Console Rollouts\nTeam: product-management\n\n- comparator ui shows side - by - side cohort - level charts for latency ( p50 / p95 ), error rate, token cost, and request throughput for a selected time window - diff view highlights statistically significant deltas and annotates percentage change with confidence intervals - user can click a diff to see sampled traces from both cohorts with request - level metadata ( route, model version, routing policy, input hash ) - trace linker pins causal spans and shows top 3 signal contributors ( e. g., model variant, batch size, region ) derived from instrumentation - auto - rollback triggers are visible per - rollout and can be toggled ; console records the reason and suggested fallback model - all",

    "a/b",
    "auto-rollback",
    "tracing"
  ],
  "parent_issue": [
    "PM-14091"
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    "ENG-20345",
    "ENG-20412",
    "DES-317"
  ],
  "customer_impact": "high",
  "release": "console-2026.03",
  "security_review_required": "false",
  "description": "Build a combined Cohort Comparator and Request Trace Linker inside the Console to make canary/A-B/shadow rollouts diagnosable end-to-end. The feature surfaces per-route metric diffs between cohorts, links anomalous metric deltas to sampled request traces, and exposes suggested rollback signals (automated and manual) backed by thresholded telemetry. This is intended to reduce MTTI for rollout regressions and make auto-rollback decisions transparent to product and platform teams.",
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    "Comparator UI shows side-by-side cohort-level charts for latency (p50/p95), error rate, token cost, and request throughput for a selected time window",
    "Diff view highlights statistically significant deltas and annotates percentage change with confidence intervals",
    "User can click a diff to see sampled traces from both cohorts with request-level metadata (route, model version, routing policy, input hash)",
    "Trace Linker pins causal spans and shows top 3 signal contributors (e.g., model variant, batch size, region) derived from instrumentation",
    "Auto-rollback triggers are visible per-rollout and can be toggled; Console records the reason and suggested fallback model",
    "All telemetry queries are reproducible (copyable query) and dashboards exportable as PNG/CSV",
    "Feature is behind a Console feature flag and gated to Dedicated/Hosted customers in beta"
  ],
  "tasks": [
    "Product: finalize comparator UX flows and error states (mockups)",
    "Design: high-fidelity mockups for comparator panel, trace overlay, and diff heatmap",
    "Engineering: instrument cohort labels in request pipeline and add trace sampling hook for cohort comparison",
    "Engineering: build backend telemetry aggregator service to compute per-route deltas and significance tests",
    "Engineering: expose API endpoints for cohort queries and trace joins",
    "SRE: validate query performance and set retention defaults for cohort metrics",
    "QA: e2e tests for trace linking across canary/A-B/shadow traffic scenarios",
    "Docs: write Console help guide and rollout observability playbook"
  ],
  "design_assets": [
    "https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/Cohort-Comparator-Prototype",
    "https://drive.redwood/internal/Console/Mockups/cohort-comparator-v2.pdf"
  ],
  "telemetry_queries": [
    "PromQL: rate(http_server_requests_total{route=~\"/v1/generate.*\"}[5m]) by (cohort)",
    "PromQL: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, cohort))",
    "SQL (clickhouse): select cohort, quantileExact(0.95, duration_ms) from requests where route='/v1/chat' and ts >= now()-interval 1 hour group by cohort"
  ],
  "rollout_plan": [
    "Alpha: enable feature flag for internal Redwood tenants only (1 week)",
    "Beta: open to selected customers on Dedicated and Hosted with opt-in (4 weeks)",
    "GA: enabled by default for all Console users with feature rollout controls (post-beta)"
  ],
  "risks": [
    "High cardinality of route/model/version labels could make diff computations slow",
    "Trace sampling bias between cohorts may create false-positive causes",
    "Auto-rollback without clear human-readable rationale could erode trust",
    "Data retention costs if coarse-grained sampling is insufficient for forensic analysis"
  ],
  "tradeoffs": [
    "Aggressive trace sampling increases root-cause fidelity but raises cost \u2014 start with adaptive sampling tied to metric deltas",
    "Pre-computing cohort diffs reduces UI latency but increases storage/compute; prefer on-demand with short cache window initially",
    "Expose simple auto-rollback toggles first; defer fully automated ML-driven rollback recommendations to later cycle"
  ],
  "reviewers": [
    "Nina Rodriguez (Security)",
    "Omar Patel (SRE)",
    "Leah Chen (Design)",
    "Devon Morris (Engineering lead)"
  ],
  "notes": [
    "PM/Design sync 2026-03-11: prioritize clear reasoning cards next to each suggested rollback action",
    "Prototype session 2026-03-12: product asked for side-by-side trace waterfall comparison; design to iterate",
    "Engineering spike 2026-03-13 showed ClickHouse aggregation of cohort diffs at 5m windows is 3x cheaper than per-request joins"
  ],
  "comments": [
    "2026-03-10 Aisha Kapoor: Created ticket \u2014 goal is to reduce MTTI for rollout regressions by surface-level correlation -> request-level evidence.",
    "2026-03-11 Marco Lin: Spun up spike; backend will reuse existing metrics pipeline but needs a lightweight join index for cohort -> trace linking (ENG-20345)",
    "2026-03-12 Leah Chen: Uploaded first mockups; recommended adding a confidence ribbon to diff charts to indicate statistical significance",
    "2026-03-13 Omar Patel: SRE flagged potential retention cost issue; recommending adaptive sampling and a 14-day lookback default",
    "2026-03-14 Marco Lin: Marked 'in progress' \u2014 backend API contract drafted and PR linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4128"
  ],

  ],

    "title": "Fn schema mapper and streaming handshake for cross-SDK invocation",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/linear",
    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"ENG-77120\",\n  \"team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"title\": \"Fn schema mapper and streaming handshake for cross-SDK invocation\",\n  \"status\": \"In Progress\",\n  \"priority\": \"P1\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-02-18\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2025-03-05\",\n  \"creator\": \"Marcus Li\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Elena Rodriguez\",\n  \"project\": \"sdk-function-calls\",\n  \"cycle\": \"2025-W09\",\n  \"estimate\": \"5\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2025-03-14\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"sdk\",\n    \"function-calling\",\n    \"cross-language\",\n    \"streaming\",\n    \"retry\",\n    \"telemetry\"\n  ],\n  \"dependencies\": [\n    \"ENG-61452\",\n    \"ENG-74290\"\n  ],\n  \"customer_impact\": \"medium\",\n  \"release\": \"sdk-2025.03\",\n  \"security_review_required\": \"false\",\n  \"description\": \"Implement a lightweight, portable function-schema mapper and streaming handshake layer used by Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. The mapper will normalize model-declared function schemas into SDK-native typed descriptors, provide coercion and graceful-degradation rules, and expose invocation helpers that handle idempotency tokens, adaptive retry/backoff for non-streamed and streamed calls, and a streaming handshake that enables resume/fallthrough semantics when partial responses arrive or a connection drops.\",\n  \"acceptance_criteria\": [\n    \"SDKs (py/ts/go) include a shared schema mapper that converts model function definitions into native call signatures and JSON validators\",\n    \"Invocation helpers expose a consistent call surface across languages, including: call(), stream_call(), call_with_idempotency(), and fallback_to_text()\",\n    \"Retry/backoff policy supports at-least-once vs exactly-once semantics toggles, with telemetry events emitted for retry attempts and fallback triggers\",\n    \"Streaming handshake protocol enables resume from KV-prefix if server supports resume tokens; otherwise client falls back to graceful abort and server-side best-effort completion\",\n    \"Comprehensive unit and integration tests cover schema coercion, optional argument handling, enum coercion, nested objects, and streaming resume scenarios\",\n    \"Documentation pages and three example apps (py/ts/go) demonstrating function call patterns and recommended safety knobs\"\n  ],\n  \"design_notes\": [\n    \"Keep mapper small: generate validator code at package build-time where feasible, fall back to runtime checks for dynamic models\",\n    \"Prefer permissive coercion by default (string->enum, numeric strings->numbers) but surface a strict mode for enterprise users needing deterministic validation\",\n    \"Streaming handshake: introduce a small four-step exchange (CLIENT_HELLO -> SERVER_ACK(with resume_token?) -> CLIENT_STREAM_START -> KEEPALIVE frames). If SERVER_ACK includes no resume token, client must checkpoint locally and allow idempotent retry only for non-side-effecting tools\",\n    \"Idempotency token strategy: allow user-provided token or generate RFC4122 v4 by default; include an optional idempotency window header so routers can garbage-collect tokens early\",\n    \"Telemetry: emit events for schema_mismatch, coercion_event, retry_attempt, retry_abort_reason, stream_resume_success, stream_resume_failure\",\n    \"Trade-offs: full schema strictness reduces user errors but increases friction for rapid prototyping. Default to permissive but log and surface mismatches via console warnings and SDK diagnostics API\"\n  ],\n  \"implementation_plan\": [\n    \"Week 1: Implement core schema mapper library in a neutral TypeScript reference package with a minimal runtime validator interface\",\n    \"Week 2: Port mapper to Python and Go wrappers, add generator to produce thin language bindings (type stubs for py, d.ts for ts, go structs)\",\n    \"Week 3: Implement streaming handshake protocol and client-side resume logic; add resume_token plumbing to server contract (spec PR)\",\n    \"Week 4: Add invocation helpers with retry policies and idempotency token handling; expose policy knobs via client config\",\n    \"Week 5: Tests, examples, docs, and API reviews. Prepare SDK release artifacts and coordinate with Console/Runtime teams for telemetry keys and server-side resume support\"\n  ],\n  \"test_plan\": [\n    \"Unit: validator coercion matrix for primitives, enums, nested objects and arrays\",\n    \"Integration: end-to-end example calling a toy function (echo, counter) in all three SDKs verifying idempotency behavior\",\n    \"Chaos: simulate dropped connections during streaming and assert resume/fallback semantics and no double-execution where exact-once is requested\",\n    \"Performance: measure additional latency/cpu of runtime validation under high QPS and validate generator reduces runtime overhead\",\n    \"Security: fuzz malformed schemas and inputs to ensure validators fail closed when strict mode is enabled\"\n  ],\n  \"rollout_plan\": [\n    \"Alpha: release TypeScript reference package and experimental Python wrapper to internal SDK alpha channel; invite 3 beta customers to opt-in\",\n    \"Beta: widen to public SDK releases behind feature flag (enable_schema_mapper=true) and collect telemetry for coercion events\",\n    \"GA: enable by default with documentation and migration guide. Coordinate with runtime team to stop accepting legacy unstructured tool formats once 90% of clients migrated or after 3 months\",\n    \"Backward compatibility: provide an adapter that maps old 'tools' flat payload to new function schema descriptors for 6 months\"\n  ],\n  \"references\": [\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/3214\",\n    \"https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Function+Call+Schema+Platform+Spec\",\n    \"https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk/function-calling#streaming-handshake\",\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/412\"\n  ],\n  \"comments\": [\n    \"2025-02-18 Marcus Li: Initial write-up and scope. Decided to standardize on permissive coercion by default and expose strict mode.\",\n    \"2025-02-22 Elena Rodriguez: Added streaming handshake design. Concern: server needs resume_token support \\u2014 opened runtime issue #412\",\n    \"2025-02-26 Backend review (Raj Patel): Suggested adding idempotency_window header and clarified router GC implications. Marked as resolved in design notes.\",\n    \"2025-03-01 PR feedback (Sara Nguyen): Requested clearer examples for exactly-once vs at-least-once and a sample using external DB side effects. Assigned follow-up test task.\",\n    \"2025-03-05 Elena Rodriguez: Merged TS reference + Python wrappers into internal alpha branch. Triggered internal validation job; performance within budget on p3-standard test harness\"\n  ],\n  \"linked_pr\": [\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/3214\",\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/89\"\n  ],\n  \"artifacts\": [\n    \"design/fn-schema-mapper-v1.md\",\n    \"examples/py/function_call_echo.py\",\n    \"examples/ts/function_call_streaming.ts\",\n    \"examples/go/function_call_idempotent.go\",\n    \"benchmarks/schema-validator-overhead.csv\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"acceptance_criteria\",\n    \"design_notes\",\n    \"implementation_plan\",\n    \"test_plan\",\n    \"rollout_plan\",\n    \"comments\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_169dca195c96410b80ff166803a50512\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Fn schema mapper and streaming handshake for cross-SDK invocation\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-77120-fn-schema-mapper-compatibility-and-streaming-handshake.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: sdk-function-calls\nTeam: engineering\n\n- eng - 74290 customer impact : medium release : sdk - 2025. 03 security review required : false description : implement a lightweight, portable function - schema mapper and streaming handshake layer used by python / typescript / go sdks. the mapper will normalize model - declared function schemas into sdk - native typed descriptors, provide coercion and graceful - degradation rules, and expose invocation helpers that handle idempotency tokens, adaptive retry / backoff for non - streamed and streamed calls, and a streaming handshake that enables resume / fallthrough semantics when partial responses arrive or a connection drops. # # acceptance criteria",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Fn schema mapper and streaming handshake for cross-SDK invocation\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-77120-fn-schema-mapper-compatibility-and-streaming-handshake.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: sdk-function-calls\nTeam: engineering\n\n- keep mapper small : generate validator code at package build - time where feasible, fall back to runtime checks for dynamic models - prefer permissive coercion by default ( string - > enum, numeric strings - > numbers ) but surface a strict mode for enterprise users needing deterministic validation - streaming handshake : introduce a small four - step exchange ( client _ hello - > server _ ack ( with resume _ token? ) - > client _ stream _ start - > keepalive frames ). if server _ ack includes no resume token, client must checkpoint locally and allow idempotent retry only for non - side - effecting tools - idempotency token strategy : allow user - provided token",

{
  "key": "ENG-77120",
  "team": "engineering",
  "title": "Fn schema mapper and streaming handshake for cross-SDK invocation",
  "status": "In Progress",
  "priority": "P1",
  "created_at": "2025-02-18",
  "updated_at": "2025-03-05",
  "creator": "Marcus Li",
  "assignee": "Elena Rodriguez",
  "project": "sdk-function-calls",
  "cycle": "2025-W09",
  "estimate": "5",
  "due_date": "2025-03-14",
  "labels": [
    "sdk",
    "function-calling",
    "cross-language",
    "streaming",
    "retry",
    "telemetry"
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    "ENG-61452",
    "ENG-74290"
  ],
  "customer_impact": "medium",
  "release": "sdk-2025.03",
  "security_review_required": "false",
  "description": "Implement a lightweight, portable function-schema mapper and streaming handshake layer used by Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. The mapper will normalize model-declared function schemas into SDK-native typed descriptors, provide coercion and graceful-degradation rules, and expose invocation helpers that handle idempotency tokens, adaptive retry/backoff for non-streamed and streamed calls, and a streaming handshake that enables resume/fallthrough semantics when partial responses arrive or a connection drops.",
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    "SDKs (py/ts/go) include a shared schema mapper that converts model function definitions into native call signatures and JSON validators",
    "Invocation helpers expose a consistent call surface across languages, including: call(), stream_call(), call_with_idempotency(), and fallback_to_text()",
    "Retry/backoff policy supports at-least-once vs exactly-once semantics toggles, with telemetry events emitted for retry attempts and fallback triggers",
    "Streaming handshake protocol enables resume from KV-prefix if server supports resume tokens; otherwise client falls back to graceful abort and server-side best-effort completion",
    "Comprehensive unit and integration tests cover schema coercion, optional argument handling, enum coercion, nested objects, and streaming resume scenarios",
    "Documentation pages and three example apps (py/ts/go) demonstrating function call patterns and recommended safety knobs"
  ],
  "design_notes": [
    "Keep mapper small: generate validator code at package build-time where feasible, fall back to runtime checks for dynamic models",
    "Prefer permissive coercion by default (string->enum, numeric strings->numbers) but surface a strict mode for enterprise users needing deterministic validation",
    "Streaming handshake: introduce a small four-step exchange (CLIENT_HELLO -> SERVER_ACK(with resume_token?) -> CLIENT_STREAM_START -> KEEPALIVE frames). If SERVER_ACK includes no resume token, client must checkpoint locally and allow idempotent retry only for non-side-effecting tools",
    "Idempotency token strategy: allow user-provided token or generate RFC4122 v4 by default; include an optional idempotency window header so routers can garbage-collect tokens early",
    "Telemetry: emit events for schema_mismatch, coercion_event, retry_attempt, retry_abort_reason, stream_resume_success, stream_resume_failure",
    "Trade-offs: full schema strictness reduces user errors but increases friction for rapid prototyping. Default to permissive but log and surface mismatches via console warnings and SDK diagnostics API"
  ],
  "implementation_plan": [
    "Week 1: Implement core schema mapper library in a neutral TypeScript reference package with a minimal runtime validator interface",
    "Week 2: Port mapper to Python and Go wrappers, add generator to produce thin language bindings (type stubs for py, d.ts for ts, go structs)",
    "Week 3: Implement streaming handshake protocol and client-side resume logic; add resume_token plumbing to server contract (spec PR)",
    "Week 4: Add invocation helpers with retry policies and idempotency token handling; expose policy knobs via client config",
    "Week 5: Tests, examples, docs, and API reviews. Prepare SDK release artifacts and coordinate with Console/Runtime teams for telemetry keys and server-side resume support"
  ],
  "test_plan": [
    "Unit: validator coercion matrix for primitives, enums, nested objects and arrays",
    "Integration: end-to-end example calling a toy function (echo, counter) in all three SDKs verifying idempotency behavior",
    "Chaos: simulate dropped connections during streaming and assert resume/fallback semantics and no double-execution where exact-once is requested",
    "Performance: measure additional latency/cpu of runtime validation under high QPS and validate generator reduces runtime overhead",
    "Security: fuzz malformed schemas and inputs to ensure validators fail closed when strict mode is enabled"
  ],
  "rollout_plan": [

    "GA: enable by default with documentation and migration guide. Coordinate with runtime team to stop accepting legacy unstructured tool formats once 90% of clients migrated or after 3 months",

  ],

{
  "company_id": "LR-0472",
  "company_name": "LanternRidge SaaS Analytics",
  "company_domain": "lanternridge.ai",
  "stage": "evaluation",
  "owner": "Jordan Reyes",
  "created_at": "2024-09-18",
  "updated_at": "2024-11-06",
  "account_tier": "mid_market",
  "industry": "analytics-saas",
  "employee_count_range": "201-1000",
  "hq_region": "na",
  "interested_products": [
    "hosted_api",
    "dedicated"
  ],
  "use_cases": [
    "support-agent",
    "document-search",
    "reranking",
    "summary-generation"
  ],
  "deployment_requirements": [
    "vpc"
  ],
  "security_requirements": [
    "sso_saml",
    "soc2",
    "audit_logging",
    "kms",
    "data_residency"
  ],
  "competitors": [
    "openai",
    "anthropic"
  ],
  "forecast_close_month": "2025-01",
  "estimated_arr_range": "$120k-$250k",
  "se_assigned": "Priya Nandakumar",
  "csm_assigned": "Ethan Cole",
  "last_activity_at": "2024-11-06",
  "next_step": "internal capacity sign-off + pricing review scheduled with finance 2024-11-13",
  "blockers": [
    "cost model alignment",
    "legal review on data residency",
    "throughput SLA for business tier"
  ],
  "linked_fireflies": [
    "ff_2024-10-22_lanternridge_poc"
  ],
  "linked_gmail_threads": [
    "thread-CA12345lantern-10-22"
  ],
  "linked_drive_docs": [
    "drive:/LanternRidge/Redwood_Dedicated_POC_results_v1.xlsx",
    "drive:/LanternRidge/Redwood_pricing_deck_v3.pdf"
  ],
  "linked_support_tickets": [
    "RDW-1523"
  ],
  "activities": [
    "2024-09-20: Intro call (AE Jordan + SE Priya) - high level infra + use-case",
    "2024-10-01: Hosted API trial started (10-day credit) - three feature teams onboarded",
    "2024-10-08: Mid-trial check-in - observed latency baseline, ask for token-cost breakdown",
    "2024-10-22: Fireflies / full demo - SE reviewed batching/kv cache options (ff_2024-10-22_lanternridge_poc)",
    "2024-10-28: Trial wrap-up metrics exported; Redwood team provided dedicated sizing proposal",
    "2024-11-05: Commercial call with finance - requested committed capacity pricing options"
  ],
  "notes": [
    "POC notes: Product + Platform teams very focused on predictable unit economics",
    "Shorthand: 'hosted works well but spikes worry us' - PM (S. Alvarez)",
    "Prefers VPC for production due to PII in support transcripts; wants SOC2 + audit logs",
    "Legal: data residency check required (EU tenants) for subset of customers",
    "Cost sensitivity: target at-or-below $0.015 per 1k prompt+completion tokens across steady state",
    "AE notes: leaning toward dedicated if dedicated pricing and burst model align with finance"
  ],
  "trial_findings": [
    "Observed latency: p95 ~120-180ms for chat generation (hosted_api) at request size ~450 tokens",
    "Stability: stable under sustained QPS up to ~8, intermittent spikes to 22 QPS during batch exports",
    "Quality: model variant (open-llm-v2) met accuracy bar for reranking; no quality regressions observed",
    "Integration: embedding pipeline integrated with LangChain-style pipelines, indexing cost acceptable"
  ],
  "capacity_forecast": [
    "Hosted API POC (10 days) raw metrics: peak QPS 22, sustained QPS 6, typical concurrency observed 9",
    "Token profile (sampled POC): avg prompt tokens = 120, avg completion tokens = 320, avg tokens/request = 440",
    "Token mix: prompt:completion ~1:2.7 (support chat heavy on completions), requests/day observed ~12k => ~5.3M tokens/day",
    "Projected production (year 1): baseline QPS target = 80 sustained, peak QPS = 200 (5x current sustained), concurrency target = 120",
    "Projected token volume (year 1): 30M - 90M tokens/month depending on adoption scenarios",
    "Batching opportunity: expect 2.0-3.0x throughput uplift with Redwood batching + KV cache on common prompts"
  ],
  "dedicated_capacity_recommendation": [
    "Baseline dedicated pool recommended: 3 x 80GB-class GPUs (baseline) with autoscale to 6 during peak",
    "Estimated capacity: baseline pool approx. 120-180 QPS with aggressive batching; autoscale to 350+ QPS when burst enabled",
    "Concurrency planning: design for 150-200 concurrent inferences with soft limits and request queuing",
    "Caching: prefix/KV cache expected to reduce prompt token re-send by ~18% for conversational flows",
    "Routing: policy to route EU traffic to EU dedicated pool (data residency) + fallback to hosted in disaster recovery",
    "Cost note: dedicated reduces per-token cost but requires commit; finance asked for 12-month vs 24-month pricing scenarios"
  ],
  "business_requirements_summary": [
    "Workloads: mixed - chat-first for support agent, embeddings for search/indexing, reranking for NLU pipeline",
    "SLAs: target p95 latency <250ms for chat; throughput SLOs vary by tier (Gold = 95th percentile under peak)",
    "Resilience: automatic fallback to lower-cost model variant when primary pool saturated",
    "Observability: token-level cost breakdown and per-route dashboards required for chargeback"
  ],
  "quotes_and_observations": [
    "PM: 'We need predictable monthly spend, especially for the support product line'",
    "Platform Eng: 'If Redwood batching gives us >2x throughput we can cut GPU needs by 30%'",
    "Legal: 'Need explicit EU data residency and audit log retention policy - 3 years'"
  ],

    "quotes_and_observations"
  ],

}

document.content:
{
  "thread_id": "th_20261028_soojin_senior_infra_freeze_exception_001",
  "mailbox_owner": "soojin_lee",
  "subject": "Req acceleration request — Senior Infrastructure Engineer backfill (freeze exception)",
  "participants_internal": [
    "soojin_lee",
    "lauren_bishop",
    "hannah_schmitt",
    "jordan_blake",
    "marcus_lin"
  ],
  "participants_external": [
    "emma@talentplace.com (TalentPlace Recruiter)"
  ],
  "message_count": "5",
  "first_email_at": "2026-10-26T09:18:00-07:00",
  "last_email_at": "2026-10-28T10:05:00-07:00",
  "thread_type": "hiring",
  "region": "us",
  "has_attachments": "true",
  "attachments": [
    "Req_Form_Senior_Infra_20261026.pdf",
    "Senior_Infra_JD_v2.docx"
  ],
  "related_links": [
    "https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cHiringSprintDocs",
    "JIRA: INFRA-1287"
  ],
  "messages": [
    "From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Req acceleration request — Senior Infrastructure Engineer backfill (freeze exception)

Hi team,

Short ask: request approval for a freeze-exception and immediate sourcing for a Senior Infrastructure Engineer (backfill for A. Gomez, who is leaving end of November). This role is mission-critical for the next two quarters: we have the infra resilience sprint (Nov–Jan) and the KV cache migration that is on the critical path for Dedicated capacity cost reductions. Without a replacement we risk delaying the migration and exposing us to higher unit costs and capacity constraints.

Why now: the work is infra-facing (low ramp tax for existing systems), the candidate profile should be hireable in-market quickly, and the team can get the first deliverables within 8–10 weeks of start. Hiring a contractor is an option but we lose knowledge-transfer continuity and it will cost ~30% more for the same throughput.

Request:
- Approve a freeze exception for 1 headcount (Senior Infra Eng) and allow active sourcing immediately.
- Approve the attached req form (Req_Form_Senior_Infra_20261026.pdf).
- If budget owner needs to sign off, please confirm who (cost center) so I can route.

If you want, we can open as an SDE3 vs Staff split; my recommendation is SDE3 with a strong infra/ops background. I’ve copied Emma at TalentPlace to begin outreach if we get the green light.

Attachments: Req_Form_Senior_Infra_20261026.pdf

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Director, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
",
    "From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Req acceleration request — Senior Infrastructure Engineer backfill (freeze exception)

Soojin —

I approve in principle. This sounds like a clear risk to the migration timeline and to our cost objectives. Before formal sign-off: please confirm the cost center and the target start date. If budget sign-off will take time, approve a contingency: allow the recruiter to start active sourcing and take candidates to initial screens; final offer contingent on budget approval.

If you think contractor interim is necessary to avoid blockers, include estimated delta vs perm in the req form.

Lauren
VP, Engineering Operations

On Mon, Oct 26, 2026 at 09:18 AM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Short ask: request approval for a freeze-exception and immediate sourcing for a Senior Infrastructure Engineer (backfill for A. Gomez, who is leaving end of November).
>
> Attachments: Req_Form_Senior_Infra_20261026.pdf
",
    "From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Req acceleration request — Senior Infrastructure Engineer backfill (freeze exception)

Thanks — backing the ask but want a quick calibration against other live infra reqs. Please attach the JD and a 3-month runway estimate (salary + hiring expenses + any contractor delta). Also flag any conflicting hiring signals (e.g., other teams with higher-priority infra reqs) so we can queue appropriately.

I put a placeholder folder for docs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cHiringSprintDocs (please drop the JD there).

—Marcus
Head of Platform Delivery

On Mon, Oct 26, 2026 at 11:02 AM Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com> wrote:
> I approve in principle. This sounds like a clear risk to the migration timeline and to our cost objectives.
",
    "From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Emma (TalentPlace) <emma@talentplace.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Req acceleration request — Senior Infrastructure Engineer backfill (freeze exception)

Thanks Marcus — uploaded the JD and a short cost runway to the drive link (Senior_Infra_JD_v2.docx). Summary below:

- Cost center: ENG-PLATFORM-2 (owner: Marcus Lin)
- Target start: ideally 2026-12-01 (accepting 2027-01-03 at latest)
- Salary band: $170–200k (USD) + standard equity band for Senior level
- 3-month runway estimate: $50k (includes recruiter fees if external)
- Contractor delta: ~30% higher total cost for same period; lower long-term ROI

Emma — can you start outreach against the JD and share initial candidate slate by Nov 9? Recruiter brief is in the drive folder.

Attachments: Senior_Infra_JD_v2.docx

--
Soojin

On Mon, Oct 26, 2026 at 02:30 PM Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks — backing the ask but want a quick calibration against other live infra reqs.
",
    "From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Emma (TalentPlace) <emma@talentplace.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Req acceleration request — Senior Infrastructure Engineer backfill (freeze exception)

Approved: I authorize a freeze exception for 1 FTE (Senior Infra Eng) and authorize active sourcing and interviews to start. Conditions:

1) Final offer requires budget owner (Marcus) sign-off on total comp within the posted band.
2) Recruiter may run active search and book screens; no offers until Marcus confirms runway.
3) If we do not have viable candidates within 3 weeks of live posting, escalate to me and we will evaluate contractor interim or re-prioritization of the backlog.

Soojin — proceed to post the JD and coordinate with Emma. Keep hiring updates to the weekly QBR hiring check-in thread.

Lauren
VP, Engineering Operations

On Tue, Oct 27, 2026 at 09:15 AM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Marcus — uploaded the JD and a short cost runway to the drive link (Senior_Infra_JD_v2.docx).

This role is critical to the data-plane migration scheduled for Q4; without a replacement we expect increased SLA risk and a potential multi-week delay.\\n\\nWhy this is exceptional:\\n- Role is highly specialized: candidate has deep KV-cache & continuous-batching experience (not easily covered by generalist backend hires).\\n- Timing: two weeks notice from current engineer (last day 9/3). document.content:
{
  "thread_id": "gmail-soojin-20260818-hc-exc-001",
  "mailbox_owner": "soojin_lee",
  "subject": "Request: Exception to hiring freeze for Senior Infra IC (platform-migrate)",
  "participants_internal": [
    "soojin_lee",
    "laura_bennett",
    "markus_klein",
    "neha_kapoor"
  ],
  "participants_external": [
    "Polaris Talent <sarah@polaris-talent.com>",
    "GreenCore migrations (eng@greencore.com)"
  ],
  "message_count": "4",
  "first_email_at": "2026-08-12T09:15:00-07:00",
  "last_email_at": "2026-08-18T16:05:00-07:00",
  "thread_type": "hiring",
  "related_links": [
    "JIRA: INFRA-2247",
    "Drive: https://drive.redwood/workspace/platform/migration-risk-matrix"
  ],
  "has_attachments": "true",
  "attachments": [
    "hc_exception_form.pdf",
    "migration_risk_matrix.xlsx",
    "cost_breakdown_6mo.csv"
  ],
  "messages": [
    "From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, sarah@polaris-talent.com
Date: 2026-08-12 09:15 -0700
Subject: Request: Exception to hiring freeze for Senior Infra IC (platform-migrate)

Hi Laura / Markus,

Tl;dr: Requesting a one-time hiring-freeze exception to backfill a departing Senior Infrastructure Engineer (IC4) on Platform Services. This role is critical to the data-plane migration scheduled for Q4; without a replacement we expect increased SLA risk and a potential multi-week delay.

Why this is exceptional:
- Role is highly specialized: candidate has deep KV-cache & continuous-batching experience (not easily covered by generalist backend hires).
- Timing: two weeks notice from current engineer (last day 9/3). Migration has hard deadlines tied to customer contract INFRA-2247.
- Impact: with current staffing we estimate +30–45% risk of missing the rollout milestone and elevated on-call burden across two teams.

Proposed path:
1) Approve HC exception to backfill Senior IC (IC4) with either direct hire or 6-month contractor through Polaris Talent (attachment: cost_breakdown_6mo.csv).
2) If approved, prioritize internal candidates first (we have one internal transfer candidate in org).
3) If approval delayed >7 days, we will request temporary time-limited escalation budget for overtime and hiring agency retained search.

Attached: HC exception form (filled), migration risk matrix, six-month cost comparison (direct hire vs contractor).

Ask: Approve or provide guidance on preferred funnel (internal transfer vs external contractor) by EOD Aug 18 so we can start vendor engagement.

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee
Director, Platform Services
Redwood Inference
phone: (415) 555-0142

[attachment: hc_exception_form.pdf] [attachment: migration_risk_matrix.xlsx] [attachment: cost_breakdown_6mo.csv]",
    "From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-13 11:02 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Exception to hiring freeze for Senior Infra IC (platform-migrate)

Soojin — thanks for the clear summary. A couple quick Qs before I greenlight:

1) Headcount budget: do you have the hiring cost vs committed budget this FY (include recruiting fees if external)? I saw your attachment but would like a one-line delta to the org budget.
2) Coverage plan: if we approve internal transfer, who covers the gaps left by that transfer? (need names/teams).
3) SLA tolerances: quantify the customer impact in $ or churn risk if migration slips by 4 weeks.

If you can get me the answers and sign-off from Finance (Markus) and HR (Neha) by EOD Aug 18 I can approve the exception. If Finance can't commit, consider a 6-month contractor approval as fallback.

— Laura
VP Engineering
Redwood Inference

On Wed, Aug 12, 2026 at 9:15 AM Soojin Lee wrote:...",
    "From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, sarah@polaris-talent.com
Date: 2026-08-14 08:45 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Exception to hiring freeze for Senior Infra IC (platform-migrate)

Laura — quick follow with the concrete numbers you asked for:

1) Budget delta: direct hire (mid-band IC4) fully loaded = $240k/yr total comp equivalent; recruiting + ramp = ~ $30k in Y1, so net delta to FY budget = +$270k. 6-month contractor via agency = ~$85k (includes agency fee). See cost_breakdown_6mo.csv.
2) Internal transfer candidate: Marcus's team (Runtime) has Anna Park (IC3) flagged as stretch candidate; if Anna moves we estimate a 40% drop in Velocity on two active runtime tickets for 8 weeks. Proposed mitigation: shift two noncritical tickets to FY27 backlog and assign a 3rd rotation from SRE for 6 weeks.
3) SLA impact: conservative estimate is $120k ARR at risk (single large customer migration) and increased engineering support cost ~$25k in third-party consulting if we miss milestone by 4 weeks.

Attached is an updated one-pager summarizing these points and the requested approval box filled out on the HC exception form. I recommend approving a contractor for 6 months while we run a parallel external search — this minimizes SLA risk and gives time to evaluate internal transfer without blocking the migration schedule.

If you want, I can arrange a short sync with Finance (Markus) and Neha to run through the numbers tomorrow.

— Soojin

[inline: migration_risk_matrix.xlsx excerpt]

--- Forwarded message ---
From: Sarah Miller <sarah@polaris-talent.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-14 07:22 -07:00
Subject: Candidate availability

Soojin — we have two senior infra contractors available starting 9/7 and a permanent candidate who could move by late Sept. If you'd like the contractor hold we'll need a 3-day confirmation.

Best,
Sarah
Polaris Talent",
    "From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18 16:05 -07:00
Subject: RE: Request: Exception to hiring freeze for Senior Infra IC (platform-migrate)

All — reviewed the cost sheet and migration risk matrix. Finance can support a time-limited contractor approval up to $95k for six months on the condition that: 

- Recruiting runs concurrently and we aim for a permanent hire within 4 months,
- Team documents handover & runbooks in the first 30 days (Soojin, please own),
- A post-mortem and budget reconciliation is provided to Finance within 90 days.

Laura — if that's acceptable from your side, consider this the Finance conditional approval. Neha — please confirm any compliance/contracting constraints on short-term contractor engagements and confirm whether Polaris has passed vendor onboarding.

Markus Klein
Director, Finance Planning
Redwood Inference

    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"ADR: Declarative Contract Tests and Schema Fencing\",\n  \"space\": \"architecture-and-standards\",\n  \"author\": \"Aisha Patel\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-02-15\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2026-03-01\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Diego Martinez\",\n    \"Sara Kim\",\n    \"Liam O'Connor\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"adr\",\n    \"contract-testing\",\n    \"schema-fencing\",\n    \"ci-cd\",\n    \"conformance\"\n  ],\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/canonical-request-schema-and-validation-playbook-2025\",\n    \"/architecture-and-standards/model-serving-standards/variant-compatibility-ledger-and-stewardship-protocol-2026\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"internal\",\n  \"content\": \"Summary\\n\\nThis ADR defines a company-wide standard for declarative contract tests and a complementary \\\"schema fencing\\\" discipline to prevent schema drift between services and the Redwood platform (APIs, telemetry, and model-serving payloads). The goal is to make API and model I/O contracts machine-testable, versioned, and CI-gated, minimizing production surprises and simplifying rollback and compatibility reasoning.\\n\\nContext and motivation\\n\\nRecent incidents and near-misses were traced to silent schema changes that allowed malformed or unexpectedly shaped requests/telemetry to flow into the runtime. Ad-hoc unit tests are insufficient for cross-service contract guarantees because:\\n\\n- Contracts span teams (edge proxies, gateways, runtime, and client SDKs).\\n- Behavioral compatibility is not captured by type checks alone (e.g., field deprecation with semantic changes).\\n- Runtime routing fallback and model-variant compatibility require an explicit, testable matrix.\\n\\nThis ADR proposes:\\n\\n1. A declarative, YAML-first contract-test spec that lives next to service code and in a central conformance repo for cross-service scopes.\\n2. A \\\"schema fencing\\\" lifecycle that fences allowed shape changes via explicit change proposals, automated conformance checks, and CI gates.\\n3. A conformance status ledger and telemetry for contract drift and failed-matrix cell SLI.\\n\\nScope\\n\\nApplies to:\\n\\n- Public and internal HTTP/GRPC REST endpoints (edge, control-plane, telemetry ingestion).\\n- Model-serving input/output schemas (prompts, structured responses, embeddings metadata).\\n- Streaming/session protocols where message schemas are negotiated.\\n\\nOut of scope:\\n\\n- Internal-only helper functions that are never consumed by other services.\\n- Ad-hoc developer prototypes until they are promoted to a supported service.\\n\\nKey concepts\\n\\nDeclarative contract test spec (DCTS):\\n- A human-friendly YAML format that describes request/response shapes, example inputs, success/failure predicates, and conformance categories (strict, tolerant, deprecated).\\n- DCTS entries can be unit-run (local), CI-run (service-level), and cross-service-run (integration conformance matrix).\\n\\nSchema fencing:\\n- Every change to a DCTS schema field must be accompanied by a Change Proposal (CP) file and an automated compatibility check.\\n- CPs are accepted automatically if they pass compatibility rules or fail open for manual review if they are breaking.\\n\\nConformance matrix and ledger:\\n- A centrally aggregated matrix that tracks which service versions (and model variants) satisfy which DCTS cells.\\n- Each matrix cell has a pass/fail history and a conformance SLI aggregated daily.\\n\\nRules and compatibility classes\\n\\nFields are labeled with one of: required, optional, deprecated, extension. Compatibility rules:\\n\\n- required -> optional: allowed but requires explicit CP and CI signal.\\n- optional -> required: breaking change; requires canary/rollout plan and staged opt-in.\\n- remove deprecated field: allowed only after 3 release cycles and >95% conformance across callers.\\n- add new field marked extension: always allowed if receivers ignore unknown fields (tolerant mode).\\n\\nChange proposal workflow (brief)\\n\\n1. Author creates a CP file in the service repo under docs/contracts/cps/<pr>.yaml describing intent, compatibility class, rollout plan, and rollback criteria.\\n2. CI runs: unit tests, DCTS local run, contract linters, and cross-service dry-run against the latest conformance snapshot.\\n3. If auto-check passes (non-breaking or safe extension), merge proceeds. If flagged as potentially breaking, the CP moves to manual review by contract stewards and product owners.\\n4. After merge, integration conformance jobs run nightly to validate callers and receivers.\\n\\nExample DCTS snippet (YAML)\\n\\n# Example: /v1/generate request/response\\n# Save as service/docs/contracts/dcts/generate.v1.yaml\\n---\\nendpoint: POST /v1/generate\\nscope: public\\nversion: 1.0.0\\nmode: strict\\nrequest: \\n  content-type: application/json\\n  schema: |\\n    type: object\\n    properties:\\n      prompt:\\n        type: string\\n      features:\\n        type: object\\n        additionalProperties: true\\n    required: [prompt]\\nexamples:\\n  - name: simplest\\n    request: {\\\"prompt\\\": \\\"Summarize the following text...\\\"}\\nresponse:\\n  schema: |\\n    type: object\\n    properties:\\n      id: {type: string}\\n      output: {type: string}\\n      tokens_consumed: {type: integer}\\n    required: [id, output]\\npredicates:\\n  - description: output must be non-empty\\n    jq: \\\".output | length > 0\\\"\\nconformance_category: strict\\n\\nAutomation and CI integration\\n\\nCI responsibilities (service repo):\\n- Run local DCTS validation (schema validity, example conformance).\\n- Run contract linter: enforces required metadata fields (owner, risk_level, test_coverage_min).\\n- Publish DCTS artifact to conformance-bucket/<service>/<version>/dcts.yaml on successful merge.\\n\\nCross-repo conformance job (central):\\n- Nightly job that pulls the published DCTS artifacts and runs pairwise checks across known callers and receivers.\\n- Failing cells create RFC-style issues in the responsible service repo and update the conformance ledger with failure signals.\\n\\nConformance ledger and dashboard\\n\\nThe ledger is a time-series-friendly table with columns described below and exposed in the Redwood Console and an internal dashboard. Store as rows in our metrics DB and index in the conformance service. (Table described in prose below.)\\n\\nRequired columns (ledger row): timestamp, service_a, service_a_version, service_b, service_b_version, endpoint, dcts_version, test_case_id, result (pass|fail), failure_reason, run_id.\\n\\nOperational SLOs and alerting\\n\\n- Nightly conformance pass rate for critical public endpoints >= 99.0%. Alert if < 98.0% over a 24-hour rolling window.\\n- Any new CP that causes a regression in an existing passing matrix cell triggers a P1 review if the affected client is production and >= 10% traffic.\\n\\nGating and release policy\\n\\n- Service merge gating: Non-breaking CPs are mergeable. Breaking CPs require manual approval and a staged rollout with canary conformance verifying client behavior.\\n- Platform releases (runtime, SDKs): must maintain 100% conformance for official SDK bindings across supported minor versions.\\n\\nRollout and rollback playbook (high level)\\n\\n1. Pre-merge: author runs smoke DCTS locally and creates CP with rollout notes.\\n2. Merge: DCTS published and cross-repo nightlies scheduled.\\n3. Canary: route 5% traffic to new service variant for 2 hours while conformance checks run.\\n4. Monitor: observe ledger and user-facing errors for regressions.\\n5. If failure SLI breached or critical callers fail, execute rollback to previous version and open an incident review.\\n\\nTelemetry and observability requirements\\n\\nEach contract-test run must emit:\\n- conftest.run_id (UUID)\\n- conftest.service (service name/version)\\n- conftest.endpoint\\n- conftest.test_case_id\\n- conftest.result (pass|fail)\\n- conftest.duration_ms\\n\\nThese fields are sent to the conformance-ingest pipeline with low-cardinality sampling for historical debugging. Link failures to trace IDs when available.\\n\\nOwner and stewardship\\n\\n- Contract steward role: a cross-functional team (API Platform + SRE + Product) that maintains the conformance harness, linter rules, and central ledger.\\n- Service owners: must author and maintain DCTS files for each public surface and model variant.\\n\\nOpen questions and tradeoffs\\n\\n- How strict should default mode be for internal endpoints? Proposal: internal endpoints default to tolerant mode, but any endpoint used by another service must be promoted to strict with a DCTS.\\n- Cost vs. coverage: nightly full-matrix checks are expensive. We propose prioritized sweeps (critical endpoints every night, others weekly).\\n\\nMigration plan\\n\\n1. Pilot: Onboard three services (edge-proxy, runtime-controller, and the embeddings-ingest) to the DCTS and CP workflow over Q2 2026.\\n2. Expand to all public endpoints and model-serving inputs by Q4 2026.\\n3. Enforce gate for new public endpoints starting Q1 2027.\\n\\nAppendix: sample CLI commands and linter config\\n\\n# Local validation\\n#   conftest validate service/docs/contracts/dcts/*.yaml\\n\\n# Publish artifact (CI step)\\n#   conftest publish --bucket=conformance-bucket --service=$SERVICE --version=$VERSION dcts.yaml\\n\\n# Central conformance run (dry-run example)\\n#   conformance-runner --matrix-file=matrix.json --artifacts-dir=artifacts/ --output=ledger.csv\\n\\n# Linter rules (excerpt)\\n# required: [owner, risk_level, conformance_category, test_coverage_min]\\n\\nNotes on documentation style\\n\\n- Keep DCTS files short and example-driven. Prefer real-world examples over exhaustive machine-generated schemas.\\n- Use the CP description field to capture rationale and expected client impact.\\n\\nReferences\\n\\n- See canonical request schema and validation playbook: /architecture-and-standards/api-standards/canonical-request-schema-and-validation-playbook-2025\\n- Variant compatibility ledger: /architecture-and-standards/model-serving-standards/variant-compatibility-ledger-and-stewardship-protocol-2026\\n\\nApproval\\n\\nApproved by: API Platform leadership, SRE management, and Product for runtime conformance.\\n\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"content\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_04b24bf957c047f4b7d8ceefdfde8290\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: ADR: Declarative Contract Tests and Schema Fencing\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-declarative-contract-tests-and-schema-fencing-2026.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: architecture-and-standards\n\nnew field marked extension : always allowed if receivers ignore unknown fields ( tolerant mode ). change proposal workflow ( brief ) 1. author creates a cp file in the service repo under docs / contracts / cps / < pr >. yaml describing intent, compatibility class, rollout plan, and rollback criteria. 2. ci runs : unit tests, dcts local run, contract linters, and cross - service dry - run against the latest conformance snapshot. 3. if auto - check passes ( non - breaking or safe extension ), merge proceeds. if flagged as potentially breaking, the cp moves to manual review by contract stewards and product owners. 4. after merge, integration conformance jobs run nightly to validate callers and receivers.",

document.title: ADR: Declarative Contract Tests and Schema Fencing
