document.content:
{
  "thread_id": "gmail-soojin-20260818-hc-exc-001",
  "mailbox_owner": "soojin_lee",
  "subject": "Request: Exception to hiring freeze for Senior Infra IC (platform-migrate)",
  "participants_internal": [
    "soojin_lee",
    "laura_bennett",
    "markus_klein",
    "neha_kapoor"
  ],
  "participants_external": [
    "Polaris Talent <sarah@polaris-talent.com>",
    "GreenCore migrations (eng@greencore.com)"
  ],
  "message_count": "4",
  "first_email_at": "2026-08-12T09:15:00-07:00",
  "last_email_at": "2026-08-18T16:05:00-07:00",
  "thread_type": "hiring",
  "related_links": [
    "JIRA: INFRA-2247",
    "Drive: https://drive.redwood/workspace/platform/migration-risk-matrix"
  ],
  "has_attachments": "true",
  "attachments": [
    "hc_exception_form.pdf",
    "migration_risk_matrix.xlsx",
    "cost_breakdown_6mo.csv"
  ],
  "messages": [
    "From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, sarah@polaris-talent.com
Date: 2026-08-12 09:15 -0700
Subject: Request: Exception to hiring freeze for Senior Infra IC (platform-migrate)

Hi Laura / Markus,

Tl;dr: Requesting a one-time hiring-freeze exception to backfill a departing Senior Infrastructure Engineer (IC4) on Platform Services. This role is critical to the data-plane migration scheduled for Q4; without a replacement we expect increased SLA risk and a potential multi-week delay.

Why this is exceptional:
- Role is highly specialized: candidate has deep KV-cache & continuous-batching experience (not easily covered by generalist backend hires).
- Timing: two weeks notice from current engineer (last day 9/3). Migration has hard deadlines tied to customer contract INFRA-2247.
- Impact: with current staffing we estimate +30–45% risk of missing the rollout milestone and elevated on-call burden across two teams.

Proposed path:
1) Approve HC exception to backfill Senior IC (IC4) with either direct hire or 6-month contractor through Polaris Talent (attachment: cost_breakdown_6mo.csv).
2) If approved, prioritize internal candidates first (we have one internal transfer candidate in org).
3) If approval delayed >7 days, we will request temporary time-limited escalation budget for overtime and hiring agency retained search.

Attached: HC exception form (filled), migration risk matrix, six-month cost comparison (direct hire vs contractor).

Ask: Approve or provide guidance on preferred funnel (internal transfer vs external contractor) by EOD Aug 18 so we can start vendor engagement.

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee
Director, Platform Services
Redwood Inference
phone: (415) 555-0142

[attachment: hc_exception_form.pdf] [attachment: migration_risk_matrix.xlsx] [attachment: cost_breakdown_6mo.csv]",
    "From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-13 11:02 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Exception to hiring freeze for Senior Infra IC (platform-migrate)

Soojin — thanks for the clear summary. A couple quick Qs before I greenlight:

1) Headcount budget: do you have the hiring cost vs committed budget this FY (include recruiting fees if external)? I saw your attachment but would like a one-line delta to the org budget.
2) Coverage plan: if we approve internal transfer, who covers the gaps left by that transfer? (need names/teams).
3) SLA tolerances: quantify the customer impact in $ or churn risk if migration slips by 4 weeks.

If you can get me the answers and sign-off from Finance (Markus) and HR (Neha) by EOD Aug 18 I can approve the exception. If Finance can't commit, consider a 6-month contractor approval as fallback.

— Laura
VP Engineering
Redwood Inference

On Wed, Aug 12, 2026 at 9:15 AM Soojin Lee wrote:...",
    "From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, sarah@polaris-talent.com
Date: 2026-08-14 08:45 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Exception to hiring freeze for Senior Infra IC (platform-migrate)

Laura — quick follow with the concrete numbers you asked for:

1) Budget delta: direct hire (mid-band IC4) fully loaded = $240k/yr total comp equivalent; recruiting + ramp = ~ $30k in Y1, so net delta to FY budget = +$270k. 6-month contractor via agency = ~$85k (includes agency fee). See cost_breakdown_6mo.csv.
2) Internal transfer candidate: Marcus's team (Runtime) has Anna Park (IC3) flagged as stretch candidate; if Anna moves we estimate a 40% drop in Velocity on two active runtime tickets for 8 weeks. Proposed mitigation: shift two noncritical tickets to FY27 backlog and assign a 3rd rotation from SRE for 6 weeks.
3) SLA impact: conservative estimate is $120k ARR at risk (single large customer migration) and increased engineering support cost ~$25k in third-party consulting if we miss milestone by 4 weeks.

Attached is an updated one-pager summarizing these points and the requested approval box filled out on the HC exception form. I recommend approving a contractor for 6 months while we run a parallel external search — this minimizes SLA risk and gives time to evaluate internal transfer without blocking the migration schedule.

If you want, I can arrange a short sync with Finance (Markus) and Neha to run through the numbers tomorrow.

— Soojin

[inline: migration_risk_matrix.xlsx excerpt]

--- Forwarded message ---
From: Sarah Miller <sarah@polaris-talent.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-14 07:22 -07:00
Subject: Candidate availability

Soojin — we have two senior infra contractors available starting 9/7 and a permanent candidate who could move by late Sept. If you'd like the contractor hold we'll need a 3-day confirmation.

Best,
Sarah
Polaris Talent",
    "From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18 16:05 -07:00
Subject: RE: Request: Exception to hiring freeze for Senior Infra IC (platform-migrate)

All — reviewed the cost sheet and migration risk matrix. Finance can support a time-limited contractor approval up to $95k for six months on the condition that: 

- Recruiting runs concurrently and we aim for a permanent hire within 4 months,
- Team documents handover & runbooks in the first 30 days (Soojin, please own),
- A post-mortem and budget reconciliation is provided to Finance within 90 days.

Laura — if that's acceptable from your side, consider this the Finance conditional approval. Neha — please confirm any compliance/contracting constraints on short-term contractor engagements and confirm whether Polaris has passed vendor onboarding.

Markus Klein
Director, Finance Planning
Redwood Inference

    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"ENG-146201\",\n  \"team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"title\": \"Release Horizon Supervisor: staged rollout heuristics and safepoints\",\n  \"status\": \"In Progress\",\n  \"priority\": \"P1\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-02-10\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-03-12\",\n  \"creator\": \"Avery Chen\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Luis Martinez\",\n  \"project\": \"model-lifecycle\",\n  \"cycle\": \"2026-W10\",\n  \"estimate\": \"8\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2026-03-30\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"release-safety\",\n    \"canary-orchestration\",\n    \"observability\",\n    \"auto-rollback\",\n    \"shadowing\"\n  ],\n  \"dependencies\": [\n    \"ENG-5314\",\n    \"ENG-21456\"\n  ],\n  \"release\": \"runtime-1.19\",\n  \"customer_impact\": \"medium\",\n  \"security_review_required\": \"false\",\n  \"description\": \"Goal: Implement a supervisor component (Release Horizon Supervisor) that composes staged rollout heuristics, safepoints, and automatic rollback triggers for model variant introductions. This ticket covers the configuration model, policy evaluation loop, and integration hooks for shadow traffic and A/B experiments.\\n\\nScope:\\n- Define a compact, human- and API-friendly rollout spec (traffic steps, dwell windows, attenuation curves, and safepoints).\\n- Implement policy evaluator that (a) enforces guardrails (latency/error/quality thresholds), (b) advances or pauses steps based on telemetry, and (c) emits structured audit events for console and runbooks.\\n- Add shadowing toggles for parallel probing of candidate variants without impacting live split.\\n- Provide an auto-rollback policy with hysteresis and graduated backoff to avoid flapping.\\n- Expose diagnostic endpoints and Grafana panels for per-step metrics and rationale.\\n\\nDesign highlights and novel ideas:\\n- \\\"Safepoints\\\": explicit named checkpoints in a rollout where non-reversible expansion requires additional approval or stronger signals. Safepoints can be configured as time-based or metric-based.\\n- \\\"Horizon decay\\\": a configurable attenuation function that slows traffic growth if variance in key metrics increases; helps prevent step overshoot for bursty workloads.\\n- Quality-aware splits: traffic weights can be dynamically rebalanced by integrating a lightweight quality signal (e.g., rerank drift or semantic similarity) for A/B tests.\\n- Shadow probes: sampled requests are mirrored to candidate variants with separate budget accounting; failures in the shadow path do not affect the live split but surface in the supervisor's risk score.\\n\\nAcceptance criteria:\\n1) POST /rollouts accepts new spec and validates schema, including safepoints and attenuation curve.\\n2) Supervisor advances steps automatically when configured SLOs are met for a configurable consecutive window, and pauses when the guardrail is violated.\\n3) Automatic rollback triggers when sustained regression (configurable window) exceeds threshold; rollback includes a cooldown to prevent immediate reattempt.\\n4) Shadowing mode can be enabled per-route and produced mirrored telemetry tracked independently.\\n5) E2E integration tests added that simulate latency spikes, error bursts, and quality regressions and assert supervisor behavior.\\n6) Grafana dashboard with per-step metrics and an \\\"explain\\\" view (why step advanced/paused/rolled back).\\n\\nImplementation plan (phases):\\n- Phase 1 (this ticket): rollout spec + evaluator + basic guardrails (latency, 5xx, request rate) + API and metrics emission.\\n- Phase 2: add shadow traffic support, quality signal plumbing, attenuation curves, and safepoints approval flow.\\n- Phase 3: UI integration, runbook generation, and SLO tuning recommendations from Optimize.\\n\\nOpen trade-offs:\\n- Conservative defaults vs. rapid exposure: we will default to conservative step sizes (5%, 15%, 30%, 100%) but expose power-user profiles for aggressive rollouts.\\n- Local vs centralized evaluation: central evaluator simplifies policy enforcement and auditing but increases coordination cost for dedicated/private deployments. We'll implement a central evaluation service with a thin local cache for private mode.\",\n  \"links\": [\n    \"https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PL/Release+Horizon+Supervisor+Spec\",\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/service/pull/4382\",\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/supervisor/pull/27\",\n    \"https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abc123/canary-health\",\n    \"https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/rollout-horizon\"\n  ],\n  \"comments\": [\n    \"2026-02-12 - Avery Chen: Initial spec drafted; opened design doc and initial proto of JSON schema. Asked infra for rate-limiter quota estimates for shadow probes.\",\n    \"2026-02-18 - Luis Martinez: Pushed validator and first pass API. Local test harness simulates step progression. TODO: wire metrics tags for safepoint evaluation.\",\n    \"2026-02-25 - Priya Nambiar (PM): Reviewed; requested explicit support for \\\"canary groups\\\" (cohorts) so we can route subsets by tenant. Marked requirement for Phase 2.\",\n    \"2026-02-28 - QA (Jordan Lee): Ran chaos scenarios: latency spike causes pause as expected, but observed a race where step timer advanced despite transient metric delay. Added deterministic windowing to address flakiness (see PR comments).\",\n    \"2026-03-05 - Security (Marta Ruiz): Confirmed no additional secrets; recommended audit-event enrichment with request IDs for postmortems. security_review_required=false noted.\",\n    \"2026-03-09 - Luis Martinez: Integrated shadow probe accounting; shadow traffic uses a separate budget and appears on the Grafana panel. Opening PR to supervisor repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/supervisor/pull/27\",\n    \"2026-03-11 - Avery Chen: Decision: default attenuation curve will be exponential-backoff shaped to penalize variance; conservative profile will be the default to minimize customer impact. Logged design rationale in Confluence.\",\n    \"2026-03-12 - Release Engineering (Olga Petrov): Requested that safepoints be surfaced in the Console before GA. Phase 2 dependency added for UI work.\"\n  ],\n  \"review_feedback\": [\n    \"Priya Nambiar (PM): Please include a simple escape hatch for emergency instant rollback (manual trigger + API) and ensure runbook has steps annotated.\",\n    \"Jordan Lee (QA): Add deterministic replay test for shadow traffic to ensure no data loss in mirroring pipeline.\",\n    \"Marta Ruiz (Security): Audit events must include principal and token hash for compliance.\"\n  ],\n  \"next_steps\": [\n    \"Finish PR reviews and merge supervisor runtime changes (ENG-146201).\",\n    \"Add E2E tests to ci/integration that simulate quality regressions fed from fake-eval harness.\",\n    \"Coordinate with Console team for safepoint UI (add as dependency for Phase 2).\",\n    \"Schedule internal dogfood rollout for a non-critical model next cycle.\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"comments\",\n    \"review_feedback\",\n    \"next_steps\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_7fbe479eafbf4493a14376324c723a95\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Release Horizon Supervisor: staged rollout heuristics and safepoints\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-146201-release-horizon-supervisor.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: model-lifecycle\nTeam: engineering\n\n. this ticket covers the configuration model, policy evaluation loop, and integration hooks for shadow traffic and a / b experiments. scope : - define a compact, human - and api - friendly rollout spec ( traffic steps, dwell windows, attenuation curves, and safepoints ). - implement policy evaluator that ( a ) enforces guardrails ( latency / error / quality thresholds ), ( b ) advances or pauses steps based on telemetry, and ( c ) emits structured audit events for console and runbooks. - add shadowing toggles for parallel probing of candidate variants without impacting live split. - provide an auto - rollback policy with hysteresis and graduated backoff to avoid flapping. - expose diagnostic endpoints and grafana panels for per - step metrics and rationale.",

document.content:
{
  "key": "ENG-146201",
  "team": "engineering",
  "title": "Release Horizon Supervisor: staged rollout heuristics and safepoints",
  "status": "In Progress",
  "priority": "P1",
  "created_at": "2026-02-10",
  "updated_at": "2026-03-12",
  "creator": "Avery Chen",
  "assignee": "Luis Martinez",
  "project": "model-lifecycle",
  "cycle": "2026-W10",
  "estimate": "8",
  "due_date": "2026-03-30",
  "labels": [
    "release-safety",
    "canary-orchestration",
    "observability",
    "auto-rollback",
    "shadowing"
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    "ENG-5314",
    "ENG-21456"
  ],
  "release": "runtime-1.19",
  "customer_impact": "medium",
  "security_review_required": "false",
  "description": "Goal: Implement a supervisor component (Release Horizon Supervisor) that composes staged rollout heuristics, safepoints, and automatic rollback triggers for model variant introductions. This ticket covers the configuration model, policy evaluation loop, and integration hooks for shadow traffic and A/B experiments.\n\nScope:\n- Define a compact, human- and API-friendly rollout spec (traffic steps, dwell windows, attenuation curves, and safepoints).\n- Implement policy evaluator that (a) enforces guardrails (latency/error/quality thresholds), (b) advances or pauses steps based on telemetry, and (c) emits structured audit events for console and runbooks.\n- Add shadowing toggles for parallel probing of candidate variants without impacting live split.\n- Provide an auto-rollback policy with hysteresis and graduated backoff to avoid flapping.\n- Expose diagnostic endpoints and Grafana panels for per-step metrics and rationale.\n\nDesign highlights and novel ideas:\n- \"Safepoints\": explicit named checkpoints in a rollout where non-reversible expansion requires additional approval or stronger signals. Safepoints can be configured as time-based or metric-based.\n- \"Horizon decay\": a configurable attenuation function that slows traffic growth if variance in key metrics increases; helps prevent step overshoot for bursty workloads.\n- Quality-aware splits: traffic weights can be dynamically rebalanced by integrating a lightweight quality signal (e.g., rerank drift or semantic similarity) for A/B tests.\n- Shadow probes: sampled requests are mirrored to candidate variants with separate budget accounting; failures in the shadow path do not affect the live split but surface in the supervisor's risk score.\n\nAcceptance criteria:\n1) POST /rollouts accepts new spec and validates schema, including safepoints and attenuation curve.\n2) Supervisor advances steps automatically when configured SLOs are met for a configurable consecutive window, and pauses when the guardrail is violated.\n3) Automatic rollback triggers when sustained regression (configurable window) exceeds threshold; rollback includes a cooldown to prevent immediate reattempt.\n4) Shadowing mode can be enabled per-route and produced mirrored telemetry tracked independently.\n5) E2E integration tests added that simulate latency spikes, error bursts, and quality regressions and assert supervisor behavior.\n6) Grafana dashboard with per-step metrics and an \"explain\" view (why step advanced/paused/rolled back).\n\nImplementation plan (phases):\n- Phase 1 (this ticket): rollout spec + evaluator + basic guardrails (latency, 5xx, request rate) + API and metrics emission.\n- Phase 2: add shadow traffic support, quality signal plumbing, attenuation curves, and safepoints approval flow.\n- Phase 3: UI integration, runbook generation, and SLO tuning recommendations from Optimize.\n\nOpen trade-offs:\n- Conservative defaults vs. rapid exposure: we will default to conservative step sizes (5%, 15%, 30%, 100%) but expose power-user profiles for aggressive rollouts.\n- Local vs centralized evaluation: central evaluator simplifies policy enforcement and auditing but increases coordination cost for dedicated/private deployments. We'll implement a central evaluation service with a thin local cache for private mode.",
  "links": [
    "https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PL/Release+Horizon+Supervisor+Spec",
    "https://github.com/redwood-inference/service/pull/4382",
    "https://github.com/redwood-inference/supervisor/pull/27",
    "https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abc123/canary-health",
    "https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/rollout-horizon"
  ],
  "comments": [
    "2026-02-12 - Avery Chen: Initial spec drafted; opened design doc and initial proto of JSON schema. Asked infra for rate-limiter quota estimates for shadow probes.",
    "2026-02-18 - Luis Martinez: Pushed validator and first pass API. Local test harness simulates step progression. TODO: wire metrics tags for safepoint evaluation.",
    "2026-02-25 - Priya Nambiar (PM): Reviewed; requested explicit support for \"canary groups\" (cohorts) so we can route subsets by tenant. Marked requirement for Phase 2.",
    "2026-02-28 - QA (Jordan Lee): Ran chaos scenarios: latency spike causes pause as expected, but observed a race where step timer advanced despite transient metric delay. Added deterministic windowing to address flakiness (see PR comments).",
    "2026-03-05 - Security (Marta Ruiz): Confirmed no additional secrets; recommended audit-event enrichment with request IDs for postmortems. security_review_required=false noted.",
    "2026-03-09 - Luis Martinez: Integrated shadow probe accounting; shadow traffic uses a separate budget and appears on the Grafana panel. Opening PR to supervisor repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/supervisor/pull/27",
    "2026-03-11 - Avery Chen: Decision: default attenuation curve will be exponential-backoff shaped to penalize variance; conservative profile will be the default to minimize customer impact. Logged design rationale in Confluence.",
    "2026-03-12 - Release Engineering (Olga Petrov): Requested that safepoints be surfaced in the Console before GA. Phase 2 dependency added for UI work."
  ],
  "review_feedback": [
    "Priya Nambiar (PM): Please include a simple escape hatch for emergency instant rollback (manual trigger + API) and ensure runbook has steps annotated.",
    "Jordan Lee (QA): Add deterministic replay test for shadow traffic to ensure no data loss in mirroring pipeline.",
    "Marta Ruiz (Security): Audit events must include principal and token hash for compliance."
  ],
  "next_steps": [
    "Finish PR reviews and merge supervisor runtime changes (ENG-146201).",
    "Add E2E tests to ci/integration that simulate quality regressions fed from fake-eval harness.",
    "Coordinate with Console team for safepoint UI (add as dependency for Phase 2).",
    "Schedule internal dogfood rollout for a non-critical model next cycle."
  ],
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "description",
    "comments",
    "review_feedback",
    "next_steps"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_7fbe479eafbf4493a14376324c723a95"
}

    "id": "dsid_8c928a8dd9364b1fad4c2f4753559718",

    "title": "Private release stager and rollback playbook generator",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/linear",
    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"ENG-847531\",\n  \"team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"title\": \"Private release stager and rollback playbook generator\",\n  \"status\": \"In Progress\",\n  \"priority\": \"P0\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-02-12\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2025-03-04\",\n  \"creator\": \"Aisha Patel\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Liam Chen\",\n  \"project\": \"Private Upgrade Safety\",\n  \"cycle\": \"2025-W09\",\n  \"estimate\": \"8\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2025-04-01\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"private\",\n    \"upgrade\",\n    \"lts\",\n    \"release-engineering\",\n    \"telemetry\"\n  ],\n  \"dependencies\": [\n    \"ENG-33188\",\n    \"ENG-47291\"\n  ],\n  \"customer_impact\": \"high\",\n  \"release\": \"private-upgrade-2025.04\",\n  \"security_review_required\": \"true\",\n  \"description\": \"Build an automated release stager and runbook generator for Redwood Private upgrades. The tool will assemble staged cohorts, preflight checks, canary gating rules, and a machine-readable rollback playbook from version metadata and migration manifests. Goal: reduce manual runbook creation, surface safe fallbacks, and enable telemetry-driven automatic abort/rollback triggers for private (VPC/on-prem) upgrade runs.\",\n  \"acceptance_criteria\": [\n    \"CLI or API can produce a per-version release bundle (manifest + staged cohorts + runbook) from a model/operator release tag within < 60s\",\n    \"Generated runbook includes step-by-step commands, required approvals, and automatic rollback hooks that can be consumed by the upgrade agent\",\n    \"Preflight checks execute against a customer-like sandbox and surface blocking signals (schema drift, DB migration preview failures, node capacity shortfall)\",\n    \"Canary gate can be configured to auto-abort based on telemetry (p95 latency, error-rate, KV cache miss), with documented thresholds\",\n    \"Rollout metadata exposed in Console (per-cohort progress, blocked step reasons) and emits standardized telemetry events to the Upgrade dashboard\",\n    \"Integration tests covering dry-run generation, a simulated canary abort, and scripted rollback against the upgrade simulator pass in CI\"\n  ],\n  \"implementation_notes\": [\n    \"Design a small declarative manifest format (YAML) that describes: version, LTS channel, cohort definitions, migration SQL artifacts, preflight commands, expected invariants\",\n    \"Generator will incorporate: version compatibility matrix, LTS policies, pinned component versions, and 'rollback recipe' templates\",\n    \"Expose a 'preview' mode that runs all preflight checks without mutating state; capture outputs and synthesize a risk score\",\n    \"Integrate with existing Private upgrade agent via a contract: /v1/upgrades/start endpoint which accepts the generated bundle\",\n    \"Wire telemetry hooks to Console's Upgrade dashboard and to existing tracing (otlp) so gates can evaluate p95, error-rate, and custom migration metrics\",\n    \"Provide a 'manual approval' gate that posts to Slack channel and requires an approver to click a link (SAML/SSO-aware) before continuing\",\n    \"Ship initial generator as 'alpha' CLI + a lightweight web preview; rollout to internal customers first before external tenants\"\n  ],\n  \"rollout_plan\": [\n    \"Stage 0 (internal): generate bundles for two non-production clusters and run dry-run preflight (2 weeks)\",\n    \"Stage 1 (canary): run staged release against 3 low-risk customer tenants with manual approval gates and telemetry monitoring (2 weeks)\",\n    \"Stage 2 (gradual): expand cohorts to 20% of private fleet with auto-gating enabled; if any auto-abort occurs, execute rollback playbook (4 weeks)\",\n    \"Stage 3 (ga): enable default runbook generation for all scheduled Private upgrades; include opt-out and custom playbook extensions\"\n  ],\n  \"telemetry_signals\": [\n    \"api.request.latency.p95 (global & per-tenant)\",\n    \"api.request.error_rate (5xx/4xx spike by tenant)\",\n    \"gpu.utilization and host.cpu.utilization\",\n    \"kv_cache.hit_rate (drop > 10% signals regression)\",\n    \"db.migration.lag and db.lock-wait-count\",\n    \"upgrade.step.failures (unexpected non-zero exit)\",\n    \"suite.preflight.check_failures and preflight.risk_score\"\n  ],\n  \"runbook_links\": [\n    \"https://confluence.redwood.com/display/UPGRADE/Playbook+Generator+Design\",\n    \"https://drive.redwood.com/Shared/PrivateUpgrade/alpha-bundles\",\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-upgrades/pull/492\",\n    \"https://grafana.redwood.com/d/upgrade/upgrade-dashboard?orgId=1\",\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/upgrade-agent/issues/118\"\n  ],\n  \"migration_strategy\": [\n    \"Prefer online, idempotent migrations where possible. When transactional migrations are required, generate a two-phase: preview->apply pattern\",\n    \"All SQL DDL must be run with compatibility guards and scheduled with low-traffic windows\",\n    \"Keep a 'compat shim' loader for older control-plane agents to accept bundles and gracefully reject incompatible fields\",\n    \"For heavy data transforms, include a migration-progress probe and a 'quiesce' step that drains incoming requests to affected shards\"\n  ],\n  \"risks\": [\n    \"Automated playbook might miss tenant-specific customizations; mitigated by an 'extensions' hook and manual review step\",\n    \"Telemetry false positives could trigger unnecessary rollbacks; mitigate with smoothing window and multi-signal confirmation\",\n    \"Edge-case migrations (on-prem air-gapped installs) may lack observability; provide offline checklist and fallback manual commands\",\n    \"Tight coupling between generator and agent API could require coordinated versioning\\u2014use clear contract versioning and LTS pins\"\n  ],\n  \"notes\": [\n    \"Design review 2025-02-21: agreed to keep manifest schema minimal and additive; avoid embedding secrets\",\n    \"Security review kickoff 2025-02-28 (pending) - will validate bundle signing and KMS integration for Private\",\n    \"PM feedback (Sofia Martinez) 2025-03-01: require a one-click export to PDF for support runbooks\",\n    \"Dev feedback (R&D): prefer to store generated bundles in a signed S3 location with TTL to support replay\"\n  ],\n  \"comments\": [\n    \"2025-02-13 \\u2014 Aisha Patel: Created ticket and initial draft of manifest schema; linked Confluence design\",\n    \"2025-02-18 \\u2014 Liam Chen: Spike finished for preflight harness; implemented schema validation and a basic preview CLI (branch: feature/runbook-gen)\",\n    \"2025-02-21 \\u2014 Sofia Martinez (PM): Reviewed goals; asked for PDF export and Console preview. Marked as high customer impact for enterprise tenants\",\n    \"2025-02-26 \\u2014 Security (Ravi Desai): Asked for signed bundles and retention policy. Raised requirement to include bundle checksum and KMS-encrypted metadata\",\n    \"2025-03-01 \\u2014 QA (Maya Roberts): Completed test plan for dry-run scenarios. Found a fragile migration-step parser; Liam to address in PR #512\",\n    \"2025-03-04 \\u2014 Liam Chen: Merged CLI preview to internal CI; started wiring telemetry events to upgrade-dashboard. Next: integrate agent contract and run internal canary\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"acceptance_criteria\",\n    \"implementation_notes\",\n    \"rollout_plan\",\n    \"telemetry_signals\",\n    \"migration_strategy\",\n    \"risks\",\n    \"notes\",\n    \"comments\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_8c928a8dd9364b1fad4c2f4753559718\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Private release stager and rollback playbook generator\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-847531-private-release-stager-and-rollback-playbook-generator.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: Private Upgrade Safety\nTeam: engineering\n\n- cli or api can produce a per - version release bundle ( manifest + staged cohorts + runbook ) from a model / operator release tag within < 60s - generated runbook includes step - by - step commands, required approvals, and automatic rollback hooks that can be consumed by the upgrade agent - preflight checks execute against a customer - like sandbox and surface blocking signals ( schema drift, db migration preview failures, node capacity shortfall ) - canary gate can be configured to auto - abort based on telemetry ( p95 latency, error - rate, kv cache miss ), with documented thresholds - rollout metadata exposed in console ( per - cohort progress, blocked step reasons ) and emits standardized telemetry events to the upgrade dashboard - integration tests covering dry",

{
  "key": "ENG-847531",
  "team": "engineering",
  "title": "Private release stager and rollback playbook generator",
  "status": "In Progress",
  "priority": "P0",
  "created_at": "2025-02-12",
  "updated_at": "2025-03-04",
  "creator": "Aisha Patel",
  "assignee": "Liam Chen",
  "project": "Private Upgrade Safety",
  "cycle": "2025-W09",
  "estimate": "8",
  "due_date": "2025-04-01",
  "labels": [
    "private",
    "upgrade",
    "lts",
    "release-engineering",
    "telemetry"
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    "ENG-33188",
    "ENG-47291"
  ],
  "customer_impact": "high",
  "release": "private-upgrade-2025.04",
  "security_review_required": "true",
  "description": "Build an automated release stager and runbook generator for Redwood Private upgrades. The tool will assemble staged cohorts, preflight checks, canary gating rules, and a machine-readable rollback playbook from version metadata and migration manifests. Goal: reduce manual runbook creation, surface safe fallbacks, and enable telemetry-driven automatic abort/rollback triggers for private (VPC/on-prem) upgrade runs.",
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    "CLI or API can produce a per-version release bundle (manifest + staged cohorts + runbook) from a model/operator release tag within < 60s",
    "Generated runbook includes step-by-step commands, required approvals, and automatic rollback hooks that can be consumed by the upgrade agent",
    "Preflight checks execute against a customer-like sandbox and surface blocking signals (schema drift, DB migration preview failures, node capacity shortfall)",
    "Canary gate can be configured to auto-abort based on telemetry (p95 latency, error-rate, KV cache miss), with documented thresholds",
    "Rollout metadata exposed in Console (per-cohort progress, blocked step reasons) and emits standardized telemetry events to the Upgrade dashboard",
    "Integration tests covering dry-run generation, a simulated canary abort, and scripted rollback against the upgrade simulator pass in CI"
  ],
  "implementation_notes": [
    "Design a small declarative manifest format (YAML) that describes: version, LTS channel, cohort definitions, migration SQL artifacts, preflight commands, expected invariants",
    "Generator will incorporate: version compatibility matrix, LTS policies, pinned component versions, and 'rollback recipe' templates",
    "Expose a 'preview' mode that runs all preflight checks without mutating state; capture outputs and synthesize a risk score",
    "Integrate with existing Private upgrade agent via a contract: /v1/upgrades/start endpoint which accepts the generated bundle",
    "Wire telemetry hooks to Console's Upgrade dashboard and to existing tracing (otlp) so gates can evaluate p95, error-rate, and custom migration metrics",
    "Provide a 'manual approval' gate that posts to Slack channel and requires an approver to click a link (SAML/SSO-aware) before continuing",
    "Ship initial generator as 'alpha' CLI + a lightweight web preview; rollout to internal customers first before external tenants"
  ],
  "rollout_plan": [
    "Stage 0 (internal): generate bundles for two non-production clusters and run dry-run preflight (2 weeks)",
    "Stage 1 (canary): run staged release against 3 low-risk customer tenants with manual approval gates and telemetry monitoring (2 weeks)",
    "Stage 2 (gradual): expand cohorts to 20% of private fleet with auto-gating enabled; if any auto-abort occurs, execute rollback playbook (4 weeks)",
    "Stage 3 (ga): enable default runbook generation for all scheduled Private upgrades; include opt-out and custom playbook extensions"
  ],
  "telemetry_signals": [
    "api.request.latency.p95 (global & per-tenant)",
    "api.request.error_rate (5xx/4xx spike by tenant)",
    "gpu.utilization and host.cpu.utilization",
    "kv_cache.hit_rate (drop > 10% signals regression)",
    "db.migration.lag and db.lock-wait-count",
    "upgrade.step.failures (unexpected non-zero exit)",
    "suite.preflight.check_failures and preflight.risk_score"
  ],
  "runbook_links": [
    "https://confluence.redwood.com/display/UPGRADE/Playbook+Generator+Design",
    "https://drive.redwood.com/Shared/PrivateUpgrade/alpha-bundles",
    "https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-upgrades/pull/492",
    "https://grafana.redwood.com/d/upgrade/upgrade-dashboard?orgId=1",
    "https://github.com/redwood-inference/upgrade-agent/issues/118"
  ],
  "migration_strategy": [
    "Prefer online, idempotent migrations where possible. When transactional migrations are required, generate a two-phase: preview->apply pattern",
    "All SQL DDL must be run with compatibility guards and scheduled with low-traffic windows",
    "Keep a 'compat shim' loader for older control-plane agents to accept bundles and gracefully reject incompatible fields",
    "For heavy data transforms, include a migration-progress probe and a 'quiesce' step that drains incoming requests to affected shards"
  ],
  "risks": [
    "Automated playbook might miss tenant-specific customizations; mitigated by an 'extensions' hook and manual review step",
    "Telemetry false positives could trigger unnecessary rollbacks; mitigate with smoothing window and multi-signal confirmation",
    "Edge-case migrations (on-prem air-gapped installs) may lack observability; provide offline checklist and fallback manual commands",
    "Tight coupling between generator and agent API could require coordinated versioning\u2014use clear contract versioning and LTS pins"
  ],
  "notes": [
    "Design review 2025-02-21: agreed to keep manifest schema minimal and additive; avoid embedding secrets",
    "Security review kickoff 2025-02-28 (pending) - will validate bundle signing and KMS integration for Private",
    "PM feedback (Sofia Martinez) 2025-03-01: require a one-click export to PDF for support runbooks",
    "Dev feedback (R&D): prefer to store generated bundles in a signed S3 location with TTL to support replay"
  ],
  "comments": [
    "2025-02-13 \u2014 Aisha Patel: Created ticket and initial draft of manifest schema; linked Confluence design",
    "2025-02-18 \u2014 Liam Chen: Spike finished for preflight harness; implemented schema validation and a basic preview CLI (branch: feature/runbook-gen)",
    "2025-02-21 \u2014 Sofia Martinez (PM): Reviewed goals; asked for PDF export and Console preview. Marked as high customer impact for enterprise tenants",
    "2025-02-26 \u2014 Security (Ravi Desai): Asked for signed bundles and retention policy. Raised requirement to include bundle checksum and KMS-encrypted metadata",
    "2025-03-01 \u2014 QA (Maya Roberts): Completed test plan for dry-run scenarios. Found a fragile migration-step parser; Liam to address in PR #512",
    "2025-03-04 \u2014 Liam Chen: Merged CLI preview to internal CI; started wiring telemetry events to upgrade-dashboard. Next: integrate agent contract and run internal canary"
  ],
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "description",
    "acceptance_criteria",
    "implementation_notes",
    "rollout_plan",
    "telemetry_signals",
    "migration_strategy",
    "risks",
    "notes",
    "comments"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_8c928a8dd9364b1fad4c2f4753559718"
}

{
  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_c99764bff8ee439289cb05f9aab24680",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-42109-vector-score-contract-and-graceful-upgrade-path.json",
    "title": "vector-score-contract-and-graceful-upgrade-path",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/linear",
    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"ENG-42109\",\n  \"team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"title\": \"vector-score-contract-and-graceful-upgrade-path\",\n  \"status\": \"In Progress\",\n  \"priority\": \"P1\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-02-20\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-03-13\",\n  \"creator\": \"Priya Shah\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Marco Li\",\n  \"project\": \"Embeddings & Rerank\",\n  \"cycle\": \"2026-W10\",\n  \"estimate\": \"5\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2026-04-03\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"embeddings\",\n    \"reranker\",\n    \"backcompat\",\n    \"perf\"\n  ],\n  \"dependencies\": [\n    \"ENG-36102\",\n    \"ENG-38214\"\n  ],\n  \"customer_impact\": \"high\",\n  \"release\": \"runtime-1.24\",\n  \"security_review_required\": \"false\",\n  \"description\": \"Problem: We have observed inconsistent reranking scores across clients and SDK versions due to unclear normalization semantics and subtle numerical differences between cosine and raw dot scoring paths. Root causes include (1) mixed assumptions about whether embeddings are pre-normalized, (2) quantized storage (fp16 / int8) losing scale information, (3) zero or near-zero vectors from some models or tokenizers, and (4) divergent client-side post-processing (some SDKs applied L2-normalization, some did not). This leads to user-facing ranking regressions and noisy A/B metrics when switching models or runtimes. Goal: establish a clear, testable server-side score contract, implement a backward-compatible opt-in migration path, and add runtime checks/telemetry to detect regressions early.\",\n  \"acceptance_criteria\": [\n    \"Define and publish canonical scoring contract (cosine vs dot) in docs with exact math and edge-case rules\",\n    \"Server exposes explicit score_mode header and response metadata: X-Embed-Score-Mode / embed_score_mode\",\n    \"Clients can opt into new behavior via header; default remains legacy for 4 weeks while collecting telemetry\",\n    \"End-to-end test suite (unit + integration + property tests) reproduces reference numpy/scipy baselines within 1e-6 for fp32 and documents allowable delta for quantized paths\",\n    \"No customer regressions on NDCG@10 or rerank success rate above defined tolerance during canary rollout\"\n  ],\n  \"proposal_summary\": \"1) Formalize contract: two canonical modes 'cosine' and 'dot_product' with explicit L2-normalization rules (float32 intermediate), handling for zero vectors (return score 0 and flag), and deterministic tie-breaker behavior. 2) Implement server-side normalization for 'cosine' mode and an opt-in request header 'X-Embed-Score-Mode' that clients can set. 3) Add a compatibility warning header when legacy mode is used and an auditing tool to show per-client score deltas. 4) Provide a migration path: opt-in -> staged default flip after telemetry window. 5) Add telemetry, alerts, and gating in Console and runtime to catch regressions.\",\n  \"design_links\": [\n    \"https://confluence.redwood.com/display/ENG/Vector+Score+Contract+Design\",\n    \"https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-vector-score-spec\"\n  ],\n  \"related_prs\": [\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3245\",\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1189\"\n  ],\n  \"rollout_plan\": [\n    \"Stage 0: unit + property tests merged behind feature flag (runtime-1.24)\",\n    \"Stage 1: internal canary (platform team + 2 customers) for 48h with detailed telemetry\",\n    \"Stage 2: 1% hosted traffic for 7 days with continuous NDCG/latency monitoring\",\n    \"Stage 3: 10% traffic if metrics stable, then 50% then full roll\",\n    \"Stage 4: after 4 weeks of stable metrics, change default behavior and send deprecation notices to clients still relying on legacy semantics\"\n  ],\n  \"migration_steps\": [\n    \"Publish SDK update and docs with example header usage and code snippets\",\n    \"Expose per-client 'score-delta' dashboard in Console showing median and P95 deltas vs legacy baseline\",\n    \"Provide one-click toggle in Console for enterprises on Dedicated/Private to pin legacy semantics\",\n    \"Offer a compatibility API parameter 'legacy_embed_semantics=true' for a final 12-week grace period\"\n  ],\n  \"test_matrix\": [\n    \"Unit tests: numerical equivalence to numpy for small batches and quantized representations\",\n    \"Property tests: random vectors, extremes (zero, tiny, huge), deterministic tie-breakers\",\n    \"Integration: end-to-end reranker pipelines (embedding -> store -> rerank) against benchmark queries\",\n    \"Performance: latency p50/p95 impact, CPU/GPU normalization cost, throughput under batching\",\n    \"Compatibility: SDKs (python, js, go) exercising opt-in header and legacy path\"\n  ],\n  \"perf_estimate\": \"Server-side L2 normalization adds ~1.5-3% CPU / token cost in hot paths for typical batch sizes; memory overhead negligible due to streaming normalization. Quantized dot-product paths are unchanged when mode='dot_product'.\",\n  \"monitoring_and_alerts\": [\n    \"New metric: embed_score_mode.delta_median_by_client\",\n    \"Alert: embed_score_regression if NDCG drop > 2% at P95 across top 10 customers during rollout\",\n    \"Dashboards: per-model and per-client histograms of pre/post normalization vector norms\",\n    \"Log flags: emit embed_score_note for any zero-vector encounter with model_id and request_id\"\n  ],\n  \"open_risks_and_tradeoffs\": [\n    \"Performance: normalization increases CPU on runtime nodes \\u2014 mitigated by optional hardware-accelerated kernels and batching tweaks\",\n    \"Backcompat complexity: maintaining two modes increases surface area; mitigate with clear default window and Console toggles\",\n    \"Quantized storage: some customers rely on stored scales; server normalization may obscure intended dot-scale semantics \\u2014 we will document and offer toggles\",\n    \"Edge cases: models that intentionally produce sparse/near-zero vectors must be flagged and handled per-customer\"\n  ],\n  \"qa_notes\": \"Run the full benchmark set (internal 'rerank-blue') at every rollout step. {
  "key": "ENG-42109",
  "team": "engineering",
  "title": "vector-score-contract-and-graceful-upgrade-path",
  "status": "In Progress",
  "priority": "P1",
  "created_at": "2026-02-20",
  "updated_at": "2026-03-13",
  "creator": "Priya Shah",
  "assignee": "Marco Li",
  "project": "Embeddings & Rerank",
  "cycle": "2026-W10",
  "estimate": "5",
  "due_date": "2026-04-03",
  "labels": [
    "embeddings",
    "reranker",
    "backcompat",
    "perf"
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    "ENG-36102",
    "ENG-38214"
  ],
  "customer_impact": "high",
  "release": "runtime-1.24",
  "security_review_required": "false",
  "description": "Problem: We have observed inconsistent reranking scores across clients and SDK versions due to unclear normalization semantics and subtle numerical differences between cosine and raw dot scoring paths. Root causes include (1) mixed assumptions about whether embeddings are pre-normalized, (2) quantized storage (fp16 / int8) losing scale information, (3) zero or near-zero vectors from some models or tokenizers, and (4) divergent client-side post-processing (some SDKs applied L2-normalization, some did not). This leads to user-facing ranking regressions and noisy A/B metrics when switching models or runtimes. Goal: establish a clear, testable server-side score contract, implement a backward-compatible opt-in migration path, and add runtime checks/telemetry to detect regressions early.",
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    "Define and publish canonical scoring contract (cosine vs dot) in docs with exact math and edge-case rules",
    "Server exposes explicit score_mode header and response metadata: X-Embed-Score-Mode / embed_score_mode",
    "Clients can opt into new behavior via header; default remains legacy for 4 weeks while collecting telemetry",
    "End-to-end test suite (unit + integration + property tests) reproduces reference numpy/scipy baselines within 1e-6 for fp32 and documents allowable delta for quantized paths",
    "No customer regressions on NDCG@10 or rerank success rate above defined tolerance during canary rollout"
  ],
  "proposal_summary": "1) Formalize contract: two canonical modes 'cosine' and 'dot_product' with explicit L2-normalization rules (float32 intermediate), handling for zero vectors (return score 0 and flag), and deterministic tie-breaker behavior. 2) Implement server-side normalization for 'cosine' mode and an opt-in request header 'X-Embed-Score-Mode' that clients can set. 3) Add a compatibility warning header when legacy mode is used and an auditing tool to show per-client score deltas. 4) Provide a migration path: opt-in -> staged default flip after telemetry window. 5) Add telemetry, alerts, and gating in Console and runtime to catch regressions.",
  "design_links": [
    "https://confluence.redwood.com/display/ENG/Vector+Score+Contract+Design",
    "https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-vector-score-spec"
  ],
  "related_prs": [
    "https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3245",
    "https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1189"
  ],
  "rollout_plan": [
    "Stage 0: unit + property tests merged behind feature flag (runtime-1.24)",
    "Stage 1: internal canary (platform team + 2 customers) for 48h with detailed telemetry",
    "Stage 2: 1% hosted traffic for 7 days with continuous NDCG/latency monitoring",
    "Stage 3: 10% traffic if metrics stable, then 50% then full roll",
    "Stage 4: after 4 weeks of stable metrics, change default behavior and send deprecation notices to clients still relying on legacy semantics"
  ],
  "migration_steps": [
    "Publish SDK update and docs with example header usage and code snippets",
    "Expose per-client 'score-delta' dashboard in Console showing median and P95 deltas vs legacy baseline",
    "Provide one-click toggle in Console for enterprises on Dedicated/Private to pin legacy semantics",
    "Offer a compatibility API parameter 'legacy_embed_semantics=true' for a final 12-week grace period"
  ],
  "test_matrix": [
    "Unit tests: numerical equivalence to numpy for small batches and quantized representations",
    "Property tests: random vectors, extremes (zero, tiny, huge), deterministic tie-breakers",
    "Integration: end-to-end reranker pipelines (embedding -> store -> rerank) against benchmark queries",
    "Performance: latency p50/p95 impact, CPU/GPU normalization cost, throughput under batching",
    "Compatibility: SDKs (python, js, go) exercising opt-in header and legacy path"
  ],
  "perf_estimate": "Server-side L2 normalization adds ~1.5-3% CPU / token cost in hot paths for typical batch sizes; memory overhead negligible due to streaming normalization. Quantized dot-product paths are unchanged when mode='dot_product'.",
  "monitoring_and_alerts": [
    "New metric: embed_score_mode.delta_median_by_client",
    "Alert: embed_score_regression if NDCG drop > 2% at P95 across top 10 customers during rollout",
    "Dashboards: per-model and per-client histograms of pre/post normalization vector norms",
    "Log flags: emit embed_score_note for any zero-vector encounter with model_id and request_id"
  ],
  "open_risks_and_tradeoffs": [
    "Performance: normalization increases CPU on runtime nodes \u2014 mitigated by optional hardware-accelerated kernels and batching tweaks",
    "Backcompat complexity: maintaining two modes increases surface area; mitigate with clear default window and Console toggles",
    "Quantized storage: some customers rely on stored scales; server normalization may obscure intended dot-scale semantics \u2014 we will document and offer toggles",
    "Edge cases: models that intentionally produce sparse/near-zero vectors must be flagged and handled per-customer"
  ],
  "qa_notes": "Run the full benchmark set (internal 'rerank-blue') at every rollout step. Capture NDCG, MRR, and top-1 stability. Have a rollback playbook ready to pin legacy semantics by customer. Coordinate with Solutions Engineering for any high-risk customers.",
  "stakeholders": [
    "Priya Shah (owner)",
    "Marco Li (engineer)",
    "Riley Gomez (PM)",
    "Anya Voronov (ML Research)",
    "SRE oncall"
  ],
  "notifications": "Announcement draft in #embeddings and #platform-release channels; targeted emails to Dedicated/Private customers one week before default change; release notes entry in 1.24",
  "implementation_notes": "Implementation will add a lightweight normalization kernel in the runtime hot path and a request header parser. We will reuse existing batching pipeline; normalization will be applied while building the key-value cache to avoid extra memory passes. Add a small 'compat' shim to the embeddings API layer that records deltas but forwards to legacy scoring when requested.",
  "post_deploy_checks": [
    "Verify sample of 10k requests show expected embed_score_mode header in responses",
    "Compare stored embedding norms distribution vs pre-change baseline",
    "Check no regression in throughput greater than 5% on dedicated pools"
  ],
  "follow_up_tasks": [
    "Create migration playbook for account managers",
    "Add sample notebooks showing how to reproduce score-mode locally",
    "Schedule customer office hours during migration window"
  ],
  "notes": [
    "Feedback from Design review: call out UX for toggles in Console; make the score mode prominent in API docs",
    "Eng review comment: prefer float32 intermediate for normalization to avoid fp16 drift (accepted)",
    "SRE: ensure metric tag cardinality limited by sampling (will sample 0.5% of requests for delta metric)"
  ],
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "description",

    "post_deploy_checks",
    "follow_up_tasks",
    "notes"
  ],

{
  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_b4bd83b46612452e858bc02b380082e2",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/probe-heatmap-rollout-decision-protocol-2024.json",
    "title": "Probe heatmap -> rollout decision protocol",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Probe heatmap -> rollout decision protocol\",\n  \"space\": \"applied-ml-and-evals\",\n  \"author\": \"Anjali Mehta\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2024-11-12\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2025-01-08\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Evan Park\",\n    \"Luis Ortega\",\n    \"Marina Cole\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"regression-triage\",\n    \"telemetry\",\n    \"rollout-policy\",\n    \"probe-heatmap\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"internal\",\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/eval-mesh-and-workload-fingerprinting-2026\",\n    \"/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/regression-impact-index-and-prioritization-framework-2024\"\n  ],\n  \"content\": \"Summary\\n-------\\nThis document defines a reproducible protocol to convert probe heatmaps (telemetry-driven failure density views) into rollout decisions for model promotions, quantization migrations, and configuration changes. The goal is to make decisions auditable, time-bounded, and aligned with SLOs so product and ops can act consistently across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.\\n\\nScope\\n-----\\n- Applies to any promotion or rollout that is gated by probe-driven quality signals: model promotions, quantized rollouts, prompt rewrites, and routing policy changes.\\n- Focuses on probe heatmaps produced by the eval harness and live shadow probes (not human labelling pipelines).\\n- Excludes legislated/regulatory decisions (finance/compliance) - see separate compliance approval flow.\\n\\nKey definitions\\n---------------\\n- Probe heatmap: a time-windowed 2D histogram where rows are probes (slice identifiers) and columns are failure modes (fidelity, hallucination, latency, embeddings drift). Each cell contains count and a severity score.\\n- Decision score (DS): a normalized scalar computed from heatmap aggregates that maps to GO / CAUTION / HOLD / ROLLBACK actions.\\n- Tiered slice: pre-defined group of probes that share an SLO (e.g., CriticalTenantFlows, BillingIntents, LowRiskExplorations).\\n\\nInputs required\\n---------------\\n1) Heatmap snapshot covering the last N hours (default N=24) with per-probe metrics: total_calls, failure_count, avg_severity, median_latency_ms, embedding_drift_score.\\n2) Active rollout plan metadata: target model id, variant (quantized/float16), percent_traffic, scheduled_start.\\n3) Baseline reference heatmap from the control population (previous model or canary).\\n4) SLO manifest for target slices (SLO window, allowed error budget, latency SLO).\\n5) Operational constraints: maintenance windows, capacity headroom, and dependency map.\\n\\nDecision scoring algorithm (summary)\\n----------------------------------\\nWe compute three sub-scores and aggregate them into DS (range 0..100):\\n\\n- StabilityScore (SS): weighted failure density normalized by probe priority. Formula: SS = 100 * sum_p (w_p * (failure_count_p / max(1,total_calls_p))) / sum_p(w_p)\\n- LatencyPenalty (LP): 10 * max(0, (median_latency_ms - latency_slo_ms) / latency_slo_ms) clipped at 30\\n- DriftFactor (DF): 50 * embedding_drift_score_95pct_quantile normalized against baseline drift\\n\\nFinal Decision Score: DS = clamp(SS + LP + DF, 0, 100)\\n\\nAction mapping (recommended)\\n---------------------------\\n- DS <= 15: GO (promote / continue rollout)\\n- 15 < DS <= 35: CAUTION (slow rollout to 10% and schedule targeted human review within 4 hours)\\n- 35 < DS <= 60: HOLD (pause rollout; trigger automated bisect & focused probes)\\n- DS > 60: ROLLBACK (automatically revert to baseline variant and open incident ticket)\\n\\nConfiguration table (defaults)\\n-----------------------------\\n- heatmap_window_hours: 24 -- Time window to compute the snapshot\\n- probe_priority_weights: CriticalTenantFlows:10, BillingIntents:8, UXTextGen:3 -- Priority map used in SS\\n- latency_slo_ms: 250 -- latency SLO used for LP calculation\\n- drift_baseline_window_days: 7 -- Days used to compute baseline drift\\n- slow_roll_threshold: 35 -- DS threshold to switch to slow rollout\\n- human_review_timeout_hours: 4 -- Max time to complete targeted review\\n\\nOwnership and roles\\n-------------------\\n- Eval Oncall (primary): validates heatmap integrity, runs automated bisect and approves/requests human review.\\n- Model Owner (secondary): responsible for quick triage of failing slices and submitting patch/rollforward.\\n- Release Engineer: executes percent traffic adjustments and rollbacks in the serving control plane.\\n- Oncall Platform SRE: monitors capacity/latency regressions and authorizes emergency rollbacks for tail latency incidents.\\n\\nProcedure: from snapshot to decision (operational runbook)\\n------------------------------------------------------\\n1. Fetch heatmap snapshot and baseline. Verify telemetry completeness (missing probes < 5% of expected).\\n2. Run validation script to confirm probe schema and timestamps: 'python tools/heatmap_validate.py --snapshot /tmp/heatmap.json'\\n3. Compute DS using the scoring algorithm and emit a decision document to /incidents/probe-decisions/YYYYMMDD-HHMM.json. Example: curl -X POST 'https://ops-api.internal/decisions' -d '{'ds': 27, 'action': 'CAUTION', 'top_slices': ['BillingIntents:charge-failure'] }'\\n4. If action == GO: continue rollout. Log event and schedule a 24h follow-up check.\\n5. If action == CAUTION: cap rollout at 10% for 6 hours, assign Model Owner and Eval Oncall for targeted human validation, and run automated bisect on top 5 degrading slices.\\n6. If action == HOLD: pause rollout, mark the release as blocked in release tracker, and create a regression investigation ticket with pre-populated triage fields.\\n7. If action == ROLLBACK: trigger automated rollback playbook and notify the incident channel #regression-ops with summary and rollback links.\\n\\nAutomated bisect integration\\n---------------------------\\n- The decision pipeline calls the bisect service with the top N probes by (failure_count * avg_severity). The bisect run ID is included in the decision document.\\n- If bisect identifies a single suspect change (probability > 0.7) the Model Owner must decide to either patch or rollback within human_review_timeout_hours.\\n\\nTelemetry contract (minimal required fields)\\n-----------------------------------------\\nEmitters must provide a compact heatmap JSON with the following fields (example snippet):\\n\\n'{'\\n  'snapshot_ts': '2025-01-08T08:00:00Z',\\n  'window_hours': 24,\\n  'slices': [\\n    {\\n      'slice_id': 'BillingIntents:charge-failure',\\n      'total_calls': 12450,\\n      'failure_count': 312,\\n      'avg_severity': 2.8,\\n      'median_latency_ms': 430,\\n      'embedding_drift_score': 0.34\\n    }\\n  ]\\n}'\\n\\nRequired export fields (flat): snapshot_ts, window_hours, slices[].slice_id, slices[].total_calls, slices[].failure_count, slices[].avg_severity, slices[].median_latency_ms, slices[].embedding_drift_score. Optional: host_cluster, model_variant, tenant_id.\\n\\nSafety checks and hard gates\\n---------------------------\\n- If any CriticalTenantFlows slice has failure_rate > 0.5% AND avg_severity >= 3.0 the system must ROLLBACK regardless of DS.\\n- If more than 10% of probes lack current telemetry, mark decision state as INCONCLUSIVE and require human approval.\\n- For private/on-prem customers with per-customer SLO overrides, consult the customer SLO manifest before automatic rollback - use the per-customer override endpoint.\\n\\nRollback criteria and runbook steps\\n----------------------------------\\n1. Lock the rollout in the control plane: 'redwoodctl rollout lock --id <rollout-id>'\\n2. Execute the variant revert: 'redwoodctl rollout revert --id <rollout-id> --target <baseline-model>'\\n3. Post-rollback verification: run a 2-hour fast-probe sweep across top 20 slices and confirm DS falls below 20.\\n4. Create incident with severity mapping: DS>80 -> Sev2, DS 60-80 -> Sev3.\\n\\nExample: case study (short)\\n-------------------------\\n- Scenario: Quantized v1.2 was promoted to 20% across US-hosted tenants. After 12 hours heatmap snapshot showed elevated embedding_drift_score in 3 billing-related slices. Computed DS = 42 -> HOLD. Automated bisect pointed to a tokenizer change in the preprocessor. Model Owner rolled back quant patch and re-run priming probes; DS dropped to 12 within 3 hours and rollout resumed at a slow cadence.\\n\\nAppendix A: configuration YAML sample\\n------------------------------------\\n'heatmap_window_hours: 24\\nprobe_priority_weights:\\n  CriticalTenantFlows: 10\\n  BillingIntents: 8\\n  UXTextGen: 3\\nlatency_slo_ms: 250\\ndrift_baseline_window_days: 7\\nslow_roll_threshold: 35\\nhuman_review_timeout_hours: 4'\\n\\nAppendix B: links and references\\n--------------------------------\\n- Eval mesh and workload fingerprinting: /applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/eval-mesh-and-workload-fingerprinting-2026\\n- Regression prioritization index: /applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/regression-impact-index-and-prioritization-framework-2024\\n\\nAppendix C: change history\\n--------------------------\\n- 2024-11-12 (Anjali Mehta): First draft and internal review.\\n- 2024-12-02 (Evan Park): Added bisect integration details and telemetry contract.\\n- 2025-01-08 (Marina Cole): Clarified safety gates for private deployments and updated example.\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"content\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_b4bd83b46612452e858bc02b380082e2\"\n}",

document.content:
{
  "title": "Probe heatmap -> rollout decision protocol",
  "space": "applied-ml-and-evals",
  "author": "Anjali Mehta",
  "owner_team": "engineering",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2024-11-12",
  "last_updated": "2025-01-08",
  "reviewers": [
    "Evan Park",
    "Luis Ortega",
    "Marina Cole"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "regression-triage",
    "telemetry",
    "rollout-policy",
    "probe-heatmap"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "related_pages": [
    "/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/eval-mesh-and-workload-fingerprinting-2026",
    "/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/regression-impact-index-and-prioritization-framework-2024"
  ],
  "content": "Summary
-------
This document defines a reproducible protocol to convert probe heatmaps (telemetry-driven failure density views) into rollout decisions for model promotions, quantization migrations, and configuration changes. The goal is to make decisions auditable, time-bounded, and aligned with SLOs so product and ops can act consistently across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Scope
-----
- Applies to any promotion or rollout that is gated by probe-driven quality signals: model promotions, quantized rollouts, prompt rewrites, and routing policy changes.
- Focuses on probe heatmaps produced by the eval harness and live shadow probes (not human labelling pipelines).
- Excludes legislated/regulatory decisions (finance/compliance) - see separate compliance approval flow.

Key definitions
---------------
- Probe heatmap: a time-windowed 2D histogram where rows are probes (slice identifiers) and columns are failure modes (fidelity, hallucination, latency, embeddings drift). Each cell contains count and a severity score.
- Decision score (DS): a normalized scalar computed from heatmap aggregates that maps to GO / CAUTION / HOLD / ROLLBACK actions.
- Tiered slice: pre-defined group of probes that share an SLO (e.g., CriticalTenantFlows, BillingIntents, LowRiskExplorations).

Inputs required
---------------
1) Heatmap snapshot covering the last N hours (default N=24) with per-probe metrics: total_calls, failure_count, avg_severity, median_latency_ms, embedding_drift_score.
2) Active rollout plan metadata: target model id, variant (quantized/float16), percent_traffic, scheduled_start.
3) Baseline reference heatmap from the control population (previous model or canary).
4) SLO manifest for target slices (SLO window, allowed error budget, latency SLO).
5) Operational constraints: maintenance windows, capacity headroom, and dependency map.

Decision scoring algorithm (summary)
----------------------------------
We compute three sub-scores and aggregate them into DS (range 0..100):

- StabilityScore (SS): weighted failure density normalized by probe priority. Formula: SS = 100 * sum_p (w_p * (failure_count_p / max(1,total_calls_p))) / sum_p(w_p)
- LatencyPenalty (LP): 10 * max(0, (median_latency_ms - latency_slo_ms) / latency_slo_ms) clipped at 30
- DriftFactor (DF): 50 * embedding_drift_score_95pct_quantile normalized against baseline drift

Final Decision Score: DS = clamp(SS + LP + DF, 0, 100)

Action mapping (recommended)
---------------------------
- DS <= 15: GO (promote / continue rollout)
- 15 < DS <= 35: CAUTION (slow rollout to 10% and schedule targeted human review within 4 hours)
- 35 < DS <= 60: HOLD (pause rollout; trigger automated bisect & focused probes)
- DS > 60: ROLLBACK (automatically revert to baseline variant and open incident ticket)

Configuration table (defaults)
-----------------------------
- heatmap_window_hours: 24 -- Time window to compute the snapshot
- probe_priority_weights: CriticalTenantFlows:10, BillingIntents:8, UXTextGen:3 -- Priority map used in SS
- latency_slo_ms: 250 -- latency SLO used for LP calculation
- drift_baseline_window_days: 7 -- Days used to compute baseline drift
- slow_roll_threshold: 35 -- DS threshold to switch to slow rollout
- human_review_timeout_hours: 4 -- Max time to complete targeted review

Ownership and roles
-------------------
- Eval Oncall (primary): validates heatmap integrity, runs automated bisect and approves/requests human review.
- Model Owner (secondary): responsible for quick triage of failing slices and submitting patch/rollforward.
- Release Engineer: executes percent traffic adjustments and rollbacks in the serving control plane.
- Oncall Platform SRE: monitors capacity/latency regressions and authorizes emergency rollbacks for tail latency incidents.

Procedure: from snapshot to decision (operational runbook)
------------------------------------------------------
1. Fetch heatmap snapshot and baseline. Verify telemetry completeness (missing probes < 5% of expected).
2. Run validation script to confirm probe schema and timestamps: 'python tools/heatmap_validate.py --snapshot /tmp/heatmap.json'
3. Compute DS using the scoring algorithm and emit a decision document to /incidents/probe-decisions/YYYYMMDD-HHMM.json. Example: curl -X POST 'https://ops-api.internal/decisions' -d '{'ds': 27, 'action': 'CAUTION', 'top_slices': ['BillingIntents:charge-failure'] }'
4. If action == GO: continue rollout. Log event and schedule a 24h follow-up check.
5. If action == CAUTION: cap rollout at 10% for 6 hours, assign Model Owner and Eval Oncall for targeted human validation, and run automated bisect on top 5 degrading slices.
6. If action == HOLD: pause rollout, mark the release as blocked in release tracker, and create a regression investigation ticket with pre-populated triage fields.
7. If action == ROLLBACK: trigger automated rollback playbook and notify the incident channel #regression-ops with summary and rollback links.

Automated bisect integration
---------------------------
- The decision pipeline calls the bisect service with the top N probes by (failure_count * avg_severity). The bisect run ID is included in the decision document.
- If bisect identifies a single suspect change (probability > 0.7) the Model Owner must decide to either patch or rollback within human_review_timeout_hours.

Telemetry contract (minimal required fields)
-----------------------------------------
Emitters must provide a compact heatmap JSON with the following fields (example snippet):

'{'
  'snapshot_ts': '2025-01-08T08:00:00Z',
  'window_hours': 24,
  'slices': [
    {
      'slice_id': 'BillingIntents:charge-failure',
      'total_calls': 12450,
      'failure_count': 312,
      'avg_severity': 2.8,
      'median_latency_ms': 430,
      'embedding_drift_score': 0.34
    }
  ]
}'

Required export fields (flat): snapshot_ts, window_hours, slices[].slice_id, slices[].total_calls, slices[].failure_count, slices[].avg_severity, slices[].median_latency_ms, slices[].embedding_drift_score. Optional: host_cluster, model_variant, tenant_id.

Safety checks and hard gates
---------------------------
- If any CriticalTenantFlows slice has failure_rate > 0.5% AND avg_severity >= 3.0 the system must ROLLBACK regardless of DS.
- If more than 10% of probes lack current telemetry, mark decision state as INCONCLUSIVE and require human approval.
- For private/on-prem customers with per-customer SLO overrides, consult the customer SLO manifest before automatic rollback - use the per-customer override endpoint.

Rollback criteria and runbook steps
----------------------------------
1. Lock the rollout in the control plane: 'redwoodctl rollout lock --id <rollout-id>'
2. Execute the variant revert: 'redwoodctl rollout revert --id <rollout-id> --target <baseline-model>'
3. Post-rollback verification: run a 2-hour fast-probe sweep across top 20 slices and confirm DS falls below 20.
4. Create incident with severity mapping: DS>80 -> Sev2, DS 60-80 -> Sev3.

Example: case study (short)
-------------------------
- Scenario: Quantized v1.2 was promoted to 20% across US-hosted tenants. After 12 hours heatmap snapshot showed elevated embedding_drift_score in 3 billing-related slices. Computed DS = 42 -> HOLD. Automated bisect pointed to a tokenizer change in the preprocessor. Model Owner rolled back quant patch and re-run priming probes; DS dropped to 12 within 3 hours and rollout resumed at a slow cadence.

Appendix A: configuration YAML sample
------------------------------------
'heatmap_window_hours: 24
probe_priority_weights:
  CriticalTenantFlows: 10
  BillingIntents: 8
  UXTextGen: 3
latency_slo_ms: 250
drift_baseline_window_days: 7
slow_roll_threshold: 35
human_review_timeout_hours: 4'

Appendix B: links and references
--------------------------------
- Eval mesh and workload fingerprinting: /applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/eval-mesh-and-workload-fingerprinting-2026
- Regression prioritization index: /applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/regression-impact-index-and-prioritization-framework-2024

Appendix C: change history
--------------------------
- 2024-11-12 (Anjali Mehta): First draft and internal review.
- 2024-12-02 (Evan Park): Added bisect integration details and telemetry contract.
- 2025-01-08 (Marina Cole): Clarified safety gates for private deployments and updated example.",
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "content"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_b4bd83b46612452e858bc02b380082e2"
}
